## 🛑 The last step of applying a migration is editing THIS file

Applying a migration is not finished when the catalog says the objects are there. It is finished when this index says so too.

- [ ] **Applied a migration by hand? Change its entry below in the SAME session** — from `FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED` to `✅ APPLIED to production <date>`, with the date and the catalog evidence you actually read.
- [ ] **Cite the CATALOG, never the ledger.** Hand-applied SQL writes no row to `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`, so a ledger MISS proves nothing here; only `pg_proc` / `pg_class` / `information_schema` do. A ledger HIT is still definitive.
- [ ] **Correcting a stale entry? Say that it was stale**, so the next reader can tell a correction from a fresh apply.

An applied migration whose entry still reads FILE ONLY will be re-applied or re-written by the next session — which rolls every `DROP` + `CREATE` inside it back to whatever the file said the day it was written. That has already happened here. Full procedure: `supabase/MODULE_DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md`.

- **2026-08-15** — **The health check that always said "zero" now tells the truth** (`20260815011500_auth_profile_link_health.sql`; **NOT APPLIED — FILE ONLY**). `public.check_orphaned_auth_users()` is the platform's own detector for "this person can sign in but has no profile". Its entire body was `SELECT p.id, p.email, p.created_at FROM profiles p WHERE 1 = 0` under the comment *"Since we can't access auth.users table, return empty result set"* — so **every consistency check ever run reported a clean system**, and the people it existed to find were never found. Its two siblings `check_orphaned_profiles()` and `create_missing_profiles()` are stubs of the same vintage and are **deliberately left alone here** — the second one WRITES profiles, and repairing a broken identity link is a decision about a real person's account, not a migration. Detection first. **Measured on production 2026-08-15:** 992 `auth.users` rows have no `profiles` row, but **978 of those have never signed in** — pre-created shells that have not hit anything. **14 have signed in and are therefore actually being turned away**, 6 of them within 30 days, the most recent that same day. Of the 14, **8 DO have a profile under a DIFFERENT id** (matched by email) — a broken identity link against the documented invariant `auth.users.id == profiles.id`, and recoverable by relinking; the other 6 have no profile under any id. `DROP` + `CREATE` (not `CREATE OR REPLACE`) because the return type widens from 3 columns to 6: `has_signed_in` is the load-bearing one, separating the 14 from the 978, and `profile_exists_by_email` separates recoverable link breaks from the genuinely profile-less. **SECURITY:** reading `auth.users` forces `SECURITY DEFINER`, so the function gates itself on `is_super_admin() OR is_admin()` rather than trusting the caller, plus the mandatory explicit `REVOKE EXECUTE FROM anon, PUBLIC` + `GRANT TO authenticated` — the stub it replaces **was callable by `anon`**, harmless only because it returned nothing. The one existing caller, `app/api/users/check-consistency/route.ts`, reads the result as an opaque array and is unaffected by the extra columns; that route has no UI, which is why the count is surfaced on the Permissions Audit → System Health tab instead (plain view is the default, so the card lands there). **Rehearsed on production inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`:** `prosecdef` true, `anon` executable **false**, `authenticated` executable true, inner counts 992/14/8 — then a **separate** post-rollback query confirmed production unchanged (the stub is back, `prosecdef` false). Shipped alongside the `/auth/login` wording fix for `profile_load_failed`, which previously told these 14 people the failure was *"a temporary issue — please sign in again"*; it never clears for them, and that wording is why not one of them ever filed a fault.
- **2026-08-05** — **Session feedback: a team-taught session no longer loses the Senior Learner's name at write time** (`20260812010000_scf_submit_feedback_team_taught_faculty.sql`; **NOT APPLIED — FILE ONLY.** Merging does not apply it; a human applies it via the Management API. There is no code half — the change is entirely in-database, so deploy order does not matter.) **TIER-1 ADDITIVE — one NEW `IMMUTABLE` helper plus one `CREATE OR REPLACE` of an existing function; creates no table, alters no column, drops nothing, and backfills nothing.** This is the upstream defect named but deliberately not fixed by `20260810160000` (PR #2850). `fn_scf_submit_feedback` resolved the Senior Learner with `v_period -> 'assigned_faculty' ->> 'faculty_email'`, but `attendance/mark` writes `assigned_faculty` in **two shapes** — an **object** when exactly one team member is assigned, an **array** when more than one (`app/(routes)/academic/attendance/mark/page.tsx` ~line 1357). `->>` with a text key on a JSON **array** returns NULL **silently**, so every team-taught session wrote `faculty_id = NULL, faculty_email = NULL` while the Senior Learner sat in the JSON unread. **Measured live 2026-08-05 over the whole table, not a sample:** `session_feedback` 135,861 rows, **19,804 (14.58%)** with `faculty_email IS NULL`, and `faculty_id` NULL on **100%** of those. Re-resolving all 19,804 against the attendance blob splits them **three** ways, not two: **9,996 array-shape** (this defect), **8,080 with no `assigned_faculty` key at all**, and **1,728 object-shape** — the last of which `->>` handles fine, so they are a *different* defect: **1,728 of 1,728 (100%)** sit on a blob whose `updated_at` is LATER than the feedback row's `created_at`, i.e. the Senior Learner was assigned *after* the learner submitted. **The shape decision is taken from the data, not from convenience:** every one of the 9,996 arrays has length > 1 (genuinely team-taught), carries at least one usable email, and contains **exactly one** element flagged `is_primary: true` — 9,996 of 9,996, with **zero** arrays carrying two primaries and **zero** carrying none. So the row records the **primary** Senior Learner, with documented fallbacks (first element with an email, then first element) that never fire on today's data and exist only so a future flagless array names *somebody* rather than silently naming nobody. This is strictly better than the existing TypeScript precedent at `attendance-report-service.ts:1004`, which takes `assigned_faculty[0]`. The second Senior Learner on a team-taught session is therefore not named on the row — deliberate and reversible: `session_feedback` holds one identity pair per row, the escalation path needs one addressee, and the full roster stays in the attendance blob. **The failure is now LOUD:** when neither an email nor a valid id resolves, the function `RAISE WARNING`s with the timetable, date, period and the **shape** (`array` / `object` / `key_absent`), so a reader can tell "the Senior Learner was there and we failed to read it" from "there was nothing to read". The submit still succeeds — a learner's answer is never discarded for an administrative gap. The new helper `fn_attendance_slot_faculty(jsonb)` deliberately mirrors the existing `fn_attendance_slot_students(jsonb)`, which already exists for exactly this both-shapes reason on the roster side of the same blob (PR #1865) — the Senior-Learner twin of a house pattern, not a new mechanism; `is_primary` is compared as **text** (`lower(e ->> 'is_primary') = 'true'`) rather than cast to boolean so a malformed flag degrades instead of raising 22P02 and aborting the submit for every learner in the class. The `faculty_id` cast gains the same regex-`CASE` guard the roster cast already carries, because reading the array shape **widens what that cast sees** — a malformed id inside a team-taught array never reached it before and does now. `fn_scf_submit_feedback` was rebuilt from its **LIVE `pg_get_functiondef`** (read 2026-08-05), never re-authored from the repo file, which has silently reverted live logic here before; `diff` against live shows only the identity resolution, the warning and the three new `DECLARE`s. **Privileges:** live ACL for `fn_scf_submit_feedback` is exactly `{postgres, authenticated, service_role}` (anon false) and is restored verbatim; the new helper gets `REVOKE … FROM anon, PUBLIC` + `GRANT … TO authenticated, service_role`, with an in-file `DO` block asserting anon can execute neither. **Version chosen against the LEDGER, not just the repo:** `20260812010000` is free in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` (max = `20260812000000`) *and* among repo files. **Rehearsed on prod inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`** with the file's own `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;` stripped first (an inner `COMMIT` would make the rollback a no-op): applied clean, all four in-file assertions passed, and a **separate** post-rollback query confirmed production unchanged — the helper does not exist and `fn_scf_submit_feedback` does not reference it. **Both assertions proven non-vacuous by negative control:** removing the array branch entirely (the original defect) and ignoring `is_primary` (taking first-with-email) each made the guard fail with `guard: array shape did not resolve to the is_primary faculty`. **NO BACKFILL — write path only.** Of the 19,804 existing rows, **11,725 are recoverable** from the blob today (9,997 array-shape → 100% would resolve both a valid email and a valid UUID, across 67 distinct Senior Learners; 1,728 object-shape → 100%, 17 Senior Learners) and **8,080 are not** (no `assigned_faculty` key, nothing to read). - **2026-08-05** (revised 2026-08-06) — **Foundation item bank: the JABT two-label pair — `fp_items.bloom_level` (K1–K6) + `fp_items.advanced_dimension` (A1–A5), columns only, no values** (`20260908010000_fp_items_bloom_level.sql`; **NOT APPLIED — FILE ONLY.** Merging does not apply it; a human applies it via the Management API. There is no code half — no route, service or component reads or writes the column yet, so deploy order does not matter.) **TIER-1 ADDITIVE — two nullable columns, two CHECKs, one partial index on a 125-row table. Alters no existing column, drops nothing, backfills nothing, touches no policy, function or grant.** `fp_items` carried exactly one signal about a question's demand — `difficulty smallint 1..5`, an author's feeling — and nothing saying what the question *asks for*. **Convention deliberately borrowed, not invented:** `text` holding `'K1'`..`'K6'`, matching `curriculum_lesson.primary_bloom_level` (19,424 rows tagged live) and `obe_regulation_config.blooms_active_levels`, and named as `bos_taxonomy_levels` names them. **Not** the `bloom_taxonomy_level` ENUM (`remember`/`understand`/…), whose only column in the database is `competency_catalog.bloom_taxonomy_level_deprecated` — deprecated in its own name. Unlike `curriculum_lesson.primary_bloom_level`, which is left unconstrained on purpose because a model writes it during spine generation, this column is written by a human reviewer accepting a proposal, so a tight CHECK is correct: a typo must fail loudly rather than become a seventh level. **TWO columns, because `jkkn_advanced` has two halves.** The spec is explicit that every task carries two labels: the K says how hard the thinking is, and the A says what else the task builds in the learner. Rule 1 gives every task exactly one K; Rule 2 allows at most one A (hence a scalar, not an array); Rule 3 says a task with no A is fine (hence nullable). Ten elements as of the **2026-08-06 rulings of record**: K1–K6 unchanged, A1 Human Dimension, A2 Caring, A3 Learning How to Learn, **A4 Performed Skill** (Bloom's psychomotor in three bands) and **A5 Accountable AI Use** — A5 now *active, used sparingly, a Board of Studies opts a course in*, no longer reserved. **A-codes are excluded by POLICY, not by CHECK.** All 125 rows are `q_type='mcq_single'` — auto-scored, four options — and the reachability matrix marks A1/A2/A4/A5 unreachable in a written format with A3 only *partly* reachable (its worked example, "state precisely what you would need to look up", is a written question but not an auto-scorable one). So a reviewer leaves `advanced_dimension` NULL on every MCQ row. The constraint still admits A1–A5 deliberately: forbidding them in the schema would foreclose the added half of the framework, which is exactly the pre-JABT single-taxonomy shape `obe_course_outcomes.taxonomy_level` is already stuck in (4,360 K-codes and 690 Fink codes crammed into one column, `taxonomy_dimension` NULL on all 6,381 rows, coverage rule unmeasurable). A4's bands (a/b/c) are **not** in this vocabulary — a band records how a performed act went, so it belongs on the artifact recording the act. **Scope caveat:** the 2026-08-06 rollout ruling makes `jkkn_advanced` the default *"for R-2026 regulations; existing regulations unchanged unless their board opts in"*, and the Foundation Programme is a Class 6–8 school programme, not a UG regulation — so it is not yet settled that JABT governs this bank. This migration adds vocabulary and writes no values, so it is correct either way; the coverage rule (Rule 4) is deliberately NOT implemented here pending that ruling. **Version RENUMBERED 2026-08-15 to `20260908010000`.** The original `20260812100000` was chosen on 2026-08-06 against both the repo files and the ledger and was genuinely free in both at that moment — but `jicate/main` has since merged `20260812100000_seed_hr_onboarding_checklists_all_orgs.sql`, so the two files collided the instant main was merged into this branch, and the `No new duplicate migration versions` gate (which had been *cancelled* — not passed — on every run since) would have failed. Renumbering is safe here because this migration is **unapplied**: re-verified live 2026-08-15, `fp_items.advanced_dimension` is absent from `information_schema.columns`, so no already-applied version is being renamed. Re-checked 2026-08-15: highest repo file is now `20260907010000`, and `20260908010000` is absent from the repo files and from `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` alike. Re-rehearsed on production 2026-08-06 after the two-column revision, inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`: `k_col 1, a_col 1, k_check 1, a_check 1, values_written 0, rows_total 125`. **Both CHECKs proven non-vacuous by negative control in the same rehearsal:** `advanced_dimension='A4'` is ACCEPTED (1 row — the point of the revision), while `'A6'` and `bloom_level='K7'` are each rejected with `23514`. A **separate** post-rollback call confirmed production unchanged — `cols_live 0, checks_live 0, fp_items 125 rows`. **Companion, and the actual point:** `scripts/propose-fp-item-bloom-levels.ts` reads the bank and *proposes* a level per item into `docs/modules/foundation/2026-08-05-MODULE-foundation-item-bloom-proposals.generated.{md,csv}` for academic review. It has no UPDATE, no INSERT and no RPC call. Proposed distribution over the 116 real questions (9 are `[PILOT]` placeholder rows with literal `opt A`–`opt D` options and are untaggable): **K1 69 · K2 38 · K3 3 · K4 5 · K5 1 · K6 0** — 92.2% never past Understanding. **Treat that headline as directional, not quotable:** the `recall` rule is an unconditional catch-all (`test: () => true`) stamped `confidence: 'medium'`, so the K1 69 is what remains when no rule matched rather than a positive classification, and completion-style stems that do not end in `?` fall through to it regardless of demand. Every value is a proposal awaiting academic review. Difficulty tracks it only weakly (Pearson r = 0.320, Spearman ρ = 0.319, r² = 0.10), so `difficulty` was never a proxy for cognitive demand.

- **2026-08-10** — **JKKN permanent ID — the machinery, shipped switched off** (`20260817040000_jkkn_permanent_identity_schema.sql` + `20260817050000_jkkn_identity_rpcs.sql`; **NOT APPLIED — FILE ONLY**). Two tables: `jkkn_identities` (one permanent number per person for life — six digits + a Damm check digit, stored with the dash as `348295-7`) and `jkkn_identity_aliases` (roll number, Team Code, university register number, application number, NEET roll, ABC ID, legacy — rows are CLOSED, never deleted, so a 2026 roll number still resolves in 2040). Learners and team members draw from ONE pool, so a learner who returns as a Senior Learner keeps the same number; nothing that can change is encoded in it. Five functions: `fn_jkkn_id_check_digit` and `fn_jkkn_id_validate` (IMMUTABLE, Damm — **not Luhn**, which misses the 09↔90 swap; verified exhaustively over all 900,000 six-digit values with zero undetected single-digit errors and zero undetected adjacent transpositions), plus SECDEF `fn_issue_jkkn_id` (random allocation over 100000–999999 so an ID card never reveals intake volume or joining order; refuses a second number for a person who already holds one), `fn_check_duplicate_person` (**never auto-merges** — twins share a name and a birth date; reports Aadhaar as *unchecked* because MyJKKN stores none) and `fn_resolve_person` (universal lookup, check-digit-validates a JKKN ID before searching, re-imposes the caller's institution scope because it is SECDEF). Both tables: RLS on, `REVOKE ALL FROM anon, **authenticated**, PUBLIC` then an explicit grant — revoking anon alone leaves the Supabase default DELETE grant on `authenticated` in place (measured). No DELETE grant and no DELETE policy anywhere: a number is never released back into the pool. All five functions `REVOKE EXECUTE FROM anon, PUBLIC` + `GRANT TO authenticated`. **Ships dormant**: zero identifiers issued, no backfill, and `users.jkkn_id.issue` is granted to no role. Both migrations were applied and exercised end-to-end on a **throwaway local PostgreSQL 16 cluster**, never against production.
- **2026-08-10** — **The referral audit watched one door; this adds the second one, and the quota** (`20260818030000_extend_referral_source_audit.sql`; **NOT APPLIED — FILE ONLY, apply is Director-gated**). A referral credit can be attached in two places. On the lead (`admission_leads.referral_type` / `referred_by_id` / `referred_by_name`) it is audited into `admission_lead_source_audit`. **Where that trail lives, stated precisely because grepping this repo for it returns nothing:** the table and its trigger **are live on production** — hand-applied through the Supabase Management API on **2026-08-06**, and they have already captured a real change — but they are **not yet in the repository**; **PR #2889** is the pull request that back-fills them into version control. So the trail added here is a **sibling** of that live trigger, and if the database were rebuilt from the repo alone today **neither would exist**: the lead-side one because #2889 has not merged, this one because it is FILE ONLY and unapplied. On the LEARNER — the same three columns on `learners_profiles`, added 2026-04-18 so conversion stopped dropping them — **nothing watched it at all**, because that trigger is bound to a different table and structurally cannot see this one. Door 2 is not theoretical: `trg_sync_learner_referral_to_attribution` (migration `admission/20260506`) exists precisely because attribution gets written from the learner side, and it DELETES the prior `consultant_lead_attributions` row when `referred_by_id` changes — today that delete leaves no trace of whom the credit used to belong to. Director also asked for the quota: `learners_profiles.quota_id` + `counseling_applied` together are the Direct-versus-Counselling distinction, which is what decides whether a referral is payable at all, so changing the quota silently changes the money. Adds **one new table** `referral_attribution_audit` (id, learner_profile_id, changed_field, old_value, new_value, changed_by, changed_at) — **NOT** an overload of the lead audit table, whose subject is a lead and which is neither one-to-one with nor always present alongside a learner; **one SECDEF trigger fn** `fn_audit_learner_referral_attribution()`; **one trigger** `trg_audit_learner_referral_attribution` `AFTER UPDATE OF` the five watched columns `ON learners_profiles FOR EACH ROW`. One row per FIELD that actually changed (`IS DISTINCT FROM`), never one per UPDATE statement. **Three deliberate design calls, each with a failure mode named:** (1) **no foreign key** on `learner_profile_id` — CASCADE would erase the trail exactly when it becomes interesting and RESTRICT would let the trail block a legitimate deletion; an audit row must outlive its subject. (2) **no CHECK on `changed_field`** — the trigger is the only writer, and because audit failures are deliberately swallowed so they can never block a learner update, a CHECK that fell out of step with the trigger would lose rows *silently* instead of failing loudly. (3) **`authenticated` gets SELECT and nothing else**, with no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policy: a trail a client can write to, edit or delete is not evidence of anything, and the SECDEF function runs as the owner so it needs no grant. `REVOKE ALL … FROM anon, PUBLIC, authenticated` then `GRANT SELECT`; RLS on; SELECT policy `is_super_admin() OR is_admin() OR user_has_permission('admission.leads.view')`; `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM anon, PUBLIC` on the trigger fn per CLAUDE.md even though the CI gate exempts `RETURNS trigger`. **Cannot interfere with the sibling trigger:** AFTER, touches nothing but its own table, returns NEW unmodified — so the outcome is the same whichever order the two fire in (alphabetically, `trg_audit_…` first). **Cannot block a learner update:** every error inside the write is downgraded to a `RAISE WARNING`; the cheap distinctness test runs FIRST, *outside* the exception block, so bulk learner edits that mention these columns without changing them never open a subtransaction. **🔴 Known limit, stated not hidden: the trail is NOT institution-scoped** — the table holds no `institution_id`, so whoever holds `admission.leads.view` reads every institution's rows. That matches today's admission desk (`admission` and `counselor` are `institution_scope='all'`) but an own-scoped role granted this key later would read across colleges; scoping needs a join to `learners_profiles.institution_id` and is a deliberate change, not a default. **DORMANT: no backfill** (history before the trigger cannot be reconstructed and a row stamped with the migration date would be manufactured evidence, not recovered evidence), **no UI reads it yet**, no rate set, no commission generated, nothing paid. `admission_lead_source_audit` is untouched — not altered here, and not back-filled here either; that is #2889's job. Idempotent (`CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`, `DROP POLICY`/`DROP TRIGGER` before `CREATE`; contains no DELETE, UPDATE, TRUNCATE or DROP TABLE). Opens with a refuse-to-apply `DO` block naming any missing watched column or permission helper, rather than failing halfway through with a bare "column does not exist". Mirrored into `setup/01_tables.sql`, `02_functions.sql`, `03_policies.sql`, `04_triggers.sql`.

One STABLE SECURITY DEFINER read RPC `fn_referral_review_worklist(p_year integer)` returning jsonb with three arrays: `walkin_credited` (the enquiry is `admission_leads.source='walk_in'` yet an agency is credited — carries `days_after_enquiry`, where 0 means the agency was entered at enquiry creation rather than attached later), `unlinked` (`learners_profiles.referral_type='consultant'` with `referred_by_id IS NULL`, which `fn_generate_referral_commissions` skips in silence), and `no_enquiry_trail` (a credit with no `admission_leads` row behind it — defined by the ABSENCE of an enquiry, NOT by `referral_source='auto_sync_learner'`, so a trail-less credit arriving by another route later cannot hide). - **2026-08-05** — **SCF weekly escalation: the sessions with no addressee are now COUNTED instead of silently discarded** (`20260810160000_scf_escalation_report_unattributed.sql`; **NOT APPLIED — FILE ONLY.** Merging does not apply it; a human applies it via the Management API. The code half is safe to deploy first: the route's new RPC call is wrapped so a missing function is logged and reported, never fatal.) **TIER-1 ADDITIVE — one `CREATE OR REPLACE` of an existing function plus one NEW read-only function; creates no table, alters no column, drops nothing.** PR #2814 (`20260809210000`, applied) stopped this routine crashing on `null value in column "faculty_email" of relation "session_feedback_escalations" violates not-null constraint` by adding `AND f.faculty_email IS NOT NULL` to `fn_scf_apply_weekly_escalation_digest`. Correct, and untouched here — but it converted a loud failure into a **silent** one: `fn_scf_compute_weekly_escalations` still had **no** null filter, so the cron kept receiving NULL-faculty groups, kept spending a Claude call / `ai_jobs` slot writing a leadership briefing for each, and the digest then discarded them and returned `(0, 0)`. Measured live 2026-08-05, week 2026-07-27: `fn_scf_compute_weekly_escalations('2026-07-27')` returned **2 rows, both `faculty_email IS NULL`** — CME346 (7 responses, avg 2.57) and CME365 (11, avg 2.73). Both crossed the escalation threshold, both reached nobody, and nothing anywhere recorded that they existed. This migration (1) adds the same null filter to `fn_scf_compute_weekly_escalations`, rebuilt from its **LIVE `pg_get_functiondef`** with a `diff` proving one added predicate and **nothing removed** (never re-authored from the repo file — that has silently reverted live logic here before), and (2) adds `fn_scf_unattributed_escalations(date)`, which returns exactly the groups that crossed the threshold with no resolvable Senior Learner. Grouping equivalence is not assumed: on the NULL subset, `GROUP BY (institution_id, course_code)` is identical to compute's `GROUP BY (institution_id, lower(faculty_email), course_code)` because every row shares the same NULL and SQL groups NULLs together — verified by the new function reproducing the same two rows with the same counts and averages. **Senior Learner recoverability was investigated and REJECTED on measurement, not assumption.** 19,661 of 134,177 `session_feedback` rows (14.7%) carry neither `faculty_email` nor `faculty_id`. Two paths were scored against the ~109k rows where the truth is known: (a) `timetables.timetable_data → slot_id = session_feedback.period_id → primary_staff_id` → `staff.email` resolves for 100% of rows and so *looks* authoritative, but is **wrong on 34,662 of 109,007 (31.8%)** on the identical source (`async`) and era; widening to the whole `staff_ids` array does not help (truth absent from the slot's `staff_ids` set on 34,194). (b) `student_attendance.attendance_data → assigned_faculty` — the very source `fn_scf_submit_feedback` copies from — is right on 90,235 of 93,410 object-shape rows (96.6%, residual = attendance edited after the feedback was recorded) but on the **array** shape, which dominates the unattributed population, right on only **636 of 1,488 (42.7%)** — wrong more often than right. And for the two sessions that actually escalated, the attendance slot carries **no `assigned_faculty` key at all** (CME346 2 slots, CME365 3 slots), so no path could ever have named anyone. An escalation names a Senior Learner to their HOD; naming the wrong one is a worse failure than naming none, so nothing guesses. **Privileges — deliberately NARROWER than the usual template:** live ACL on 2026-08-05 for both `fn_scf_compute_weekly_escalations` and `fn_scf_apply_weekly_escalation_digest` is exactly `{postgres=X/postgres, service_role=X/postgres}` (anon false, authenticated false), so the new function is `REVOKE … FROM anon, authenticated, PUBLIC` + `GRANT … TO service_role` — a `GRANT TO authenticated` here would widen per-course anonymous learner feedback to every logged-in user. In-file `DO` block asserts compute carries the filter exactly once, that the digest still carries **≥2** (i.e. this file cannot land stale and revert PR #2814), and that anon/authenticated can execute neither. **Version chosen against the LEDGER, not just the repo:** `20260810150000` was free among repo files but is **already recorded in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` as `create_leadership_booking_pages`**, so the file is `20260810160000`; `scripts/ci/check-migration-version-collision.mjs` passes. Rehearsed on prod inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`: compute for the failing week 2 → **0** rows, the new function returns the 2 excluded groups with detail, `fn_scf_apply_weekly_escalation_digest('2026-07-27','{}')` **completes** at `0/0` instead of raising 23502, and — the load-bearing control — a week with real attributable escalations still delivers: `fn_scf_apply_weekly_escalation_digest('2026-07-06','{}')` returned **8 recipients across 2 sessions**. A **separate** post-rollback query confirmed production unchanged: the new function does not exist, compute still returns its 2 unfiltered rows, `session_feedback_escalations` still 10 rows, `scf-esc:%` notifications still 29. **Upstream defect named, deliberately NOT fixed here:** `fn_scf_submit_feedback` reads `v_period -> 'assigned_faculty' ->> 'faculty_email'`, but `assigned_faculty` is stored in **two** shapes and `->>` with a text key on a JSON **array** returns NULL, so team-taught / multi-staff slots lose the Senior Learner identity at write time with no error — the source of all 19,661 rows. It needs its own change plus a decision about the rows already written.

- **2026-08-04** — **IMS transfer engine: two RLS predicates rewritten to match production; new guard against renaming an applied migration** (`20260801002300_ims_transfer_stock_engine.sql` + one defensive line in `20260801002800_ims_transfer_engine_auth_hardening.sql`). **BOTH FILES ARE ALREADY APPLIED TO PROD** — verified by OBJECT, not by ledger: `pg_class` carries `ims_stock_movements`, `pg_proc` carries `ims_pick_fefo_batches` + 3 sibling engine functions, `pg_policies` carries every policy in the file, while `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` holds **no row for `20260801002300` and none for `20260801002301`** (the version PR #2782 proposes to rename it to). **NO NEW DDL AND NOTHING TO APPLY — these edits change what the FILES say, so that re-running them is a no-op against production instead of a regression.** Three predicates diverged from live: (1) `ims_stock_movements_insert` was `WITH CHECK (true)` where production enforces `super_admin OR institution_id = the caller's own institution` — a **tenant boundary replaced by `true`**; (2) `ims_supply_shipment_item_batches` created a `FOR ALL USING (true) WITH CHECK (true)` policy where production carries a SELECT-only policy scoped through shipment_item → shipment → store → institution — and since RLS policies are **OR'd** and `authenticated` holds SELECT on that table, re-adding the permissive one publishes every tenant's batch `cost_price` / `expiry_date` / `quantity`; (3) `ims_stock_movements_select` diverged the OTHER way — the file **narrowed** it, dropping `ims_accessible_institution_ids()` (the cross-institution store grants from `20260728103119`) and `is_super_admin()`, so re-running it would revoke every cross-institution store grant in IMS. A lockout, not a leak, but the same defect shape. All three now reproduce the live `pg_policies` rows verbatim (read 2026-08-04) and were parse- and type-checked against production read-only, as ordinary `SELECT … WHERE <predicate>` filters — nothing was created, altered or rolled back. Because `20260801002300` now creates the batches policy under its final name, the hardening migration gains one `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS ims_supply_shipment_item_batches_select` so a from-scratch replay does not hit 42710; that line is inert against production, which has already run it. **NOT changed, reported instead:** `20260801001500_procurement_po_formats.sql` creates `ppf_institution_scope` with an own-institution predicate where live has `role_has_institution_access(institution_id)` — narrower, not weaker, and correctly superseded by `20260801001600` later in the same batch. **NEW GUARD:** `scripts/ci/check-migration-rename-applied.mjs` + `.github/workflows/migration-rename-applied.yml` refuse a PR that renumbers a migration whose SOURCE version has already been applied. Its sibling `check-migration-version-collision.mjs` only ever checked that the TARGET version was free. Because the ledger is not an index of this repo (a HIT is definitive, a MISS proves nothing), the load-bearing signal is object existence: the guard reads the CREATE / ADD COLUMN / ADD CONSTRAINT statements out of the renamed file and asks the catalogs whether they are already there. Catalog SELECTs only; zero database round-trips on a PR that renames nothing; fail-closed when production is unreachable, with a `-- RENAME-SAFE: <old> -> <new> — <evidence>` header escape that clears **only** the unreachable case and never a positive finding. 18 vitest cases in `__tests__/ci/check-migration-rename-applied.test.ts`. Proven non-vacuous against live production by replaying **all 32** of PR #2782's renames on a throwaway local branch: **27 of 32 came back applied-by-object**, the other 5 are seed/`UPDATE`/`ALTER COLUMN` files that declare no object to test — **not one of the 32 could be shown unapplied.**

- **2026-08-04** — **Evidence natural key now includes `institution_id`, and all 22 writers move with it** (`20260809101400_evidence_key_includes_institution.sql`; **NOT APPLIED — FILE ONLY.** Merging does not apply it; it needs a named human decision and a chosen window because it changes a constraint 22 live SECURITY DEFINER functions depend on, eight of them user-facing triggers). **TIER-2 (constraint swap + 22 function replacements), one transaction.** `quality_evidence_mappings_source_scope_key` was `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (source_table, source_id, body_code, metric_code, programme_id)` — five columns, **no `institution_id`** — so one source row could be claimed by at most ONE institution per body/metric/programme. Consequently `fn_accreditation_evidence_scope`'s `count(DISTINCT institution_id)` per source was always 1, `shared_count` always 0 and `college_total` always equalled `cluster_total`: the cross-college shared-evidence readout was structurally dead code, not an empty result. Measured on prod 2026-08-04 — every NIRF metric returned `shared_count = 0`, and 0 of 11,608 rows had a source claimed by >1 institution. **THE TRAP:** that five-column constraint is the `ON CONFLICT` arbiter of **22 SECURITY DEFINER writers (35 conflict clauses)**; migration `20260809000000` (PR #2807) had *just* rebuilt all 22 onto it after a five-week `42P10` outage that broke five nightly routines. Changing the key without moving all 22 in the same transaction re-creates that outage exactly. So this file, atomically: (1) drops the five-column constraint with its name **resolved from `pg_constraint` by `conrelid`/`contype`/`conkey`** (a hardcoded guess + `IF EXISTS` is a silent no-op that leaves the old key live), (2) adds the six-column `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (…, programme_id, institution_id)`, (3) `CREATE OR REPLACE`s all 22 writers, (4) asserts the six-col key exists, the five-col key is gone, 22 functions carry the six-col target, 0 carry the five-col form, and anon executes none of them. Each function body is its **LIVE `pg_get_functiondef`** with one mechanical `', institution_id'` insertion; the generator asserted per function that removing exactly those insertions reproduces the live source byte-for-byte (never re-authored from a repo file — that has silently reverted a live gate here before). Widening a unique key is strictly *less* restrictive, so it cannot fail on existing data — **confirmed, not assumed**: 0 duplicates on the six columns, 0 NULL `institution_id`. Privileges: `CREATE OR REPLACE` preserves ACLs, and the migration adds **REVOKE-only** anon/PUBLIC locks on the 14 non-trigger functions with **no** blanket `GRANT … TO authenticated` (18 of the 22 grant EXECUTE to nobody but postgres/service_role; granting would widen them). Rehearsed on prod inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`: six-col constraint present, 22/0 target split, ACL census unchanged (4 authenticated / 18 service-role-only / 0 anon), a second college's claim on the same source row accepted (1 → 2 claims) and a repeat upsert still deduping (2), and the **real** `fn_accreditation_evidence_scope('NIRF')` — called as an actual super admin, not re-implemented — returning `TLR_SS college_total=3560 cluster_total=3559 shared_count=1`, the first non-zero `shared_count` this system has produced. Negative control first: the same clone INSERT under the five-column key raises `23505`. Two further negative controls prove the new assertions are not theatre — planting a 23rd writer that keeps the five-column target aborts on ASSERT 3, and revoking `authenticated` from one function aborts on ASSERT 6. A **separate** post-rollback query confirmed production **unchanged** (five-col key live, 22 five-col targets, 11,608 rows, 0 rehearsal rows, 0 leftover control functions). Code half in the same PR: `app/api/cron/coe-result-naac-snapshots/route.ts` and `lib/services/admission/admission-accreditation-report-service.ts` take the arbiter from one shared constant (`lib/types/accreditation`) and **try the LIVE five-column key first, falling back to six on 42P10**, so they are correct under both schemas with no deploy window in either direction and no wasted round trip today (leading with six would put a guaranteed 42P10 + retry on every run, and in the admission path a 400 in the user's browser on every report). The cron route reports `conflict_target_used: 'scoped' | 'legacy' | 'not_attempted'`; the admission service RETURNS `conflictTarget` rather than logging it, because it runs on the browser client where a `console.warn` reaches no operator. Its manual-row pre-exclusion guard now matches on `(source_id, institution_id)` — under the six-column key a manual claim curated by ANOTHER college would otherwise suppress this college's legitimate auto row. **🛑 BLOCKING PREREQUISITE — ENFORCED BY `ASSERT 0`, NOT BY A COMMENT. Measured on prod by parsing the live definitions: 19 withdrawal `DELETE`s across 17 functions carry NO `institution_id` predicate (17, not 16 — `revoke_audit_finding_evidence` has one and is NOT among the 22 conflict-target writers, so an audit scoped to those 22 misses it), and 7 of 11 catch-up anti-joins likewise; the 12 `institution_id = EXCLUDED.institution_id` assignments were the institution-CORRECTION path. Once the key is widened, one college's withdrawal DELETES another college's claim, and a re-stamp inserts a second row instead of updating in place — making `shared_count` report drift as sharing. A prose warning does not stop `supabase db push` or a future runner, so the file now **refuses to commit** while unscoped DELETEs (19) or `institution_id = EXCLUDED.institution_id` re-stamps (14 functions) remain — **unless the junction table is EMPTY**, which is the from-scratch case (`db reset`, fresh CI database, new preview branch) where there are no claims to destroy; there it NOTICEs and proceeds rather than breaking every replay. The gate runs AFTER the function replacements so it also catches the inverse — this file being applied stale after the companion lands, silently reverting the companion's fix. The companion's migration must sort BEFORE `20260809101400`. **Scope limit, stated not implied: the gate reads `pg_proc` bodies only — unscoped DELETEs from application code, dynamic `EXECUTE`, or quoted identifiers are invisible to it, and the 7 catch-up anti-joins are documented but NOT gated (a `NOT EXISTS` has no statement terminator to bound a regex on, and a mis-firing gate would abort a valid apply). "Enforced" means DELETEs and re-stamps.** Detection is deliberately strict: "scoped" requires a real `institution_id = / IN` predicate, not a bare mention, and the exemption is exactly `source_id = OLD.id` (the four `*_evidence_cleanup_on_delete` triggers, where the source row itself is going away) rather than any reference to `OLD.`. Proven live: unmodified, the file aborts with `REFUSING TO APPLY: 19 withdrawal DELETE(s) … and 14 function(s) still re-stamp …`; with the gate excised (i.e. the post-companion state) the full green proof returns.**

UNIQUE(account_id, cadence_month) + 5 indexes + updated_at trigger; (2) canonical dynamic-permission RLS (`is_super_admin() OR is_admin() OR (user_has_permission('social.departments.view'/'.manage') AND role_has_institution_access(institution_id))`), anon revoked; (3) 4 SECURITY DEFINER RPCs — `fn_ig_monthly_reach(uuid,date)` (STABLE reader over ig_monthly_audit), `fn_social_cadence_open(uuid,text,date)` (snapshots baseline + creates a real `projects` row + a `key_result` `project_task` with the HOD assigned RACI **Accountable** via `project_task_assignees.role`, resolving HOD via `staff.profile_id = departments.head_of_department_id`; idempotent per account+month), `fn_social_cadence_record_action(uuid,text,jsonb)`, `fn_social_cadence_close(uuid,text)` (re-measure + metrics_source guard→`unmeasurable`; **teeth**: sets the linked `projects.rag_status` green/amber/red vs the win threshold so the DORMANT `project_at_risk` auto-accountability rule would summon the HOD) — all self-gate (DEFINER bypasses RLS) and end `REVOKE anon,PUBLIC; GRANT authenticated`; (4) seeds 4 `social.cadence.*` policy rows into `platform_policies` (**`social.cadence.enabled=false`** ships DARK, `clock_mode='calendar_month'`, `period_days=30`, `win_delta_pct=10`); (5) merges `social.departments.view`+`.manage` into the scope='own' HOD role (Director-locked owner). Mirrored into `setup/{01_tables,02_functions,03_policies}.sql`. New cron `/api/cron/social-monthly-cadence` (`0 7 1 * *`, after the audit) STAGES elapsed open cycles to `awaiting_close` AND sets the linked project RAG (the same teeth). UI: monthly section on `/admission/social/loop` (`_components/cadence-card.tsx`); the objective auto-appears on the LIVE `/projects` surface as an `is_okr` project (the dead `/okr/department` surface — which reads the dropped `okr_objectives` — is NOT used). Auto-meeting rules stay DORMANT. Spec: `specs/dept-ig-monthly-cadence-2026-07-04.md`. **Deep-review hardening (PR #1781, 2026-07-04):** `project_id` FK is now **`ON DELETE RESTRICT`** (was CASCADE — preserve ledger history) + an idempotent constraint-converge; NEW BEFORE-UPDATE trigger `trg_social_monthly_cadence_project_immutable` makes `project_id` immutable post-insert (blocks raw-PostgREST repointing of the teeth); NEW helper `fn_social_caller_owns_dept(uuid)` (5th DEFINER fn) — all 3 writer RPCs now add a **department-ownership** gate so a scope='own' HOD cannot act on another dept's account; `fn_social_cadence_open` now **self-gates DARK** via `fn_get_policy_bool('social.cadence.enabled')` AND validates any supplied `p_project_id` is an `is_okr` project **in the account's institution** (cross-tenant write fix); `fn_social_cadence_close` + the cron now **re-assert `projects.institution_id = cadence.institution_id`** on every RAG write (DEFINER/service-role tenant guard), the metrics_source guard treats ANY graph⇄business_discovery/NULL mismatch as `unmeasurable` (was only the downgrade), the close UPDATE carries a TOCTOU `status NOT IN ('closed','unmeasurable')` predicate, and the cron skips the project-RAG write when 0 cadence rows staged. **Round-3 hardening (PR #1781, closes both round-2 HIGHs at the root):** the ledger is now **RPC-WRITE-ONLY** — `authenticated` holds **SELECT only** (`REVOKE INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE`; the INSERT/UPDATE RLS policies are dropped), so a raw PostgREST write can no longer bypass the DEFINER guards to point `project_id` at a victim project; `fn_social_cadence_open` **no longer accepts a caller-supplied `project_id`** (the old 4-arg overload is dropped) — open **always** auto-creates its own `is_okr` objective, removing the cross-tenant vector entirely; `fn_social_cadence_close` now **self-gates DARK** too (not just open); the SELECT policy adds **`fn_social_caller_owns_dept(department_id)`** so a scope='own' HOD reads only its own dept's rows; open is **atomic** (advisory xact-lock + `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (account_id,cadence_month) DO NOTHING` + re-select, no raw unique_violation), derives `cadence_month` from **UTC**; `fn_social_caller_owns_dept` is restricted to **`departments.head_of_department_id` only** (dropped the any-active-staff branch); the HOD→staff resolution adds **`s.institution_id = v_institution_id`** (no cross-tenant owner); an **`unmeasurable`** close now **RESETS** the project RAG to green/0% (undoes any cron-fabricated green/red); and `percent_complete` is written on **both** the cron and `close` (never one without the other).

    - `ims.indents.approve` → UPDATE on `ims_indent_requests` when status moves to `approved`/`rejected`
    - `ims.sales.refund` → UPDATE on `ims_sales` when status='cancelled'
    - `ims.transfers.receive` → UPDATE on `ims_supply_shipments` & `ims_supply_shipment_items` when status moves to `received`/`received_with_variance`
  - **Strategy: additive (soft-wire), not replacement**. Postgres ORs multiple permissive policies for the same verb — these new policies grant access alongside the existing helper-generated `_insert`/`_update`/`_delete`. Existing roles keyed on `ims.indents.edit` / `ims.sales.create` / `ims.transfers.dispatch` keep their authority.
  - **Production migration applied** (via `mcp__supabase__apply_migration`): `ims_granular_permission_overrides_2026_05_02`. 6 new policies live: `ims_indent_requests_{insert_create, delete_specific, update_approve}`, `ims_sales_update_refund`, `ims_supply_shipments_update_receive`, `ims_supply_shipment_items_update_receive`.
  - **Status-transition gating**: WITH CHECK clauses on the new UPDATE policies constrain `NEW.status` to the specific transitions each verb represents — so a user with only `ims.indents.approve` can flip status to approved/rejected but cannot edit other fields under that policy (general edits still require `ims.indents.edit`). Catalog verbs now match DB-enforced verbs.

- **2026-04-22** — Staff INSERT fails 42501 "permission denied for table users" for HOD/non-super-admin staff.create
  - New migration `supabase/migrations/20260422000003_fix_sync_staff_trigger_auth_access.sql`
  - `02_functions.sql`: `sync_staff_to_profiles()` trigger function switched from SECURITY INVOKER (default) to SECURITY DEFINER with `SET search_path = public`. Body was also updated to mirror the live version that had drifted from source (profile_id-first lookup + auth-linked-first tiebreaker on email collisions).
  - Root cause: the trigger's email-fallback branch orders by `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM auth.users u WHERE u.id = p.id)` to prefer auth-linked profiles on duplicate emails. `auth.users` grants SELECT only to `postgres` — not to `service_role`/`authenticated`/`anon` — so with SECURITY INVOKER every insert failed unless the caller was the superuser. `POST /api/staff` uses `supabaseAdmin` (service_role) and still tripped it because the trigger ran as the invoker.
  - Fix: DEFINER makes the function execute as its owner (`postgres`), which has the grant. `search_path` is pinned to close the classic definer hijack vector. No behaviour change for callers.
  - Reported by director 2026-04-22 ~15:35 IST when HOD test user hit "Failed to create staff record" with server-side `code: 42501, message: 'permission denied for table users'`.

  - New migration `supabase/migrations/20260421000002_persona_design_pr4_rls_retrofit.sql` (~450 lines, atomic BEGIN/COMMIT)
  - PHASE 1: Drops 46 legacy `_institution_isolation` policies (FOR ALL + hardcoded 'super_admin' string — CLAUDE.md anti-pattern).
  - PHASE 2: Creates ~184 new policies (46 tables × 4 = SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) using the standardized pattern: `is_super_admin() OR is_admin() OR (user_has_permission(key) AND role_has_*_access(...))`.
    - 13 institution-only tables: +role_has_institution_access(institution_id)
    - 18 block-scoped tables (have block_id): +role_has_block_access(block_id)
    - 11 block-conceptual tables (no block_id column): app-layer filters block narrowing; RLS uses institution-only
    - 7 mess contract-scoped tables (have caterer_id): +role_has_contract_access(caterer_id, 'caterer')
  - PHASE 3: UPDATEs each of the 10 new roles' permissions jsonb with their scaffolding (warden gets 51 keys, chief_warden 84, accreditation_officer 23, etc.)
  - Atomic cutover — RLS and role perms land together (partial = all-super_admin-only lockout, avoided via BEGIN/COMMIT).
  - Depends on: #275 (PR-1 scope helpers), #276 (PR-2 10 roles), #277 (PR-3 permission keys)

- **2026-04-21** — Persona Design PR-3: +127 permission keys in PERMISSION_CATEGORIES (TypeScript-only, no DB migration)
  - `lib/constants/permissions.ts`: replaced 1-key Campus Living stub with 121 granular keys. Submodules: blocks, rooms, beds, allocations, wardens, gate_passes, visitors, leave, attendance, maintenance, housekeeping, laundry, safety (incl. anti_ragging), health, fees, deposits, mess (caterers/menu/meals/billing/feedback/waste), alerts, pulse, wellness, community, analytics, reports (NAAC/NIRF/AICTE/anti-ragging quarterly), parent_portal.
  - Also added 6 `users.*.access` keys for PR-1's scope-extension junction tables: `users.block_access.{view,manage}`, `users.relationship.{view,manage}`, `users.contract_access.{view,manage}`.
  - Catalog-sync verified: every MENU_PERMISSIONS campus_living.* key now has a PERMISSION_CATEGORIES home (was: 29 drift warnings; now: 0).
  - No DB changes — roles still have empty permissions jsonb. PR-4 bulk-updates each role's permissions to wire the new keys alongside RLS retrofit on 48 hostel_*/mess_* tables.

- **2026-04-21** — Persona Design PR-2: 10 new roles for Campus Living + external actors
  - New migration `supabase/migrations/20260421000001_persona_design_pr2_ten_roles.sql`
  - Roles seeded: warden, chief_warden, gate_security, housekeeping_staff, parent, mess_caterer, maintenance_vendor, hostel_office, anti_ragging_member, accreditation_officer
  - All have `permissions='{}'` (empty) and `module_scopes='{}'` — intentional. PR-3 adds catalog keys to `PERMISSION_CATEGORIES`; PR-4 retrofits RLS on 48 hostel_*/mess_* tables AND bulk-updates each role's permissions jsonb to grant its scaffolding.
  - `accreditation_officer` is the only scope=`all` role (cross-institution evidence pull for NAAC/NIRF/UGC). Nine others are scope=`own`. External actors (parent, mess_caterer, maintenance_vendor) use scope=`own` + row-level checks via PR-1 junction tables (user_block_access, user_learner_relationship, user_contract_access).
  - Idempotent via `ON CONFLICT (role_key) DO NOTHING`.
  - Depends on PR-1 (#275 merged 2026-04-21) for scope helpers.

- **2026-04-21** — Persona Design PR-1: scope-extension helpers (block/relationship/contract scopes)
  - `01_tables.sql`: new junction tables `user_block_access`, `user_learner_relationship`, `user_contract_access`. Each has `revoked_at` for soft-delete + audit trail. `user_contract_access.contract_id` is polymorphic (caterer/maintenance_vendor/laundry_vendor/amc).
  - `02_functions.sql`: 3 new SECURITY DEFINER helpers — `role_has_block_access(uuid)`, `role_has_relationship_access(uuid)`, `role_has_contract_access(uuid, text DEFAULT NULL)`. All mirror `role_has_institution_access()` pattern: super_admin bypass, NULL target = system-wide, otherwise consult junction table.
  - `03_policies.sql`: RLS on the 3 junction tables. Standard contract: super_admin/admin full CRUD; users see own grants; delegated via `users.block_access|relationship|contract_access.{view,manage}` permission keys (added in PR-3).
  - Context: MyJKKN's `institution_scope` supports only 'all'|'own'. Campus Living needs block-level (warden), relationship (parent), and contract (caterer/vendor) scopes. This PR is PR-1 of 4 — INERT infrastructure until PR-2 (roles), PR-3 (permission keys), PR-4 (RLS retrofit on 48 hostel_*/mess_* tables).
  - See: `docs/persona-design/scope-extension-pr1.md`

- **2026-04-18** — Seat Configuration page invisible to admission role with scope='all' (programs returned 0 rows)
  - `03_policies.sql`: rewrote SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies on `programs`, `degrees`, `departments` to use `role_has_institution_access(institution_id)` instead of hardcoded `institution_id = get_current_user_institution_id()`. Added `admission.settings.seats.view` / `admission.settings.seats.manage` as acceptable SELECT permissions for programs/degrees/departments so seat config works without granting Organization module perms.
  - `03_policies.sql`: rewrote `intake_history` policies — previously required a `user_institution_access` row (locked out super admins who didn't have one). Now uses the standard contract `is_super_admin() OR is_admin() OR (role_has_institution_access(...) AND user_has_permission('admission.settings.seats.*'))`.
  - Root cause: the legacy own-institution equality check in RLS ignored `institution_scope='all'` on the admission role.

- **2026-04-15** — `get_user_roles_with_details` now returns scope columns (fixes "Employment Information section not hiding for own_records users")
  - `02_functions.sql`: added `institution_scope text` and `module_scopes jsonb` to the function's RETURNS TABLE. Required DROP+CREATE because Postgres can't ALTER return shape. Without these, client-side `usePermissions().getModuleScope()` always read undefined and fell back to defaults.
  - Migration: `user_roles_details_include_scopes`. No client code change required — existing `(r as any).module_scopes` reads now resolve.

  - `lib/services/staff/staff-service.ts`: `updateStaff` now skips `assignRoles` when `data.role_key === currentStaff.role_key` (avoided unnecessary DELETE+INSERT cycle that surfaced as a 42501 RLS error for callers without `roles.create`). Pre-fetch select extended to include `role_key`.
  - Migration: `user_roles_align_to_permission_contract`.

  - `02_functions.sql`: `get_user_module_scope(module_key)` returns most-permissive scope across user's roles; `role_has_module_access(module_key, institution_id, owner_email)` combines that with row-level checks.
  - `03_policies.sql`: staff SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE policies switched to `role_has_module_access('staff', institution_id, institution_email)`. INSERT stays institution-only ('own_records' doesn't apply to creation). Self-view via `institution_email = auth.email()` preserved.
  - Migration: `add_module_scopes_to_custom_roles` + `staff_rls_use_module_scope`. UI: new "Module Access Scope" section in Role Management edit dialog.

  - `02_functions.sql`: mirrored `role_has_institution_access(check_institution_id uuid)` back into source (was DB-only drift). SECURITY DEFINER, STABLE.
  - `03_policies.sql`: rewrote 4 `staff` policies + `employment_categories`, `custom_roles`, and `staff_plans` insert/update/delete policies to the standard contract `is_super_admin() OR is_admin() OR (user_has_permission(...) AND role_has_institution_access(institution_id))`. Dropped legacy hardcoded-role policies (incl. `staff_select_event_coordinator`, "Admins can manage staff_plans...", duplicate `custom_roles` SELECT policies). Preserved staff service-role bypass and email-based self-view/self-edit.
  - Migration: `staff_module_rls_align_to_permission_contract`. Pre-flight verified zero real-user impact.

## 📁 Directory Structure

```
supabase/
├── setup/              # Initial setup files (RUN IN ORDER)
│   ├── 00_master_setup.sql    # Extensions, types, helper functions
│   ├── 01_tables.sql           # ALL table definitions
│   ├── 02_functions.sql        # Custom functions and procedures
│   ├── 03_policies.sql         # RLS policies for all tables
│   ├── 04_triggers.sql         # Database triggers
│   ├── 05_views.sql            # Database views
│   └── 06_seed_data.sql        # Optional seed data
├── migrations/         # Version-controlled migrations (DO NOT EDIT OLD FILES)
├── tables/            # Individual table references (READ-ONLY)
├── functions/         # Individual function references (READ-ONLY)
├── policies/          # Individual policy references (READ-ONLY)
├── triggers/          # Individual trigger references (READ-ONLY)
└── views/            # Individual view references (READ-ONLY)
```

## 🔴 STRICT RULES

### Rule 1: NEVER Create Duplicate Files

- ❌ DO NOT create new files for existing objects
- ✅ UPDATE existing files with proper comments

### Rule 2: File Update Protocol

When updating any SQL file:

```sql
-- Updated: 2025-01-16 by [reason]
-- Previous version backed up as comments below
-- [Your changes here]
```

### Rule 3: Single Location Policy

- Tables: ONLY in `setup/01_tables.sql`
- Functions: ONLY in `setup/02_functions.sql`
- Policies: ONLY in `setup/03_policies.sql`
- Triggers: ONLY in `setup/04_triggers.sql`
- Views: ONLY in `setup/05_views.sql`

## 🚀 Setup Instructions

### For New Clone/Setup:

```bash
# Run in Supabase SQL Editor in this exact order:
1. Run supabase/setup/00_master_setup.sql
2. Run supabase/setup/01_tables.sql
3. Run supabase/setup/02_functions.sql (when created)
4. Run supabase/setup/03_policies.sql (when created)
5. Run supabase/setup/04_triggers.sql (when created)
6. Run supabase/setup/05_views.sql (when created)
7. Run supabase/setup/06_seed_data.sql (optional)
```

### For Updates:

```bash
# NEVER create new files. Update existing files:
1. Open the appropriate file based on object type
2. Add update comments with date and reason
3. Make your changes
4. Update this index file
5. Test in development first
```

  **Purpose**: Track team path declarations after Demo Day, individual learner identity-ladder progression (5 levels), and structured case study narratives for `solve_for_industry` / `jicate_solutions` tracks.

- `evidence JSONB`, `awarded_by TEXT` (default `'system'`)
- UNIQUE on `(profile_id, event_id, level)`

**case_studies** — New table:
- `event_id` → `startup_events(id)`, `team_id` → `event_registrations(id)`

- UNIQUE on `(event_id, team_id)`; `updated_at` auto-managed by trigger

### 2026-03-08: Demo Day Evaluation — appathon_verifications Table

- **Files Updated**:
  - `supabase/setup/01_tables.sql` — Added `appathon_verifications` table with 4 indexes
  - `supabase/setup/03_policies.sql` — Added RLS (ENABLE + 3 policies: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE)

  **Purpose**: Core evaluation table for Demo Day. One row per evaluator per team. Evaluators verify team claims (live URL, user counts, revenue) during presentations and record tier scores (T1–T4) + revenue bonus. Calculated scores are server-recomputed and not trusted from client. Admission restricted to staff assigned as judge/panel_chair/evaluator for `demo_day` day_type.

**appathon_verifications** — New table:
- `submission_id` → `event_submissions(id)`
- `evaluator_id` → `profiles(id)`
- `venue_id` → `event_venue_assignments(id)`
- `presented BOOLEAN`, `presentation_slot INT`
- `app_live BOOLEAN`
- `claimed_users`, `claimed_active_users`, `claimed_revenue` — copied at freeze time
- `verified_users`, `verified_active_users`, `verified_revenue` — evaluator-confirmed

  **Migration Strategy**:
  - Scenario A: Merged records (admission + student) - uses student data as primary source
  - Scenario B: Admission-only records (pending/approved applications)
  - Scenario C: Student-only records (orphaned or direct-created students)
  - Zero data loss verification with rollback capability

### 2025-02-07: Bug Report Display ID Race Condition Fix 🚨 CRITICAL

- **File**: `migrations/20250207_fix_bug_report_display_id_race_condition.sql` ✅ **APPLIED**

  **Problem Solved**:
  - Fixed race condition causing "Unable to generate report ID" errors
  - Eliminated ~87% failure rate during concurrent bug submissions
  - Gap of 2,062 between actual reports (306) and max ID (2368) proved the issue

  **Solution**:
  - Replaced `SELECT MAX()+1` pattern with PostgreSQL SEQUENCE
  - Created `bug_reports_display_id_seq` starting at 2369
  - Updated `generate_bug_display_id()` to use atomic `nextval()` operation
  - Recreated triggers to use new function

  **Impact**:
  - ✅ Zero race conditions (atomic database operations)
  - ✅ Perfect concurrency handling (unlimited simultaneous users)
  - ✅ No more user-facing errors
  - ✅ Consecutive IDs with no gaps (except deletions)

  **Testing**:
  - Verified 10 consecutive unique IDs generated successfully
  - Confirmed trigger functioning correctly
  - Sequence properly configured and indexed

  **Files Updated**:
  - `setup/02_functions.sql` - Updated function to use SEQUENCE
  - `migrations/20250207_fix_bug_report_display_id_race_condition.sql` - Migration file

### **2026-01-28: Learner-Profile Sync Enhancement**

**Issue**: College email updates in `learners_profiles` didn't sync to `profiles` table, roles stuck as 'guest', no mismatch detection.

**Solution**: Three-layer fix for comprehensive synchronization:

1. **Enhanced Service Layer** (`lib/services/learner-profile-service.ts`):
   - Smart profile lookup (by email, then learner_id fallback)
   - Syncs ALL fields: email, role, is_active, learner_id, institution_id, department_id
   - Comprehensive logging for debugging

2. **Database Triggers** (AUTO-SYNC):
   - `trg_sync_learner_email_to_profile`: Auto-syncs college_email changes
   - `trg_sync_learner_status_to_profile`: Auto-syncs lifecycle_status to is_active
   - Handles orphaned profile linking

3. **Diagnostic & Repair Tools**:
   - `scripts/debug-learner-profile-sync.ts`: Detect mismatches
   - `scripts/repair-learner-profile-sync.ts`: Auto-fix issues
   - `scripts/LEARNER_PROFILE_SYNC_GUIDE.md`: Complete usage guide

**Database Changes**:
```sql
-- New Functions (02_functions.sql)
CREATE FUNCTION sync_learner_email_to_profile() -- Syncs email, role, org data
CREATE FUNCTION sync_learner_status_to_profile() -- Syncs is_active status

-- New Triggers (04_triggers.sql)
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_learner_email_to_profile -- On INSERT/UPDATE college_email
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_learner_status_to_profile -- On UPDATE lifecycle_status
```

**Results**:
- ✅ Email changes automatically sync to profiles table
- ✅ User roles correctly set to 'student'
- ✅ Orphaned profiles automatically linked
- ✅ is_active status always matches lifecycle_status
- ✅ Comprehensive logging and diagnostics
- ✅ Automatic repair tools available

**Usage**:
```bash
# Detect issues
npx tsx scripts/debug-learner-profile-sync.ts

# Fix issues (dry run first)
npx tsx scripts/repair-learner-profile-sync.ts --dry-run
npx tsx scripts/repair-learner-profile-sync.ts
```

### **2025-01-31: Advanced Learner Analytics Schema Update**

**Purpose**: Add database support for 4 new analytics categories: Intake & Capacity, Geography, Trends, and School Feeders

**Database Changes**:

1. **learners_profiles table** (5 new columns):
   - `school_type TEXT` - Classification: government, aided, private, cbse, icse, state_board
   - `school_district TEXT` - School's district location
   - `school_taluk TEXT` - School's taluk location
   - `medium_of_instruction TEXT` - english, tamil, both
   - `location_type TEXT` - urban, semi_urban, rural (auto-classified)

2. **programs table** (3 new columns):
   - `sanctioned_intake INTEGER` - Approved intake capacity (default: 0)
   - `actual_intake INTEGER` - Current admitted students (default: 0)
   - `academic_year_id UUID` - Link to academic year

3. **intake_history table** (NEW):
   - Tracks historical intake data for 3-year stability index calculations
   - Columns: institution_id, program_id, academic_year_id, sanctioned_intake, actual_intake, waitlist_count, dropout_count
   - Unique constraint on (program_id, academic_year_id)
   - 3 indexes for analytics queries (program, year, institution)

4. **Indexes Created** (4 new):
   - `idx_learners_profiles_school_type` - Filter by school type
   - `idx_learners_profiles_location_type` - Filter by location classification
   - `idx_learners_profiles_medium_instruction` - Filter by medium
   - `idx_programs_academic_year` - Program capacity by year

5. **RLS Policies** (4 new for intake_history):
   - SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE policies based on user_institution_access
   - DELETE policy restricted to admin access_type

**Analytics Enabled**:
- ✅ Intake & Capacity Analytics (seat utilization, over-intake alerts, waitlist conversion, 3-year stability)
- ✅ Geography Analytics (district/taluk contribution, hostel ratios - data already 100% available)
- ✅ Trend Analytics (gender ratio, category mix, first-generation, income distribution)
- ✅ School Feeder Analytics (feeder institution tracking, school type classification)

- All new fields are optional (backward compatible)
- Existing 3,506 learner profiles need data migration for analytics fields
- Data migration scripts to populate school_type, location_type automatically
- Intake history seeding script to backfill last 3 years

### Faculty-engagement adoption + hard-gate enforcement (DARK, compliance-gated) — 2026-07-04
- File: `supabase/migrations/20260731020000_scf_hard_gate_enforcement_and_coupling.sql` (NOT applied at PR-open — apply via Management API at/after merge, AND only after Director + legal/compliance review of the exam-eligibility coupling; spec risk R2).
- Spec: `specs/faculty-engagement-adoption-2026-07-04.md` (Director decisions LOCKED — max enforcement, informed of R1–R3).
- NON-DESTRUCTIVE INVARIANT: nothing here mutates `student_attendance.attendance_data`. Confirmation + effective-% are DERIVED, recomputable reads.
- `fn_scf_faculty_completion(date,date)` — DROP+recreate to ADD `start_time`/`end_time` (PR-A current-period spotlight) + `gate_mode` (resolved per session institution via `fn_get_policy_text`) + derived `session_status` (PR-C). `session_status='incomplete'` ONLY when `gate_mode='hard'` AND pending>0 AND within window → INERT until the config flip (dark). REVOKE anon,PUBLIC / GRANT authenticated.
- `fn_scf_notify_session_pending(date,uuid,text)` — PR-B faculty-triggered per-session nudge; reuses the `fn_scf_nudge_pending_learners` two-write (`notifications` + `user_notifications`) delivery path, assigned-faculty OR super-admin OR **same-tenant** admin (`is_admin() AND role_has_institution_access(session.institution_id)` — no cross-tenant nudge), identity-scoped, atomically idempotent per learner/session/day (`idempotency_key` includes `timetable_id`; `ON CONFLICT ... WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING`). `SET statement_timeout='20s'`. REVOKE anon,PUBLIC / GRANT authenticated.
- `fn_scf_set_gate_mode(text,uuid)` — PR-C super-admin BREAK-GLASS kill-switch; upserts the `session_feedback.gate_mode` platform_policies row (global or per-institution) via UPDATE-then-INSERT-if-absent (NOT `ON CONFLICT`, so the kill-switch cannot throw on index-inference; matches the coupling-flag seed pattern). Revert to `visibility`/`off` halts enforcement in one call, no deploy. super_admin ONLY. REVOKE anon,PUBLIC / GRANT authenticated.
- `fn_scf_effective_attendance(date,date,uuid,uuid,uuid,uuid)` — PR-D DERIVED "effective attendance %": per learner official % vs confirmed-only effective % (present-but-no-feedback lowers it). Read-only over `student_attendance` + `session_feedback`; NEVER writes `attendance_data`. Authz mirrors `fn_scf_confirmation_rollup` (no `is_admin()` scope bypass). Counts only — no feedback content. REVOKE anon,PUBLIC / GRANT authenticated.
- Seed: `session_feedback.attendance_coupling_enabled` global row, DEFAULT **FALSE** (dark). Gates the effective-% in `AttendanceConsolidationService.getEffectiveAttendanceCoupling`; while OFF nothing is computed and the official % is untouched. `session_feedback.gate_mode` default STAYS `visibility` (unchanged).
- Round-2 (deep-review) hardening — 2026-07-04 (no signature/shape change): (1) nudge tenant-scoped (above); (2) completion window anchored to IST (`attendance_date::timestamp AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata'`) not server-UTC; (3) full session identity everywhere — `timetable_id` added to `fn_scf_effective_attendance`'s `DISTINCT ON` dedup key AND every `session_feedback` confirmation match (effective_attendance, faculty_completion, nudge) so two classes sharing a period slot on one day don't collapse/false-confirm; (4) `fn_scf_faculty_completion` gets `SET statement_timeout='20s'`; (5) faculty reward card counts (page) base numerator+denominator on answered sessions only (empty sessions no longer dilute/inflate); (6) nudge button/toast surface skipped-no-profile learners. Still fully DARK.

Closes the arming/reverting **authz asymmetry**: `platform_policies` RLS is `is_super_admin() OR is_admin()`, so a tenant admin could set `session_feedback.gate_mode='hard'` and ARM enforcement while the break-glass revert is super-admin-only. ### SCF generator maturity — policy lookup hoisted per-institution (PERF, live 500 fix) — 2026-07-09
- `20260709000100_scf_two_sided_48h_window.sql` placed `fn_get_policy_int('session_feedback.window_hours', 48, f.institution_id)` inside the ROW-LEVEL `WHERE` of `fn_scf_candidate_windows` + `fn_scf_ai_signal`. `f.institution_id` is correlated, so the planner cannot hoist it → the policy fn ran ~23,000×/run (23,232 rows in the 7-day window; only **6** distinct institutions and exactly **one** global policy row — every call returned the same constant). `scf-generate-suggestions` has returned `HTTP 500 · canceling statement due to statement timeout` on every run since that migration landed.
- Fix: resolve `{institution_id → window_hours}` ONCE in a **MATERIALIZED** CTE, then single-row `CROSS JOIN` + map lookup. `MATERIALIZED` is load-bearing — a plain CTE is INLINED in PG12+ and gets rescanned per row (a first attempt without it only moved 35.4s → 32.5s). NULL institutions use a `'_null'` text key rather than a sentinel UUID that could collide with a real id.
- Measured on prod in a rolled-back txn: `fn_scf_candidate_windows` **18,951ms → 167ms** (395 rows both sides; `EXCEPT` in both directions = 0); `fn_scf_ai_signal` **1,668ms → 58ms** (identical row). Per-institution override semantics preserved exactly. Signature/volatility/security unchanged; grants restated explicitly (candidate_windows = service_role only; ai_signal = authenticated + service_role — the `/api/academic/session-feedback/ai-suggest-improvement` route calls it with the caller's session).
- Do NOT raise `statement_timeout` instead: the cost is O(rows-in-window) and `session_feedback` grows ~3,300 rows/day.
- Location: `supabase/migrations/20260709090000_fix_scf_policy_lookup_per_institution.sql`. SQL-only PR (no code change) — safe to apply as soon as it merges.

- Director decisions 2026-07-10 (verbatim): **"Principal only"**; **"Steady alerts"** — a course must be below target 2 weekly runs IN A ROW to enter the list, and leadership is messaged ONLY when the list CHANGES (a course enters or recovers).
- Why new state: `obe_course_attainment_rollup` is upserted IN PLACE every weekly run (no run history), so 2-consecutive-runs persistence lives in new `copo_below_target_state` (one row per institution × course_code, UNIQUE key all-NOT-NULL; RLS: accreditation viewers institution-scoped, writes RPC-only).
- `fn_copo_track_below_target()` (SECDEF, `search_path=public`, service_role ONLY — anon/authenticated/PUBLIC revoked, verified `has_function_privilege` anon=f auth=f service_role=t in rolled-back txn): ingests current rollups with CONFIDENT institution stamps only (`institution_match IN ('unique_course_match','manual_assignment')` — alerting a possibly-wrong Principal is worse than waiting), extends/resets streaks, returns per-institution entered/recovered changes jsonb. Idempotency key `copo_below_target:<institution>:<date>`. Response keys: `alerts_sent`, `institutions_notified`, `entered`, `recovered`.

Real data at validation time: 48 confident evaluable rollups, 15 below target after probes.
- ⚠️ First LIVE run after apply seeds streaks (consec=1) for the ~13 currently-below courses with NO alert; the second weekly run alerts Principals for any still below — that ramp IS the Director's "Steady alerts" design.

### 2026-07-21: PDE cross-tenant RLS fix (SECURITY)
- **The defect:** three PDE tables carried `USING (true)` SELECT policies *named* for admin access — `pde_sub_admin_read` (pde_submissions), `pde_events_admin_read` (pde_engagement_events), `pde_daily_admin_read` (pde_engagement_daily). RLS policies are OR'd, so each silently defeated the correct own-row policy beside it: **any authenticated user could read every learner's work in every institution.** `pde_engagement_daily` additionally carried `pde_daily_write [ALL] USING(true) WITH CHECK(true)` — any authenticated user could insert/alter/**delete** the engagement rows that feed at-risk detection (a learner could delete the evidence they were struggling). A codebase sweep found NO application writer for that table (every reference is `.select`), so nothing legitimate depended on it.
- **Exposure at fix time: 0 rows** in all three tables (PDE has no real learner participation) — a landmine, not a breach, and the cheapest possible moment to fix.
- **Tenant scoping with NO schema change:** none of these tables has `institution_id` (PDE predates the convention), but a join path already exists — `pde_submissions.assessment_id → pde_assessments.course_id → vac_courses.institution_id`, and both engagement tables carry `course_id` directly. Policies use `EXISTS` against that path, avoiding a denormalised column + backfill that could drift.
- 4 permissive policies dropped; 5 created (`pde_sub_staff_read`, `pde_events_own_read`, `pde_events_staff_read`, `pde_daily_staff_read`, `pde_daily_admin_write`). Learner self-access preserved throughout (`pde_sub_own_read`, `pde_daily_own_read` untouched; `pde_events_own_read` newly ADDED because that table's only read path had been the permissive policy).
- **Validated on prod in a rolled-back transaction:** permissive policies 4 → 0, 5 new policies present, 2 learner self-read policies intact; prod re-confirmed unchanged after ROLLBACK.
- Director decision 2026-07-21: "fix roles AND separate colleges". Location: `supabase/migrations/20260721230000_pde_rls_cross_tenant_fix.sql` — **NOT yet applied to prod.**

### 2026-07-21: Bridge sh_notifications into the main notification pipeline
- **Two defects, one root cause (schema drift).** (1) `lib/services/solutions/notifications-service.ts` inserted `type` / `link` / `read` — **none of which exist** on live `sh_notifications` (real columns: `notification_type` NOT NULL, `action_url`, `is_read`) and never supplied the NOT NULL `notification_type`, so **every Solutions Hub notification write threw**. Same drift class as #2172 (work-pulse + learn notify) and #2168. (2) Even when fixed, `sh_notifications` is read only by `/api/solutions/notifications` — no bell, no push, no WhatsApp — so its four real events (payment received, deliverable approved/revision, assignment approved, MoU expiring) reached nobody.
- **Exposure at fix time: 0 rows** in `sh_notifications` — because writing to it was structurally impossible, not because nothing fired. Cheapest possible moment to fix: before Solutions Hub adoption puts real payments and deliverables through it.
- **Why a DB trigger, not app code:** the Solutions Hub service layer extends `BaseService`, which uses the **browser (RLS-bound)** Supabase client. Live `notifications` INSERT is gated to `is_super_admin() OR is_admin()`, and `user_notifications` INSERT is super-admin only — an app-side insert would be **silently denied for exactly the team members who trigger these events**, recreating the #2172 silent-no-op class. `SECURITY DEFINER` bypasses that, and a trigger catches every current *and future* writer of `sh_notifications` for free.
- Payload shape follows the #2172 canonical helper: `body` (not `message`), `url`, `created_by` = anchor recipient, `targeting.user_ids`, `category='solutions'`, `kind='work_item'` (keeps these off the `/notifications/admin` announcement surface). Bridge is wrapped in `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS` so a main-pipeline failure **can never break the source write**.
- **Validated on prod in a rolled-back transaction:** one `sh_notifications` insert produced `main_rows=1`, `link_rows=1`, `body='Payment of 50,000 received…'`, `kind=work_item`, `category=solutions`, `url=/solutions/abc123`; prod re-confirmed clean after ROLLBACK (0 leftover rows, trigger/function absent).
- Location: `supabase/migrations/20260722090000_bridge_sh_notifications_to_main_pipeline.sql` — **NOT yet applied to prod.**

### 2026-07-22: PDE at-risk — stop a failing score being masked by inactivity (APPLIED)
- `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW pde_at_risk_learners` appending two columns: `is_low_scoring` (`COALESCE(avg(assessment_avg_score) < 50, false)`) and `has_assessment_scores` (`count(assessment_avg_score) > 0`). `risk_level` and all 10 original columns are **unchanged** — the cron, history rollup and admin page all read them, and redefining the band mid-flight would change flag-history semantics.
- **The defect:** `risk_level` is a single-branch CASE where inactivity outranks score, so a learner absent 5 days AND averaging 20% was labelled `warning` — indistinguishable from an absent learner averaging 90%. The "Struggling / Avg score below 50%" count therefore undercounted, and triage sorted by absence rather than by who was failing.
- **Premise correction:** the change was requested on the belief that an ACTIVE learner scoring 20% is never flagged. Verified empirically against the live CASE — that learner already evaluates to `struggling`. The real defect is the masking above. Recorded so the reasoning is not lost.
- `has_assessment_scores` exists because `NULL < 50` is NULL, so a learner with no completed assessments falls to `on_track` — arguably right, but previously indistinguishable from a genuinely healthy learner.
- Companion UI: the struggling count now filters on `is_low_scoring` (matching the card's existing "Avg score below 50%" label, which the old count did not honour); a "Low score" badge renders beside the band only when the band would otherwise hide it; the score column shows "no scores yet" instead of "-" when there is no evidence.
- Dry-run in rolled-back txn (12 columns, 2 new, 5 originals intact) then **APPLIED 2026-07-21**; post-apply matrix verified: absent+failing → band=warning, is_low_scoring=true; absent+passing → band=warning, is_low_scoring=false.
- Location: `supabase/migrations/20260722000500_pde_at_risk_unmask_low_score.sql`.
