### fn_update_recruitment_step_comment — NULL guard let an anonymous caller edit review comments (2026-07-30)
- `supabase/migrations/20260730130000_fix_recruitment_comment_null_guard.sql` — **NOT applied to prod — Director-gated apply, ships as its own PR.** Rolled-back-validated only; both apply-time asserts passed inside `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`, and `anon` still holds EXECUTE on prod (proof the dry run did not leak into a live apply).
- **The bug.** The guard read `IF NOT ((v_decided_by IS NOT NULL AND v_decided_by = v_uid::text) OR is_super_admin() OR user_has_permission('hr.recruitment.approve.override')) THEN RAISE`. For an unauthenticated caller `auth.uid()` is NULL, so the first term is NULL; `is_super_admin()` and `user_has_permission()` both return a proper `false`; `NULL OR false OR false` = **NULL**; `NOT NULL` = **NULL**; and plpgsql does not take an IF branch whose condition is NULL. **The RAISE was skipped and execution fell through to the UPDATE.** Measured in the definer context on prod 2026-07-30 (that is what runs inside a SECDEF body — testing as `SET ROLE anon` is NOT equivalent and merely errors on `user_has_permission`).
- The function was anon-executable, so the caller needed nothing but a candidate UUID. **7 of 19** candidates carry a decided step with `decided_by` set — the precondition — and were writable. The write was NOT executed; proving it fully would mean modifying production recruitment data.
- **Note the asymmetry:** `false OR false` is false, but `NULL OR false` is NULL. The guard failed OPEN for exactly the caller it most needed to stop, and behaved correctly for every logged-in user — which is why it went unnoticed. Same class as the SECDEF super-admin guards corrected 2026-07-26; see `feedback_secdef_guard_not_null_safe_falls_through`.
- **Fix:** two independent barriers — an early `IF v_uid IS NULL THEN RAISE ... 42501` before any row is read, and `COALESCE(..., false)` around the whole authorization expression so a NULL from any future term fails CLOSED. Plus `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` (both — the function carried no explicit `anon=X`, it inherited from PUBLIC, so revoking anon alone is a silent no-op). The rest of the body is byte-for-byte the deployed version; no behaviour change for any caller previously allowed through.
- Once applied, delete its entry from `scripts/ci/anon-exposure-functions.json` — it is the last remaining `grandfathered` row, and the sweep drops from 1 warning to 0.
### CAC measured metrics — one guarded read for the whole grid (2026-07-30)
- `supabase/migrations/20260730110000_cac_measured_metrics_rpc.sql` — **APPLIED to prod 2026-07-30 ~08:40 UTC with explicit Director approval at the session gate** ("Ready PR + apply the read-only RPC to prod DB"). Read-only: creates one function, no table, no data written. Re-running is a no-op (`CREATE OR REPLACE`).
- `fn_cac_measured_metrics()` returns `(institution_id, metric_key, value_numeric, value_label, detail)` for the ELEVEN of the CEO's 48 CAC metrics that have real per-institution substrate. Live result: **53 rows across 14 institutions**. The other 37 metrics are absent from the response deliberately — the TS catalog (`app/(routes)/accreditation/cac/_lib/cac-metric-catalog.ts`) records why each has no number, and the page renders "not captured yet", never 0.
- **Takes NO arguments, by design.** Identity and permission are derived internally; there is no parameter to forge. This is the direct lesson of the five anon leaks closed 2026-07-28/30, one of which (`fn_hostel_unallocated_candidates`) served 49 learners' names, emails, gender, programme and year to an unauthenticated caller because it trusted a caller-supplied id.
- Guard: `COALESCE(is_super_admin(), false) OR COALESCE(user_has_permission('accreditation.cac.view'), false)` — both COALESCEd, because a SECDEF predicate returning NULL falls through and GRANTS. Raises `42501` otherwise. Lock: `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` (**both** — revoking only `anon` is a silent no-op since `anon` inherits PUBLIC's `=X/postgres`), `GRANT ... TO authenticated`. `SET search_path = public`, `STABLE`.
- Proven on prod over HTTPS: anon → **401 `42501`**; authenticated without the permission (learner, Senior Learner) → **403 `42501`**; super admin → **200, 53 rows**. Anon sweep after the change unchanged: 4 relations / 64 functions / 0 unapproved / 0 escalated.
- **Attendance is a 30-DAY WINDOW, and the label says so.** `student_attendance.attendance_data` is JSONB keyed by period holding a `students` array, so an all-history rate must unnest ~1.1M elements: measured on prod at **15.7s warm / 29.1s cold** against the `authenticated` role's **8s** `statement_timeout` — it would time out on every page load. The 30-day window runs in 3.8s. All-history figures (real, and worth a nightly snapshot later, mirroring `coe_naac_evidence`): ENGG 71.15 · ALHD 77.60 · ASSF 77.72 · PHAR 79.71 · ASAI 82.78 · NURS 87.28 · DENT 87.73, both schools >92.
- Pass percentage reads `coe_naac_evidence`, whose mirror IS live (`ai_routine_schedules` row `coe-result-naac-snapshots` last fired 2026-07-29 23:15Z, `HTTP 200 · count 8`, which also proves `COE_SUPABASE_*` are set in the deployed env). Its 8 rows are 4 sessions × **one campus counted twice** — COE institution `CAS` fans out to both Arts and Science entries with identical numbers — so the RPC carries `shared_campus_note` from the row's own `fan_out` field and the page must not read it as two independent measurements.
- 🪤 **NAMING TRAP — do not "correct" this join.** Sports and cultural registrations join **`events_registrations`** (plural-plural, FK → `events`). The near-identically named **`event_registrations`** is a DIFFERENT module's table: its `event_id` is FK-constrained to **`startup_events`**, so joining it to `events` matches nothing. Verified on prod 2026-07-30: all 2,361 of its rows are orphans against `events` — zero matches, zero null event_ids. The wrong join was shipped here first and did NOT zero the displayed figure (the event count is `count(DISTINCT ev.id)` across a LEFT JOIN, so it stayed correct at 20) — it zeroed the registrations half of the tooltip, which read "20 events · 0 registrations" when the truth was 1,594, almost all of them a single marathon. It is recorded here as well as in the migration because this index is the mandatory first stop before any SQL work, so it is the likeliest place a future editor will look.
- **No `'CAC'` row is seeded into `sh_accreditation_metrics` and `BodyCode` is untouched**, deliberately: the 48-metric catalog is fixed CEO content, and filing it there would drag in weights, ceilings and a total — exactly what the Director's "measured, no grade" decision rejects.

### PDE — unblock clinical-case access for enrolled learners + clean up on submission delete (2026-08-08)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808100000_vac_lessons_enrolled_learner_select.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Adds a SECOND permissive SELECT policy `vac_lessons_select_enrolled_learner` on `vac_lessons` so a learner enrolled in the lesson's course can read it; the existing `vac_lessons_select` is left byte-for-byte untouched (permissive policies combine with OR, so this can only widen read access, never narrow it, and cannot revert an unseen live tightening). Measured on prod 2026-07-27: course `128a9d24-1091-4bc8-ab24-0c77380fcb74` had 545 enrolled learners and exactly ONE `user_institution_access` row, so 544 got the missing-scenario notice while the preview route looked healthy because `super_admin` short-circuits every gate. Deliberately NO `is_published` gate — `app/api/pde/cases/route.ts` hardcodes `is_published: false` and nothing in the codebase ever flips it, so gating on it would leave the defect 100% unfixed. No 42P17 recursion: traced `vac_enrollments_select` → `vac_courses_select` → `user_institution_access`/`profiles`, no path returns to `vac_lessons`. **Enrolment alone is deliberately NOT the gate** — `vac_enrollments_insert` is `WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid() OR super_admin)` and places no constraint on `course_id`, so any authenticated caller can forge an enrolment for any course on the platform; a bare enrolment read door would have been a cross-tenant read escalation. The policy therefore calls new SECURITY DEFINER helper `fn_vac_learner_may_read_lesson(uuid)` (anon/PUBLIC revoked, `authenticated` granted) which requires enrolment **AND** `vac_courses.institution_id = profiles.institution_id` — the `profiles.institution_id` check the broken policy was missing. SECURITY DEFINER is required because inlining the institution join would re-evaluate `vac_courses_select`, which itself demands the `user_institution_access` row these 544 learners lack. Residual by design: within one institution a learner could still forge an enrolment into another of their own college's courses — no more than institution-scoped team members already get; the root fix is constraining `course_id` in `vac_enrollments_insert`, flagged separately. Policy is `TO authenticated` — **required, not stylistic**: with no `TO` clause it applies to PUBLIC, so `anon` would evaluate the USING clause and, having just had EXECUTE revoked, every unauthenticated `SELECT` on `vac_lessons` would raise `permission denied for function` instead of returning zero rows (reproduced locally before fixing).
- `supabase/migrations/20260808100100_pde_submission_delete_cleanup.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Two different mechanisms because the two dependent tables differ in cardinality: `pde_engagement_events` gets a genuine `source_submission_id` FK with ON DELETE CASCADE (backfilled from `metadata->>'submission_id'`, kept current by a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger that only links to an existing attempt, so no route has to change and the FK can never reject a write that succeeds today); `pde_learner_capabilities` gets an AFTER DELETE RECOMPUTE instead, because it is a `UNIQUE(learner_id, capability_id)` best-score-wins aggregate spanning many attempts and a cascade would destroy a record other surviving attempts legitimately earned. Recompute also catches the ordering a pointer-keyed cascade misses (attempt 1 = 80%, attempt 2 = 50%: deleting attempt 1 must drop the score even though the evidence pointer names attempt 2). Never blocks a delete — the body is wrapped in an exception handler that raises a WARNING and lets the DELETE stand (conscious trade: a failed recompute leaves the stale row and reports only to the Postgres log, because making an attempt undeletable is strictly worse). Recompute takes a `FOR UPDATE` lock on the capability row first, so two concurrent deletes for the same learner serialise instead of each writing a best score that points at the other's already-deleted attempt. The engagement-event link is re-derived on every write rather than only when NULL, so an UPDATE that repoints `metadata->>'submission_id'` moves the FK with it instead of leaving a stale link that would cascade away an event naming a different submission. `source_submission_id` is strictly DERIVED — one unconditional assignment on both INSERT and UPDATE, so after the trigger it is always exactly what `metadata->>'submission_id'` resolves to and nothing else. Weaker forms leaked: setting it only when NULL left a stale link after a repoint, and clearing it only when metadata *changed* let a caller forge the FK directly alongside unsupporting metadata and have it CASCADE-delete the event when the wrong attempt was removed. Because the value is only ever a just-confirmed-existing submission id, the FK can never reject a write that succeeds today on any non-route path. The link trigger is **SECURITY DEFINER scoped to `s.learner_id = NEW.learner_id`**, because it asks whether the submission EXISTS rather than whether the writer can SEE it — the learner predicate is what makes definer rights safe, since an unscoped existence lookup would be a cross-tenant existence oracle and would let a foreign tenant's delete cascade away this event. It is not enough to ask only about visibility — under caller RLS any writer other than the owning learner (`pde_sub_own_read` is what makes the route path work) would fail to link, and that event would escape the cascade cleanup entirely. Because the trigger fires for every `pde_submissions` delete (no skip condition can narrow it without also being able to skip a needed recompute), the write is **no-op-guarded**: if the recomputed score, status, pointer, attempt number and `demonstrated_at`-consistency already match what is stored (compared with `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`, so a NULL cannot collapse the predicate), nothing is written, so an unrelated MCQ delete cannot churn the row or stamp `recomputed_after_deleted_submission` with an irrelevant attempt id. Evidence is **merged** (`existing || jsonb_build_object(...)`) rather than rebuilt, so keys the scoring route writes that this trigger does not know about are not silently dropped on the first delete-triggered recompute. The recompute is additionally **provenance-gated**: it only touches a capability row whose `demonstration_evidence` carries a `submission_id`, so a capability awarded by import or by hand is never destroyed — and the "was it a clinical case / does the pointer name the deleted attempt" skip conditions were removed, because each could skip a needed recompute (the first when the attempt's assessment row is already gone, the second in the reverse-ordering case) and the latter compared a uuid as raw text. The backfill shape-guards then casts to `uuid` (rather than comparing to `s.id::text`) so it normalises exactly as the trigger does; a pre-existing event holding an upper-case uuid would otherwise never link and never be cascade-cleaned — precisely the orphan this migration removes. Threshold mirrors `clinical_reasoning.scoring.passing_threshold_pct` read from `platform_policies` directly rather than through `fn_get_policy_clinical_reasoning`, so a missing function can never raise inside the trigger and make an attempt undeletable.
- `supabase/migrations/20260808100200_pde_question_option_ids.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** `fn_pde_normalize_question_option_ids` plus a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE OF options trigger and an idempotent backfill, guaranteeing every object element of `pde_assessment_questions.options` carries a non-empty `id`. A missing id broke the learner path twice: it permanently disabled the submit control (`MCQWarmupQuestion.tsx` matches on `selectedId === o.id`, which never becomes truthy) and it made the `fn_pde_mark_objective` answer-key fallback return NULL, so every answer graded wrong. Reserves ids already present BEFORE generating any (so the three rows repaired by hand on 2026-07-27 are neither renumbered nor disturbed, and a generated id can never collide), and never reads or writes option `text`, `feedback` or `is_correct`. A **duplicate** id counts as a gap too, not as "already fine" — two options sharing `opt1` break the learner path exactly as a missing id does (`selectedId === o.id` matches both and the `LIMIT 1` answer-key fallback can resolve to the wrong one); the first occurrence keeps the id and each later collision is reassigned, and the backfill predicate selects rows in either broken shape. A normaliser rather than a CHECK constraint on purpose: a constraint would turn a silent defect into a hard AI/PMS import failure.
### Learner risk + contribution engines — attendance key, dead catalog, unreachable tiers (2026-07-30)
- `supabase/migrations/20260730160000_fix_mv_learner_attendance_summary_key_and_grain.sql` — **ALREADY APPLIED to prod 2026-07-30; this file is the repo record of live state, not a pending change.** Rebuilds `mv_learner_attendance_summary`, which had TWO independent defects. (1) It extracted `student_elem.value->>'id'`, but `student_attendance.attendance_data` identifies the learner under `student_id`. Of 297,605 array elements in the trailing 30 days, **ZERO** carried an `id` key, so the NOT NULL filter discarded 100% of format-1 rows and the view sat at **16 rows against 10,431 source rows**. Fixed with `COALESCE(value->>'student_id', value->>'id')` plus a uuid regex guard (which also stops a malformed value aborting the entire refresh at the `::uuid` cast). (2) `idx_mlas_learner` is `UNIQUE(learner_id)` — it must be, since `REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY` requires a unique index — but the view grouped by `(learner_id, institution_id, section_id)`. Fixing (1) alone yields 5,026 rows for 3,527 learners (**749 learners sit in more than one section = 1,499 unique violations**), so every future REFRESH would have aborted. The grain is now **ONE ROW PER LEARNER**; `institution_id`/`section_id` come from the most recent record via `(array_agg(... ORDER BY attendance_date DESC))[1]` — `array_agg` and not `max()` because **uuid has no `max()` aggregate**. Verified safe first: 0 learners span more than one institution. Result **16 → 3,527 rows**. 🔴 **Also carries two REVOKEs that are NOT yet live — applying this file DOES change production privileges.** Recreating the view re-triggered Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO anon`, and on 2026-07-30 an unauthenticated caller holding the public anon key got **HTTP 200 / `content-range: 0-0/3527`** from `GET /rest/v1/mv_learner_attendance_summary` — every learner's attendance percentage, delta, last-absent date, section and institution. `authenticated` is revoked as well: a materialized view is `relkind='m'` and **cannot carry an RLS policy**, so granting it to `authenticated` is necessarily cross-tenant. Neither grant is needed — no reader exists anywhere in `jicate/main` outside migrations and generated types, no `pg_cron` job touches it, and the one function that reads it is SECURITY DEFINER and reaches it as owner regardless. `service_role` is kept.
- `supabase/migrations/20260730160100_fix_compute_learner_risk_assessment_catalog_and_renormalise.sql` — **ALREADY APPLIED to prod 2026-07-30.** Body is byte-for-byte the deployed body (verified against `pg_get_functiondef`) minus two stray scaffolding comments. Two defects. (1) The source-catalog probe read `information_schema.materialized_views`, **which does not exist in PostgreSQL** — materialized views are not in the SQL standard, so the information_schema never describes them (`pg_matviews` does). Every call raised **42P01 before scoring a single learner**, so the function had **NEVER once executed successfully since 2026-05-25** and `learner_risk_assessments` held 0 rows for two months. (2) `platform_policies` `learner_risk.weights` spreads 100 points over 7 dimensions, but 4 had no data source and always contributed 0 — while the composite still divided by a **fixed literal 100**. Ceiling was therefore **55** against thresholds high=60 / critical=80: **both tiers were mathematically unreachable**, and the highest score ever observed was 54. Fixed with a `v_w_applied` accumulator summing only earnable weight and dividing by `GREATEST(v_w_applied, 1)`, plus **EXECUTE-guarded emptiness probes** that also downgrade a source which exists but holds zero rows (EXECUTE deliberately — a static reference would create a compile-time dependency on tables this function is written to tolerate the absence of). Proven locally on a stub database: a learner at 0% attendance scored **25 → `low` under the old divisor, 100 → `critical` under the new one**, same inputs. Live result: **59 critical + 403 high** now surface out of 4,342 assessed. 🔴 **One delta from live: `authenticated` is REVOKEd on the function.** It opens by DELETEing every row for the target date then loops all 4,342 learners, so an EXECUTE grant to every logged-in user is both a data-destruction primitive and a trivial DoS; nothing calls it (no caller in `jicate/main`, no `pg_cron` job) and a server-side operator is `service_role`. The explicit REVOKE is **required** — `CREATE OR REPLACE` preserves an existing ACL, so merely omitting `authenticated` from the GRANT would leave the live grant untouched (verified both ways on PostgreSQL 16). ⚠️ Known follow-up, deliberately NOT changed here: two `recommended_actions` strings still read "student" rather than "learner" — that is deployed user-facing copy and correcting it is a behaviour change belonging in its own PR.
- `supabase/migrations/20260730160200_learner_contribution_scores_engine.sql` — **ALREADY APPLIED to prod 2026-07-30.** New `learner_contribution_scores` table (FK → `learners_profiles` ON DELETE CASCADE, `UNIQUE(learner_id, assessment_date)`, `idx_lcs_learner`, `idx_lcs_inst_sc(institution_id, contribution_score DESC)`), RLS on with **exactly two** policies — `lcs_service_all` (service_role ALL) and `lcs_admin_select` (SELECT to authenticated) — plus `REVOKE ALL ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` and the SECDEF `compute_learner_contribution_score(date)` with `REVOKE EXECUTE FROM anon, PUBLIC, authenticated` / `GRANT TO service_role` (same no-caller reasoning as the risk engine). Seeds set `is_active = true` explicitly rather than leaning on the column default, because the function reads its thresholds `WHERE ... AND is_active` — if that default ever changes, the calibrated ladder goes invisible and the function silently falls back to the broken in-code 15/35/60/80 tiers. **Every guard in `lcs_admin_select` is COALESCE-wrapped and that is load-bearing**: a SECDEF helper returning NULL makes `NULL OR false` evaluate to NULL, which denies inside a USING clause but **falls through and GRANTS** inside an `IF NOT (...)` guard — the exact asymmetry behind the anon write hole closed the same day in `fn_update_recruitment_step_comment`. 🪤 **The policy also carries `AND institution_id IS NOT NULL`, which is NOT redundant with the COALESCE — do not remove it.** Measured on prod 2026-07-30, `role_has_institution_access(NULL)` returns **TRUE** (it reads a NULL institution as a system-wide record), so on a NULL-institution row the COALESCE is wrapping a genuine TRUE and never fires — any authenticated user in any college holding `learners.contribution.view` could read that row across the tenant boundary. `institution_id` is nullable because the RPC copies it from nullable `learners_profiles.institution_id`. Reproduced and closed A/B on PostgreSQL 16: 1 row readable without the clause, 0 with it. Latent today (0 of 4,342 active learners have a NULL institution), which is precisely why it was cheap to close. 🪤 **`is_admin()` is deliberately ABSENT from this policy — do not "restore" it to match the 1,276 policies that still carry it.** It is a global role-name check with no institution scoping, so as a standalone `OR` branch it lets any profile whose legacy role is `admin`/`administrator`/`super_admin` read every institution's rows. This repo has ruled that exact shape a multi-tenant leak **twice** and removed it in prod (`20260703160000_close_admission_pii_is_admin_leak.sql`, `20260731000000_fix_student_attendance_rls_is_admin_leak.sql`); measured 2026-07-30, **3 accounts** (1 `admin`, 2 `administrator`) carry `is_super_admin = false` and would have read all 4,342 learners across all 14 institutions through it. A/B proven: 1 foreign-institution row readable with the branch, 0 without. Admin-only by design; the learners it ranks never see it. 🪤 **Thresholds are 5/18/30/40, not the round 15/35/60/80 — do not "tidy" them.** No learner registers activity in more than 3 of the 5 dimensions, so the round ladder left the top tiers unreachable — the same defect the sibling migration fixes for risk. They are percentile-calibrated to the measured 2026-07-30 distribution (p50=4 / p75=18 / p90=30 / p95=37 / p99=50) and live in `platform_policies`, so recalibration is a config edit, not a deploy. Note the intentional asymmetry inside `v_w_applied`: a source empty **platform-wide** cannot be measured and leaves the denominator, but a learner merely absent from a **populated** source scored a genuine zero and stays in it — that is participation data, not missing data. 🪤 Seeds use `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS`, **never `ON CONFLICT (policy_key)`**: `platform_policies` has no unique constraint on `policy_key` alone — its unique index is `uq_platform_policies_key_scope` on `(policy_key, scope_type, COALESCE(scope_id, '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'::uuid))` — so `ON CONFLICT (policy_key)` fails outright with **42P10**. `WHERE NOT EXISTS` also avoids clobbering a value the Director has since retuned. Distribution across 4,342 learners: minimal 2,385 · emerging 759 · steady 627 · strong 414 · exceptional 157.
- ⛔ **Do NOT reconcile any of the three against `supabase/migrations/20260525200000_learner_risk_intelligence_substrate.sql`.** That file has drifted from production and is wrong in every place these three touch — it additionally declares `platform_policies` with a `policy_value` column production does not have (production uses `value` + `scope_type` + `is_active`). Read live state with `pg_get_functiondef` / `pg_matviews` instead.

### Learner 360 — plain-language standing verdict from the two live scoring engines (2026-08-08)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808110003_learner_360_verdict.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** *(Renamed from `20260808110000_…` on 2026-08-01 — that version was shared by four files; see the version-collision entry at the end of this file.)* Adds `learner_360_verdicts` (band, 2-3 sentence developmental narrative, next_actions, faculty_override) + `learner_360_verdicts_admin` (contribution_summary, value_rank_note), the `learner.360_verdict` Max-lane job type, an `ai_routine_schedules` row, and two SECDEF RPCs. **TWO tables, not one column set — this is the load-bearing decision:** Postgres RLS is ROW-level and no policy can return a row with some columns blanked, so keeping the comparative ranking language in the shared table would let any team member holding `learners.standing.view` `select *` and read where their learners rank. The admin half therefore lives behind its own table, its own policy and its own permission key (`learners.standing.admin_note.view`); the shared half gets `learners.standing.view` and a learner-self policy keyed on `profiles.learner_id -> learners_profiles.id`. Both keys are registered in `lib/constants/permissions.ts`, so they are grantable in Role Management and — being ungranted at apply time — the loop **fails closed**: nothing is visible to anyone but service_role and platform admins until the Director grants them. Deliberately **NO UPDATE policy** on either table: a correction goes through `fn_learner_360_set_override`, which touches only `faculty_override`/`overridden_by`/`overridden_at`, because an UPDATE policy cannot be restricted to a column subset and would let a corrector rewrite `standing_narrative` itself. `fn_learner_360_record_verdict` is revoked from **anon, authenticated AND PUBLIC** and granted to `service_role` alone — it bypasses RLS and authors text a learner reads about themselves, so an `authenticated` grant would let any signed-in user of any tenant write a standing verdict for any learner on the platform; `fn_learner_360_set_override` is revoked from anon+PUBLIC (both — revoking anon alone is a silent no-op while anon inherits PUBLIC's default EXECUTE) and gated in-body with every predicate `COALESCE(..., false)` wrapped. Inputs verified live on prod 2026-07-30 and **created by nothing here**: `learner_risk_assessments` 4,342 rows (59 critical · 403 high · 746 moderate · 979 low · 2,155 healthy), `learner_contribution_scores` 4,342, `mv_learner_attendance_summary` 3,527. 🔒 **HARD DATA BOUNDARY, stated in three places** (this file, the migration header, `lib/services/learner-360/verdict-prompt.ts`, and the job type's `description` row): the loop must never read or join `session_feedback` (125,571 rows), `event_session_feedback` (10,333), `carre_micro_impressions` (1,437) or `scf_learner_notes` (2,147), nor any `health_*`/medical table. All four carry a learner id and so look like free signal, but they hold feedback the learner **gave** under an explicit anonymity promise — aggregated-and-anonymous UI copy, a `fully_anonymous` policy mode that strips `author_id`, k>=3 suppression — and scoring the author would convert every candid rating into a personal record. 🪤 Scheduling trap: this is fired by the **AI-routine dispatcher** via an `ai_routine_schedules` row, NOT a `vercel.json` cron — `vercel.json` on `jicate/main` already holds **exactly 100** crons, the plan's hard ceiling, so a 101st entry would fail the deploy for every change in the repo, not just this one.
### Learner risk → department-head notifications: dedupe ledger + policy knobs + dispatcher slot (2026-07-30)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808110002_learner_risk_staff_notifications.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** The risk engine's first successful run was 2026-07-30, writing 4,342 `learner_risk_assessments` rows for that date (59 `critical`, 403 `high`, 462 in scope across 17 departments). It only WRITES rows; it notified nobody. Director approved notifying TEAM MEMBERS that day. This migration adds three things and **no RPC** — all selection, scoping and fan-out run in `app/api/cron/learner-risk-notifications/route.ts` under the service-role client, so there is no new EXECUTE surface to lock. The new table still carries an explicit `REVOKE ALL ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` because Supabase's default `GRANT ALL ON TABLES TO anon` would otherwise hand `anon` a direct grant independent of PUBLIC.
- **The dedupe signal the spec names does not exist in this database.** `previous_risk_score` and `trend_direction` are NULL on all 4,342 rows — the table's total row count equals that single date's count, so only one day of assessments has ever been written. A dedupe trusting those columns would classify everyone as "no trend" on day one and keep doing so forever, because the engine recomputes the same standing daily and nothing in the assessment row records that a human was already told. Notification state therefore lives in the new `learner_risk_notification_log`, keyed `UNIQUE(learner_id, notified_on)`: the route announces a learner only on a CHANGE against their latest ledger row — `new` (first entry into high/critical), `escalated` (high → critical), or `worsening` (same tier, score up by at least `min_score_delta`). An unchanged standing is never re-announced and an improving learner is never announced at all. The engine's own columns are still read, still shown as evidence, and a `worsening` trend is honoured as an additional trigger **only alongside a real score rise**, so a stale label cannot re-fire a flat score daily.
- 🪤 **RECIPIENT TRAP — do not resolve the department head through `departments.head_of_department_id`.** That is the pointer the HR appraisal routing uses (`20260507000001_departments_add_hod.sql`), and it is the obvious choice. Measured on prod 2026-07-30 it is set on **7 of 89** departments and on **ZERO of the 17** departments that actually have at-risk learners — resolving through it alone would build a valid message, insert cleanly, return success, and reach nobody. The populated roster is `profiles.role='hod'` + `department_id`, which covers **17/17** and yields 50 distinct recipients. The route unions both sources and scopes them to match the SELECT policy already on `learner_risk_assessments`, so a recipient can always open the record they were told about.
- 🪤 **`platform_policies` does not have the shape the risk substrate file declares.** `20260525200000_learner_risk_intelligence_substrate.sql` creates it with `policy_value`/`module`; the LIVE table has `value`, `scope_type`, `data_type`, `enum_options`, `publication_state` and no such columns — that file's version never reached this database. Seeds here use the live shape. The unique index is `uq_platform_policies_key_scope`, an EXPRESSION index over `(policy_key, scope_type, COALESCE(scope_id, <zero uuid>))`, so `ON CONFLICT` must repeat that expression verbatim; `ON CONFLICT (policy_key)` raises 42P10 and fails the migration. `ai_routine_schedules.days_of_week` is `smallint[]`, so the array literal is cast rather than left as `integer[]`.
- **Registered on the dispatcher, deliberately NOT in `vercel.json`.** That file's `crons` array is already at **100** entries, the plan cap; a 101st would fail the BUILD and block every deploy, not just this feature. The routine is an `ai_routine_schedules` row (`learner-risk-staff-notifications`, daily 17:20 IST — the engine's only observed run finished 10:57Z / 16:27 IST in one batch) plus a registry entry in `lib/ai-routines/misc-ai.ts`, so its day and time are editable in `/admin/ai-routines` without a redeploy.
- **Flood control, because this bell has no duplicate-folding and has previously grown to five figures of never-expiring rows.** Default mode is `digest` — ONE grouped message per department, not one per learner (462 on day one). Every notification row created carries an explicit `expires_at` (default 72h), which the read path honours via `liveNotificationOrFilter()`. The `idempotency_key` is per-department-per-day so two dispatcher ticks in one slot cannot double-send, and `metadata.event` gives the bell's near-duplicate collapsing a stable identity. `include_department_staff` is off by default: it adds 203 recipients across the affected departments.
- **Fails closed.** If `learner_risk_notification_log` is absent — which it is until this migration is applied — the route returns 503 and sends nothing, rather than re-announcing all 462 learners on every run.
- ⚠️ **Pre-existing engine defect found while building this, NOT fixed here (out of scope).** `compute_learner_risk_assessment`'s fee dimension filters `status IN ('unpaid','partial')`. The value `'partial'` does not exist in this database — the live statuses are `paid` (3,377), `partially_paid` (1,048), `unpaid` (496), `superseded` (59), `cancelled` (20) in a 5,000-row sample. The engine therefore counts only fully-unpaid bills and silently misses every partially-paid arrear, understating the fees dimension for ~1,048 bills. The notification route deliberately reports the ACCURATE count using `('unpaid','partially_paid')`, because mirroring the engine's undercount would print "0 overdue" beside a fee-arrears risk factor in the same message.
- **Delivery proven, not assumed** (an insert into `notifications` can return success and reach nobody — `targeting` contents are unvalidated and the bell actually reads `user_notifications`). Verified on prod 2026-07-30: a real digest built from real Pharmacy (UG) data was sent to ONE test account and then read back **as that account**, through the bell's real `!inner` join with the `expires_at` filter applied — it came back UNREAD with a live expiry, alongside neighbouring rows whose `expires_at` is null. A second run returned `skipped: "idempotent"`, exercising the duplicate guard.
### Health / sports achievements — a verified certificate was readable by everyone signed in (2026-08-08)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808105500_health_sports_certificate_visibility.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Closes a live cross-institution exposure on learner certificate scans and implements Director decision **D7 (2026-07-30)**: a certificate is visible to the learner who owns it, team members of THAT learner's own college, the IQAC/accreditation side, and the `is_super_admin()`/`is_admin()` bypass — **not** every authenticated user, and **not** a fellow learner of the same college. Two independent doors were open, and closing only one would have fixed nothing. (1) `health_sports_achievements_public` was `FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (verified = true)` — no institution predicate, no role predicate — so the instant IQAC ticked a row, any signed-in caller (including via the anon key that ships in every Next.js bundle) could read it. (2) `storage.objects` policy `cdc_docs_read` was merely `bucket_id = 'cdc-docs' AND auth.uid() IS NOT NULL`, and SELECT on `storage.objects` is what powers bucket **listing** — so a caller could enumerate every certificate path and read it **without touching the table at all**. The rule is written once as SECURITY DEFINER `fn_can_view_learner_achievement(uuid)` (anon/PUBLIC revoked, `authenticated` granted) rather than inlined, because it needs the LEARNER's `institution_id` from `learners_profiles`, which carries its own RLS: inlined, the subquery runs as the viewer, returns nothing for a team member who cannot read that learner, and the predicate collapses to deny for exactly the people D7 admits. **The function takes the row's `learner_id`, never a caller id** — identity comes from `auth.uid()` only, so there is no caller-supplied identity to forge (the shape behind the 2026-07-28 SECDEF IDOR sweep). Every guard is `COALESCE(..., false)`: a SECDEF predicate returning NULL falls through and GRANTS. Serving-team-member-ness is membership of `public.staff`, **not** `profiles.learner_id IS NULL` — that set also holds parents and service accounts (1,196 of 7,225 profiles carry no learner, against 856 rows in the serving-team relation) — AND `role_has_institution_access()`, so a deliberate cross-institution grant keeps behaving as it does platform-wide. `verified = true` is deliberately **kept**: an unverified entry is a claim, not evidence, and its owner still reads it through the untouched `_self` policy; this narrows who may read a verified row and widens nothing. The `cdc_docs_read` change is a single added conjunct carving out `sports-achievement-certificates/%` — verified on prod 2026-07-30, `cdc-docs` holds 14 objects across bulletin-attachments / company-logos / exports / internship-offer-letters / mentor-photos / offer-letters and **zero** under that prefix, so no existing CDC read changes behaviour. **No replacement grant policy is added, on purpose**: with the prefix carved out the only door is the server action, which mints a **5-minute** signed URL with the service-role client after re-checking D7. Paired app change: `certificate_url` now stores the storage **PATH**, never a signed URL — the previous one-year signed URL was both the leak (a signed URL is a bearer token, redeemable by anyone holding the string, signed in or not) and a durability bug (evidence for NAAC's five-year cycles that died at +365 days). Proven live inside `BEGIN..ROLLBACK` on prod against real identities, with residue re-read in a **separate** call (function absent, both policies byte-identical to before, 1 table row, 0 mappings, 14 cdc-docs objects): **BEFORE** — owning learner 1, other-college learner **1**, same-college learner **1**, same-college HOD 1, IQAC holder 1, and an other-college learner could list the certificate object (1 of 15). **AFTER** — owning learner 1, other-college learner **0**, same-college learner **0**, same-college HOD 1, IQAC holder 1, certificate object unlistable by anyone (0), rest of `cdc-docs` still readable (14). Nothing has leaked to date: the table holds 1 row, 0 verified, 0 with a certificate — this closes the door before the feature is used, not after. **Round 3 adds the write door (section 4):** the certificate UPLOAD had the mirror-image defect — the server action authenticated the caller and then wrote with the service-role client, deliberately bypassing `cdc_docs_write` (`WITH CHECK (bucket_id = 'cdc-docs' AND is_cdc_staff())`, which refuses a learner session), so all 7,225 authenticated profiles could write into the bucket. New SECURITY DEFINER `fn_may_attach_learner_certificate(text)` (anon/PUBLIC revoked, `authenticated` granted) takes the **path segment naming the learner's folder**, never a caller id, casts it defensively inside the function so a malformed object name DENIES instead of raising `22P02` out of a policy expression, and admits the owning learner, `accreditation.certificates.manage`, or the admin bypass — deliberately not the `.view` read key, because attaching evidence is a write. New policy `cdc_docs_write_sports_certificate` (`FOR INSERT TO authenticated`) requires `name LIKE 'sports-achievement-certificates/%/%/%'` and checks that helper against `split_part(name, '/', 2)`, so a learner session can write exactly one place — its own learner folder, inside the prefix section 3 just carved out of the blanket read. `cdc_docs_write` is left byte-for-byte untouched; permissive policies combine with OR, so this widens only that prefix. The paired app change gates the action itself (owner / IQAC / admin, on the cookie-bound session client) and now **tries the session client first, falling back to service-role only when storage refuses** — so applying this migration retires the privileged path instead of merely tolerating it.
- `supabase/migrations/20260808110100_health_sports_achievement_self_verify_lockdown.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Closes self-verification and certificate swapping on `public.health_sports_achievements`, enforcing Director decision **D4** (only the accreditation / IQAC side may tick `verified`, permission `accreditation.certificates.manage`). Measured on prod 2026-07-31: `health_sports_achievements_self` was `cmd = ALL` over the learner's own rows, and UPDATE on the **`verified` and `verified_by` columns** was granted to `anon`, `authenticated`, `postgres`, `service_role`. PostgreSQL RLS is **ROW-scoped, never COLUMN-scoped**, so "edit your own row" silently reads "verify your own row" — proven live as the owning learner (DB role `authenticated`, `request.jwt.claims.sub` set, the exact shape PostgREST uses): `SET verified = true` on their own row **updated 1 row and read back true**, and `SET certificate_url = '…/FORGED/x.pdf'` **updated 1 row**. Hiding the tick in the UI never achieved D4; the API is the boundary and the anon key ships in every Next.js bundle. **RLS cannot be the fix here** — a policy predicate cannot see OLD, so no `USING`/`WITH CHECK` can express "`verified` did not change"; the privilege system can, so column-level UPDATE carries the rule. 🪤 **ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, not stylistic:** a table-level UPDATE grant covers every column and a later column-level GRANT carves **nothing** back out of it, so `REVOKE UPDATE ON TABLE … FROM authenticated` must come FIRST or the whole migration is a no-op that reads as a fix (the same trap that made a first attempt on sibling PR #2651 look green while the probe was still being stopped by a trigger). The `FOR ALL` policy is split four ways — `_self_select` / `_self_insert` / `_self_update` / `_self_delete` — with the row predicate carried over **byte-for-byte** (its known `OR (p.id = auth.uid())` join oddity is filed as a follow-up, deliberately not restructured inside a security migration; re-measured today it is bounded to **1** visible learner record, not 7,156). `_self_insert` newly pins a row to being **born unverified** (`COALESCE(verified,false) = false AND verified_by IS NULL`) — the old `FOR ALL` carried no `WITH CHECK`, so Postgres reused its `USING` clause and constrained nothing about verification state; enforced in `WITH CHECK` rather than INSERT column grants because those would have to enumerate every insertable column and missing one silently breaks the entry form. DELETE is **preserved unchanged** on purpose (`HealthSportsService.deleteAchievement` exists, `trg_hsa_evidence_cleanup` is built for it, and a re-filed row is born unverified anyway). `REVOKE ALL … FROM anon, PUBLIC` — honestly, an `anon` UPDATE already affects 0 rows because no policy names `anon`, so `anon` is stopped by RLS **today, not by privileges**; the revoke removes exactly that accident, because the day someone writes a policy `TO public` (as `cdc_docs_read` already is, one table over) the standing default grant becomes live `anon` write access with no migration touching this table. `TRUNCATE` is revoked from `authenticated` in the same breath and called out rather than folded in quietly: **TRUNCATE bypasses RLS entirely**, so the standing default let any signed-in caller erase every achievement in one statement — strictly worse than the tampering this file was opened to stop. **Tamper-evidence** is new trigger `trg_hsa_unverify_on_certificate_change` (BEFORE UPDATE OF `certificate_url`) + `fn_hsa_unverify_on_certificate_change()` — deliberately **NOT** SECURITY DEFINER (it reads nothing and only writes NEW; EXECUTE revoked from `anon`, `PUBLIC` anyway, which costs nothing since PostgreSQL checks EXECUTE on a trigger function at CREATE TRIGGER time, never at fire time — proven by the probe). It is **unconditional**: whoever the caller and whatever the client, changing the certificate on a verified row withdraws the tick, because a tick means "a reviewer looked at THIS document" and cannot outlive the document. Unverify rather than refuse **at this layer** because refusing would need to tell callers apart, which column privileges at this level cannot do; the learner-facing REFUSAL lives in the paired server action where the caller IS known. The existing AFTER trigger `trg_hsa_evidence_fanout` then withdraws the NAAC 8.3 mapping unprompted, since BEFORE runs first. ⚠️ **Deliberate narrowing, stated plainly:** column privileges attach to a DB role and every signed-in person shares `authenticated`, so no column grant admits the IQAC officer while refusing the learner — after this file NO user session may write `verified`, and the only writer left is `service_role`, i.e. the gated action `_actions/verify-achievement.ts`. Nothing in the repo writes `verified` through a user session, so this costs no working path and buys one auditable door. Proven live inside `BEGIN..ROLLBACK` on prod against real identities (owning learner `anushyascse2023@jkkn.ac.in`; IQAC holder Narayan Rao `coo@jkkn.ac.in`, whose `accreditation.certificates.manage` was confirmed **by value** = true via the `accreditation_officer` role, not by key existence), with residue re-read in a **separate call** (function absent, trigger absent, both original policies present and the `_self` qual byte-identical, `authenticated`/`anon` privileges all restored, 1 row with its original `event_name`, `verified = false`, `certificate_url` null): **BEFORE** — learner self-verify 1 row / reads back true, learner certificate swap 1 row. **AFTER** — learner `verified` **42501**, learner `verified_by` **42501**, learner certificate swap **42501**, learner descriptive edit **1 row (still works)**, learner INSERT `verified = true` **refused by RLS**, learner INSERT `verified = false` **accepted**, `anon` UPDATE **42501**, `anon` SELECT **42501**, IQAC raw session **42501** (the documented narrowing), IQAC via the action's `service_role` client **1 row, verified = t, verified_by = the officer**, certificate swapped on a verified row **→ verified = f, verified_by = null**, certificate re-stated unchanged **→ verified stays t**, and the privilege surface read back: table UPDATE f · `verified` f · `verified_by` f · `certificate_url` f · `learner_id` f · `event_name` **t** · TRUNCATE f · `anon` SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE all f · `service_role` UPDATE t.
