### AI Pulse — AI-rejected prompts reach a champion, and a stalled safety check becomes visible (2026-08-05)
- `supabase/migrations/20260805100000_ai_pulse_safety_review_queue.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Rehearsed against prod inside `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`; a separate call re-confirmed all three functions still absent and build `a8d832e5` still `failed`. Adds three SECURITY DEFINER functions and **no schema change**: `fn_ai_pulse_champion_safety_queue(integer)` (the `safety_status='failed'` list), `fn_ai_pulse_release_prompt_build_safety(uuid)` (`failed` → `passed`), `fn_ai_pulse_prompt_safety_health()` (Director decision #10 — waiting/rejected/passed counts plus `max(safety_checked_at)`, the ONLY detector for the `*/10` safety cron silently stopping, because an empty feed is otherwise indistinguishable from nobody writing prompts). All three: `SET search_path = public`, `REVOKE EXECUTE FROM anon, PUBLIC` + `GRANT TO authenticated` in the same file, guard `COALESCE(is_super_admin() OR user_has_permission('aiPulse:anomaly.review'), false)` — the COALESCE is load-bearing, since `NOT (NULL OR NULL)` is NULL and the `IF` would fall through leaving the guard OPEN. The release gate is deliberately **narrower** than the two pre-existing decision RPCs, which also accept the Monday-Lab scoring key (named verbatim in the migration header): measured by value on prod (`permissions #>> '{key}' = 'true'`, not `?` which tests mere existence) that key is held by `faculty` 483 + `hod` 102 + `school_faculty` 1 = **586 team members**, versus **3** for `ai_pulse_champion`; the widening on the older two exists only as back-compatibility for holders already using them, and a brand-new action carries no such debt. Release **appends** `released_by`/`released_at` to `safety` (`||`, never overwrite) so the model's `reasons` and `appropriate:false` survive for audit — that record is the only evidence the checker is over-blocking. `AND safety_status = 'failed'` in the UPDATE makes it idempotent and refuses to resurrect a build rejected for any other cause; `IF NOT FOUND` then raises `P0002` so the UI can say so honestly. `safety->'reasons'` is unnested behind a `jsonb_typeof(...) = 'array'` guard because `jsonb_array_elements_text()` on an object RAISES, which would take the whole queue down over one malformed verdict; the author join is `LEFT`, never `INNER`, so a build whose `learners_profiles` row is missing stays reviewable rather than becoming invisible to the only person who can release it. `fn_ai_pulse_champion_report_queue` is deliberately left untouched — its lack of a safety/score/graduation filter is a known OPEN item the Director has not decided. Dry-run results: `anon=false public=false authenticated=true` on all three; queue returned build `a8d832e5` (score 78, 2 reasons); release flipped it to `passed` with both reasons intact; a second release raised `P0002`; a plain learner (`is_super_admin=false`, `aiPulse:anomaly.review=false`) got **42501** on all three, and an unauthenticated caller got `not authenticated`.
- `supabase/migrations/20260805140000_ai_pulse_cron_heartbeat.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Rehearsed against prod inside `BEGIN..ROLLBACK` (both files in filename order, since this one replaces a function the previous one creates); a separate call re-confirmed `ai_pulse_cron_runs`, `fn_ai_pulse_record_cron_run` and `fn_ai_pulse_prompt_safety_health` all still absent. Director decision #2 (2026-07-30): the stalled-check warning must watch a **runner heartbeat**, not a data timestamp. `fn_ai_pulse_prompt_safety_health()` as first shipped read `max(safety_checked_at)` over builds, which measures throughput, not liveness — the cron stamps a build only when one is *eligible* (graded, 60–79, non-graduated, non-disqualified), so a run that correctly finds nothing to do stamps nothing and looks dead. Measured on prod 2026-07-30 16:46 UTC: `prompt_safety_check_enabled = true`, last stamp 10:49 UTC = **357 minutes** stale, 10 builds waiting, **0 of them cron-eligible** — a red "the check has stopped" banner on a cron running correctly every ten minutes, with no path to ever clear it. Raising the threshold only postpones the identical false alarm. Adds `ai_pulse_cron_runs` (append-only run log: `job_key`, `ran_at`, `outcome` jsonb; RLS ON with zero policies **and** `REVOKE ALL FROM anon, authenticated, PUBLIC` + `GRANT ALL TO service_role`, because Supabase's default privileges grant anon/authenticated a direct table grant on a separate axis from RLS; index on `(job_key, ran_at DESC)`) and `fn_ai_pulse_record_cron_run(text, jsonb, uuid)`. Table shape, security posture, best-effort INSERT-then-7-day-prune body and `admin.rpc(...)` call style are copied from the LIVE `ai_routine_run_log` / `fn_ai_routine_record_fire` pair (migrations 20260713020000 + 20260714003000, verified against the live catalog, not a repo file) — not a third pattern. 🪤 **The writer is granted to `service_role` ONLY, never `authenticated`** — deliberate and the one place this PR departs from the house REVOKE/GRANT template: a heartbeat any of ~7,000 logged-in accounts could write is forgeable, and one forged row silences the alarm permanently. 🪤 **`DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS` precedes the health `CREATE OR REPLACE`** — it adds a column to the `RETURNS TABLE` list and Postgres rejects that with *"cannot change return type of existing function"*; the function is absent on prod today but present by the time this file runs, since the two migrations apply in filename order. The health read now returns SIX columns: the four counts unchanged, plus `checker_last_ran_at` (liveness, from the run log — an **uncorrelated** scalar subquery so it survives a caller who can see zero builds) and `last_build_checked_at` (throughput, the old `max(safety_checked_at)`); the old five-column `last_checked_at` name is retired rather than silently redefined, because reusing the name that caused the misreading would preserve the ambiguity — its only two consumers ship in the same commit. Guard, `SET search_path`, institution scoping and `REVOKE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` + `GRANT ... TO authenticated` on the health read are byte-for-byte as 20260805100000 left them. Dry-run results (both migrations applied in filename order inside one `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`, proving the DROP-then-CREATE ordering works; health fn confirmed to expose all six out-params): with a heartbeat written through the writer at `now()`, the RPC reported `checker_last_ran_at` **0 min** old — **HEALTHY** — while `last_build_checked_at` was **368 min** stale, i.e. the old signal WOULD HAVE ALARMED and the new one correctly does not; with only a 3-hour-old heartbeat it reported 180 min — **STALLED**; with no heartbeat row it returned NULL alongside unchanged counts, which the card renders as "No runs recorded yet" and never as an alarm. A row aged 8 days plus one fresh write left `rows_left = 1` (prune can never empty the log); one INSERT call followed by one MERGE call left exactly **1 row** with `{enabled, phase:done, recorded, enqueued, skipped}`; a blank `job_key` returned NULL instead of raising. Grants measured in-transaction: health read `anon=false, authenticated=true`; writer `anon=false, authenticated=false, service_role=true`; run-log table `anon SELECT=false, authenticated SELECT/INSERT=false, service_role INSERT=true`, `relrowsecurity=true` with 0 policies; `fn_ai_pulse_champion_safety_queue` and `fn_ai_pulse_release_prompt_build_safety` still `anon=false`, unchanged. A separate post-rollback call re-confirmed all three new objects absent and the md5 of `fn_ai_pulse_record_prompt_safety`, `fn_ai_routine_record_fire` and the three guard functions byte-identical to the pre-rehearsal snapshot.

### AI Pulse — hide administrator accounts from the Senior Learners board (2026-08-05)
- `supabase/migrations/20260805130000_ai_pulse_hide_admins_from_staff_board.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Director decision #1 of `specs/ai-pulse-starter-and-board-decisions-2026-07-30.md`. Replaces `fn_ai_pulse_leaderboard_staff(uuid,boolean,integer)` and `fn_ai_pulse_my_staff_leaderboard(uuid,boolean)`, each authored from its LIVE `pg_get_functiondef` body (md5 `21ba3da4…` and `92644eb8…` respectively, both re-confirmed unchanged after the rehearsal) — never from a repo file.
- **Why:** the Senior Learners board went live 2026-07-30 with the two platform administrators at ranks #1 and #2, scored under the practice institution "JKKN Testing Institution" and carrying `session_host` badges — points earned partly for RUNNING the sessions. Ruling: the people who run a session must not also appear to be winning it.
- **"Completely" is load-bearing.** The Director explicitly rejected keeping a private self-view, so BOTH readers change: no rank row on the public board AND no personal score card. `fn_ai_pulse_my_staff_leaderboard` returns zero rows for an administrator caller — the shape the existing reader already handles (`leaderboard-service.ts` returns `null` on an absent `data[0]`; `SeniorStandingCard` does `if (!data) return null`), so **no UI change was needed**.
- 🪤 **Two different questions, two different tests.** `is_super_admin()` answers "is the CALLER an administrator" (it reads `auth.uid()`) and is used ONLY for the caller early-return. Excluding OTHER people's rows must test THAT ROW's person — `profiles.is_super_admin` for the row's `profile_id`. Using the caller helper as a row filter would hide either everyone or no one. Both the row-level `role = 'super_admin'` test and the `profiles.is_super_admin` flag are excluded (OR): measured on prod they coincide exactly (2 by role, 2 by flag, intersection 2, union 2), and the OR keeps the surface correct if one drifts.
- **Rank is computed AFTER the exclusion**, inside an `eligible` CTE, not filtered out of a pre-computed sequence — otherwise the board would open at #3 with holes where the administrators were. `NOT EXISTS` rather than a JOIN, so the filter can neither drop a row for a missing profile nor duplicate one. `total_staff` on the personal card is likewise counted over the filtered set, so the card can never read "of 175" against a board showing 173.
- **Deliberately unchanged:** `fn_ai_pulse_scored_staff` is not touched (md5 `ecd29a10…` asserted identical inside the rehearsal) — point values, badges and streak logic are untouched, as are the department board and the learner board. **No institution filter**: the ruling hides administrators, not the "JKKN Testing Institution" rows, so a real person scored under the practice institution still appears.
- **Rehearsed `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`, never applied** (no standalone `COMMIT;` in the file — grep-verified, so the dry run cannot turn into a live apply). Inside the txn: board 175 → **173** rows · both administrator `profile_id`s absent · zero rows matching either administrator test · recomputing `RANK()` over the returned set reproduced the returned rank exactly (0 mismatches) with `min(rank)=1` and ranks 1 and 2 both present · the person previously at #3 is now **#1** · administrator caller card = **0 rows** · non-administrator caller card = rank 1 of 173 · both return shapes byte-identical to live. Grants re-asserted with exact signatures: `anon` EXECUTE **false** on both, `PUBLIC` false, `authenticated` true. Separate-call residue check afterwards: all three md5s identical to before, board back to 175 with the two administrators at #1/#2, no `COMMENT` persisted, no temp relations left.
### AI Pulse — starter topics from the academic offer, not from attendance (2026-08-05)
- `supabase/migrations/20260805150000_ai_pulse_starter_topics_from_timetables.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Closes the reason **8 of the 10** AI Pulse cycles produced zero starter prompts (only `d9e6b0d4` with 52 and `53a9eb29` with 4 ever produced any): `fn_ai_pulse_domain_starter_candidates` derived its topics from `ai_pulse_live_attendance` for the SAME cycle, but the generation cron fires at 09:00 UTC and on cycle `53a9eb29` (2026-07-30) the first check-in was 13:10:06 UTC — measured on prod, exactly **0** of that cycle's check-ins existed before 09:00, so the `>= min_learners` floor yielded nothing and the run enqueued nothing. This is not particular to that cycle: across **all 10 cycles, zero check-ins have ever existed before 09:08 UTC** (the first is always ~13:10-13:34), so no morning slot on any weekday can work under the attendance-based RPC. Replaced from the LIVE definition (`pg_get_functiondef` md5 `790099e503eba1e5ddd3e93f333c600a`), not from a repo file; the whole `prior_context` CASE — including the auto-revert branch and its `domain_starter_revert_margin` read — is carried over byte-for-byte, and the RETURNS TABLE shape is unchanged so the cron route needs no reshaping.
- **Grain = ACTIVE PROGRAMME, every institution** (Director decision #4). Measured on prod: **120** active programmes across **11** institutions, versus 3,833 active courses (64× over capacity) and 44 programmes inside the 5 rotation colleges. Deliberately NOT restricted to the rotation (decision #7) — the 2,049 learners in Arts & Science Self (781), Matric (552), Arts & Science Aided (490) and CBSE (226) now receive a prompt despite having no session, team or leaderboard place. (Counts re-read live 2026-07-31; total 4,342 active learners platform-wide.)
- 🪤 **The `>= p_min_learners` floor is now a PRIORITY TIER, not a filter — do not "restore" it as a WHERE.** Its original rationale was relevance + privacy for an ATTENDANCE cohort, where a group of 1 identifies a person; a programme is public catalogue data and carries no such disclosure. Re-imposing it as an exclusion would drop **44 of the 120** programmes (only 76 have ≥1 active enrolled learner) and silently delete a whole institution from the sweep — JKKN College of Education has 12 active programmes and 0 enrolled learners, which is a data gap, not an empty college. `learner_count` now counts real enrolment (`learners_profiles`, active lifecycle), not attendees.
- **Carry-over is EXCLUSION, not sort order** (decision #5). A topic already holding a starter for this cycle is dropped from the result, so each capped run continues exactly where the last stopped. 🪤 **`remaining` = topics that still hold NO prompt — it is NOT `candidates_total - enqueued`.** Enqueuing authors nothing (generation is async on the Max lane), so subtracting the just-enqueued topics reported a 121-topic cycle as ~50% done while 0 topics actually held a prompt. The route also returns `not_yet_queued` (candidates no run has reached yet) and `sweep`, which separates the two zero-candidate cases that used to emit identical JSON: `complete` (every topic authored) vs `source_empty` (the candidate source is dead — the exact signature of the defect this migration closes). Sorting-last was rejected because the Max lane's dedupe key is an IN-FLIGHT guard only (`lib/services/platform/ai-jobs-lane.ts` — queued/claimed/running), NOT an "already done" guard: a third run over a sorted-but-included list would re-enqueue served topics and `fn_ai_pulse_record_domain_starter` would UPSERT over prompts learners may already have copied.
- **General fallback = a real generated row, not SQL-embedded copy** (decision #6). One extra candidate per cycle carries `topic_type = 'general'` on the nil-UUID sentinel (verified on prod to collide with no programme and no course), so the fallback prompt is authored by the same ₹0 loop in both languages with no hardcoded text and no new table. The `ai_pulse_domain_starters_topic_type_check` CHECK is **widened only** — `'course'` and `'programme'` are untouched, `'general'` is added. It sorts first every cycle, so the safety net is always authored in the first run. `fn_ai_pulse_my_domain_starters` (replaced from live md5 `052ca151c6724e3bdf611d9a385cb7e5`; dark gate, learner resolution, removed Tamil gate and course-beats-programme rule all preserved) returns it ONLY when the learner's own topics have no starter.
- **Grants deliberately asymmetric.** `fn_ai_pulse_domain_starter_candidates` is re-granted to `service_role` ONLY — it is a cron read that exposes every programme plus prior prompt text, so granting `authenticated` would WIDEN live access (live ACL was `{postgres, service_role}`). `fn_ai_pulse_my_domain_starters` keeps `authenticated` + `service_role`. Both re-assert `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC`.
- **`fn_ai_pulse_control_vs_tuned` REPLACED** (DROP + CREATE — the RETURNS TABLE gains two columns; authored from the LIVE definition, md5 `ab46816e438ce5fd6e170d83eab7518b`, cycle resolution / unweighted avg / is_control split / rounding all preserved). 🪤 **The `'general'` row must never enter the A/B verdict.** It carries `learner_count` = every active learner (4,342) but `fn_ai_pulse_my_domain_starters` shows it ONLY to learners whose own programme has no starter, so its denominator overstates its real audience 60-100x and it is a guaranteed near-zero copy-rate outlier; in an UNWEIGHTED mean one such row moves the whole cohort average, and `isControlTopic()` hashes `(topic_id | cycle_id)`, so ~1 cycle in 10 it lands in CONTROL and **inflates the reported tuning lift**. Now excluded explicitly `WHERE topic_type <> 'general'` (the route additionally never marks a general row `is_control`). The `learner_count > 0` filter — which silently dropped the 44 zero-enrolment programmes — now RETURNS `excluded_no_learners` and `excluded_general` instead of vanishing.
- ⚠️ **This scales an UNMEASURED loop ~30x.** Read live 2026-07-31: `ai_pulse_domain_starters` has 56 rows and `count(dept_outcome_lift) = 0` — not one row has EVER carried a lift value (52 `insufficient`, 4 `pending`; 662 views, 7 copies). `fn_ai_pulse_measure_domain_starters` reaches a starter only via `ai_pulse_live_attendance` → `fn_ai_pulse_learner_topics`, and that resolver returns `'course'`/`'programme'` ONLY — so a `topic_type='general'` row is **unmeasurable by construction**. The self-improvement hinge is therefore dark: prompts are regenerated each cycle from usage (views/copies, which ARE live-maintained by `fn_ai_pulse_domain_starter_used`) but never from outcome lift. Building that measurement is out of scope here and NOT fixed by this migration.
- Rehearsed on prod in ONE `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` (no standalone `COMMIT` in the file): candidates **117** rows = 120 active programmes − 4 already served + 1 general, across **11** institutions, general at ordinal 1; serving 2 more topics dropped it to **115** (delta exactly 2, both absent); a BSC (Nursing) learner who returns **0 rows today** got the general fallback with `tamil_available = true`, while a BPHARM learner still got their own programme prompt and no general row; `has_function_privilege('anon', …)` **false** on both. Separate-call residue check: both function md5s and the constraint md5 byte-identical to before, 0 `'general'` rows, 0 probe rows, `COMMENT` still NULL.
### RCLTP gamification — enforce the documented service_role-only invariant (2026-07-30)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808110004_rcltp_gamification_lock_service_role_only.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** *(Renamed from `20260808110000_…` on 2026-08-01 — that version was shared by four files; see the version-collision entry at the end of this file.)* ACL-only, zero behaviour change: REVOKEs EXECUTE on `fn_rcltp_award_badge(uuid,text,uuid,text)` and `fn_rcltp_update_streak(uuid,uuid,text,date)` from `authenticated, anon, PUBLIC` and re-GRANTs to `service_role`, closing the gap between what four comments already claim (award/streak are "service_role EXECUTE only" and "a learner cannot self-award" — `app/api/rcltp/gamification/award/route.ts:4`, `.../streak/route.ts:4`, `hooks/rcltp/use-rcltp-gamification.ts:6-7`, `lib/services/rcltp/gamification-service.ts:10-11`) and what the live grant actually was. Measured on prod 2026-07-30: both carried `authenticated=X/postgres`, both SECURITY DEFINER, both mutating, and NEITHER body references `auth.uid()`/`is_super_admin`/`user_has_permission` (read from `prosrc`, not inferred from the creating migration) — so the API route's `rcltp.assessment.manage` gate was the ONLY barrier, and it is bypassed by calling the RPC directly with the anon key that ships in every Next.js bundle, naming your own uuid as `p_learner_id`, into a LIVE leaderboard. Safe to revoke because the ONLY two `.rpc()` call sites both use `rcltpAdminClient()` → `createServiceRoleClient()` (a real service-role key client, not a session-bound one), and there are ZERO in-DB callers and ZERO triggers. **Whole-family sweep, not a 2-of-N fix:** all 11 `public.fn_rcltp_*` functions are SECURITY DEFINER; only 4 lack an in-body guard, and 2 of those (`fn_rcltp_remedial_plan_ai_draft_upsert`, `fn_rcltp_remedial_plan_enqueue`) were ALREADY `postgres,service_role` only — they are the sibling pair proving the intended pattern, and the two here were the drift. The other 7 are deliberately left: each has a genuine in-body guard AND a `createClientSupabaseClient()` (session-bound, runs as `authenticated`) caller, so revoking would break a live screen; `fn_rcltp_spotcheck_resolve` was read in FULL rather than trusted to a keyword match, and its guard is real (`auth.uid()` NOT NULL plus the UPDATE scoped `AND s.reviewer_id = v_uid`). Ends with a `DO $guard$` block that resolves each signature through `to_regprocedure()` first (`has_function_privilege` RAISEs rather than returning false on an unresolvable identifier, which would otherwise mask a signature typo as a privilege failure) and then RAISEs unless each touched function is EXECUTE-denied to `authenticated` AND `anon` and still EXECUTE-able by `service_role`. Verified by BEHAVIOUR in a `BEGIN..ROLLBACK` rehearsal, not by objects: BEFORE, an `authenticated` session reached the function BODY of both (award raised P0001 "rcltp_badge not found", streak raised 23503 on the `rcltp_streaks` FK — i.e. it was actually attempting the INSERT), proving a real learner uuid + real badge slug would have succeeded; AFTER, both return 42501 `permission denied for function`, `anon` likewise, `service_role` still resolves past the ACL into the body for both (routes unaffected), and untouched sibling `fn_rcltp_school_dashboard` still reaches its own in-body guard (no collateral). Zero residue re-proven in a SEPARATE Management-API call (the API wraps a batch in one transaction, so in-batch checks prove nothing): prod still reads `auth=true` on both and `rcltp_learner_badges`/`rcltp_streaks` are still 0 rows. Blast radius at write time: both tables 0 rows — nothing was exploited, and the fix is free now and expensive later.
### SECDEF caller-identity guards — notifications + AI query (2026-07-30)
- `supabase/migrations/20260730180000_secdef_caller_identity_guards_notifications_ai.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** The follow-up that `20260807150000_secdef_caller_identity_lock_sweep.sql` (#2564) explicitly deferred: that sweep closed the 18 caller-identity IDORs where NO application code calls the function, so an ACL revoke could not change behaviour, and its header left "the remaining functions ARE called by application code … those need a per-function `auth.uid()`/permission guard, decided one at a time." These four are that case.
- **A revoke is NOT available on any of the four.** `app/api/notifications/acknowledge/route.ts:42` uses `createServerSupabaseClient` (`lib/supabase/server.ts:60`) and `app/api/ai-query/route.ts:372` passes `createClient` (`lib/supabase/server.ts:23`) into `AIQueryService`; **both are built from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` + the SSR cookie and therefore execute as `authenticated`, not `service_role`.** "Only called from an API route" does not make a revoke safe — only a true service-role client would. Revoking would break notification acknowledgment and the entire AI query route. Both routes already pass the caller's own id from `auth.getUser()`, so every guard is a no-op on the legitimate path.
- **`acknowledge_notification(uuid, uuid)`** bypassed the `user_notifications` UPDATE policy `user_id = auth.uid()`, letting any signed-in user mark ANY other person's notification acknowledged **and read**. Not cosmetic: the route calls acknowledgment "system-enforced and permanently recorded", so forging it destroys the compliance record AND clears the victim's blocking modal — the victim never sees a mandatory notice they are recorded as having accepted. Measured on prod 2026-07-30: 169,543 `user_notifications` rows / 6,802 people; **7** notifications carry `requires_acknowledgment = true` covering 31,966 user-rows, **14,212 still unacknowledged across 6,565 people**, largest single mandatory-ack broadcast **6,225 recipients**. Being broadcasts, an attacker already holds the real `notification_id` from their own copy — only the victim id is needed. This was also the ONLY one of the four with no `SET search_path`; added.
- **`increment_ai_query_count(uuid)`** is a targeted DoS: ~30 calls against a chosen person hits the hardcoded 30-per-5-min ceiling and their next AI question returns 429; repeat every 5 minutes for an indefinite lockout, counter unbounded. **`check_ai_query_rate_limit(uuid)`** is its enabler — its `INSERT .. ON CONFLICT` creates the row for anyone, which is what makes the DoS bite on someone who never used the assistant, and it leaks that person's remaining quota. On its own it is NOT a DoS (a stale window resets the count to 0, which *helps* the victim). **Both are genuine escalation, not merely unguarded: `ai_query_rate_limits` carries ONLY a SELECT policy — no INSERT, no UPDATE — so RLS default-denies a direct write and these SECDEF functions are the sole write path a signed-in caller has.**
- 🚨 **The worst finding is the table, not the function.** `ai_query_logs` carried policy `"System can insert query logs" FOR INSERT roles=public WITH CHECK (true)` **plus** table grants to `anon` of SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE — so any holder of the public anon key embedded in every page of https://www.jkkn.ai could forge audit rows attributed to anyone and **UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE the audit trail, unauthenticated**. `log_ai_query`'s own IDOR is therefore **strictly less capable** than the direct path (the RPC is never granted to anon), which is why the guard on it is defence-in-depth and the policy replacement is the actual fix. Same root cause as `20260726180000` / `20260728190000`: a reassuringly-named permissive policy is not a rule; `TO public WITH CHECK (true)` is. Dropping it cannot break the app — a repo-wide grep finds **no** `.from('ai_query_logs')` anywhere, all writes arrive via `log_ai_query`, which runs as owner `postgres` with `relforcerowsecurity = false` and so bypasses RLS entirely.
- **Guard shape is `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND p_user_id IS DISTINCT FROM auth.uid() AND NOT COALESCE(is_super_admin(), false)` → `42501`.** Leading with the NULL test is load-bearing, not defensive noise: a bare `IS DISTINCT FROM auth.uid()` raises for **every** `service_role` call (NULL is distinct from any id), silently breaking any trusted backend caller — and all four hold a `service_role` grant. The NULL branch is not a hole because it is reachable only by a role holding EXECUTE, and **anon holds none on any of the four (verified: `anon_exec = false` ×4)**; the migration re-asserts the revoke and the regression guard asserts it rather than trusting it. `COALESCE` on `is_super_admin()` is belt-and-braces per `feedback_secdef_guard_not_null_safe_falls_through`. Super admins pass deliberately — `user_notifications` already carries "Super admins can manage all user notifications" FOR ALL, so this widens nothing.
- Function bodies were rebuilt from the **live `pg_get_functiondef()`** output read 2026-07-30, not from a repo file (`feedback_secdef_replace_silently_reverted_money_gate`). All ten of `log_ai_query`'s parameter DEFAULTs are repeated verbatim — `CREATE OR REPLACE` redefines the signature and the caller supplies them by name.
- Ends with a `DO $guard$` regression block asserting the end state in the same transaction (still SECDEF · anon cannot EXECUTE · `authenticated` CAN, since callers are session-bound · body now contains `auth.uid()` · exactly 4 functions found · no `WITH CHECK (true)` INSERT policy remains on `ai_query_logs` · anon holds no table privilege · `authenticated` can no longer UPDATE/DELETE it).
- **Rehearsed, not applied.** `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` via the Management API returned clean with the regression guard passing. Prod re-read in a SEPARATE call afterwards (the API wraps a batch in one transaction, so an in-batch check proves nothing) confirms it is **unchanged**: all four still `guarded = false`, and `ai_query_logs` still carries `WITH CHECK (true)`. No function was executed to demonstrate the vulnerability — the grant, SECDEF and absent guard are sufficient evidence; firing a write at production is not a test, it is the incident.
### Attendance — current-intake readiness, the case the pending surface cannot see (2026-08-08)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808120000_fn_attendance_fresher_readiness.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Adds ONE new read-only function, `fn_attendance_fresher_readiness(p_window_days integer, p_institution_id uuid, p_department_id uuid)`. Creates no table, alters no existing object, so no current dashboard surface can regress.
- **Stamped `...120000`, not `...110000`, deliberately.** Eight open PRs independently computed "one tick after the newest on main" and all landed on `20260808110000` (#2646, #2647, #2650, #2651, #2655, #2656, #2665 and this one). `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations.version` is the PRIMARY KEY, so the second arrival either fails loudly on duplicate key or — the dangerous case — is treated as already-applied and skipped in silence while the ledger reports success and the function is never created. This file moved to `...120000`; the other seven still collide with each other.
- **Why it exists:** `AttendanceDashboardService.getPendingAttendance()` opens with `.from('timetables')`, so pending rows are derived from SCHEDULED PERIODS. A section with no timetable produces no periods → no pending rows → it renders as perfectly healthy on the screen meant to catch unmarked attendance. Measured on prod 2026-07-30: one college has 164 current-intake learners in 10 sections holding ZERO timetable rows, none of them visible to that surface.
- **The inversion:** the row set starts at SECTIONS HOLDING CURRENT-INTAKE LEARNERS, never at timetables, so a section cannot disappear by having nothing scheduled. `blocked` = no timetable at all (attendance impossible; learner count is the exposure) · `not_started` = timetable exists, nothing marked in the trailing window · `ok` = marked in window. Window is a clamped parameter (`GREATEST(1, LEAST(365, COALESCE(p_window_days, 21)))`) — it is caller-supplied and reachable from the browser.
- 🪤 **`student_attendance` has BOTH `section_id` and `section_ids`, and they are NOT redundant.** The marked-check is `sa.section_id = <s> OR <s> = ANY(sa.section_ids)`. Verified on prod: **856 rows carry `section_ids` naming a section the scalar column does not**, so a scalar-only check silently misclassifies every combined-section sitting as never-marked. Do not "simplify" this to the scalar column.
- **`blocked` keys on the absence of ANY timetable, not an ACTIVE one** — an inactive timetable is a different operational problem needing a different fix ("switch it on", not "create one"). The row still returns `active_timetable_count` so the UI flags "timetable exists but none is active" without hiding it inside the blocked bucket. This is exactly Dental's single fresher section (one timetable, `is_active = false`), which therefore reads `not_started`.
- **"Current intake"** = `learners_profiles.admission_year_id` resolving to an `admission_years` row with `is_current = true`, plus `lifecycle_status = 'active'`. `is_current` is one-per-institution, so the IN-set means "each learner's own college's newest batch" and the all-colleges view stays correct without a per-row institution correlation. Same rule as `p_first_year_only` in `fn_attendance_dashboard_section_stats` (`20260804100000`) — deliberately NOT semester-based, because semester data is not reliably advanced as learners progress.
- **No new permission key.** Self-authorizes on the EXISTING `academic.attendance.dashboard.view`, which is present in `lib/constants/permissions.ts` and therefore grantable from Role Management. A guard requiring a key absent from that registry can never be granted and the surface would be super-admin-only forever.
- Guard: `COALESCE(is_super_admin(), false) OR COALESCE(is_admin(), false) OR COALESCE(user_has_permission('academic.attendance.dashboard.view'), false)` — every leg COALESCEd, because a SECDEF predicate returning NULL makes `NOT (...)` evaluate to NULL, which is not TRUE, so an uncoalesced guard FALLS THROUGH instead of raising. Rows then bounded by `role_has_institution_access(institution_id)`, so a `scope='own'` caller reads only its own institution even if it passes another institution's id. `SET search_path = public`, `STABLE`, `statement_timeout = 20s`.
- Lock: `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` (**both** — revoking only `anon` is a no-op while `anon` inherits PUBLIC, and revoking only PUBLIC is a no-op against Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES ... GRANT ALL ON FUNCTIONS TO anon` direct grant), then `GRANT ... TO authenticated, service_role`.
- Rehearsed `BEGIN..ROLLBACK` through the Management API and verified from `pg_proc`/`has_function_privilege` in-transaction, NOT from the migration text: `prosecdef = true`, `proconfig = search_path=public | statement_timeout=20s`, anon EXECUTE `false`, PUBLIC EXECUTE `false`, authenticated EXECUTE `true`. Negative control in the same shape: an unauthenticated call raised `P0001: not authenticated` at the guard. Production re-verified absent in a SEPARATE call after each rollback — the API wraps the whole batch in ONE transaction, so an in-batch check proves nothing.
- Surface: a new **Intake Readiness** tab on the already-registered `/academic/attendance/dashboard` page (`?tab=readiness`) — deliberately NOT a new route, which would pull in the 4-link registration chain and the route-reachability gate.
### SCF prepared pulse — auto-opened pulse gets the same answer window as a lead-opened one (2026-07-30)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808110001_scf_prepared_pulse_close_window.sql` — **NOT applied to any database.** Rehearsed on prod inside ONE `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` Mgmt-API batch (replace succeeded, ACL asserted inside the txn); production verified unchanged in a SEPARATE call — `md5(pg_get_functiondef(...))` back to `8e964c407ed308b1b5645cd394fdfb66`, grants still `postgres=X/postgres | service_role=X/postgres`, kill switch still `false`, `scf_live_pulse` still 11 rows.
- Defect: `fn_scf_prepared_pulse_sweep` (`20260802010000`) hardcodes `now() + interval '240 minutes'` for `auto_close_at`, but `fn_live_poll_open_class_poll` was changed by `20260731040000` (decision #37) to close at 21:00 IST of the opening day. The prepared-pulse sweep is the NEWER migration carrying the OLDER convention, so the two open paths disagree.
- Impact: attendance for a 09:30 IST session is marked around 09:30, so the sweep opens the pulse then and it dies at 13:30 IST, while the identical pulse opened by a Senior Learner lives until 21:00. The window is enforced — `_fn_live_poll_learner_can_answer` gates on `auto_close_at > now()` and `fn_scf_submit_feedback` flips the source to `async` past it — so a learner who checks after class finds the pulse closed. That defeats the sweep's own "open at session-end if it was never opened" purpose.
- Fix: declare `v_close`, compute it exactly as `fn_live_poll_open_class_poll` does (21:00 IST today; `+2h` if the sweep runs after 21:00), and use it at all THREE close-time sites — the anchor INSERT, the poll INSERT, and the anchor UPDATE. Those three sites write two columns: `scf_live_pulse.auto_close_at` (twice) and `induction_session_poll.auto_close_at` (once).
- **Body copied from the VERBATIM live definition, not the repo file** (ref `feedback_secdef_replace_silently_reverted_money_gate`). Normalised comparison of `pg_get_functiondef` against `20260802010000` was identical except the statement terminator, so no later work is silently reverted. Candidate query, kill switch, present-gate, idempotency, advisory lock and seeded question are unchanged. Grants re-asserted (`REVOKE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC, authenticated` / `GRANT ... TO service_role`).
- **NOT a go-live enabler.** `platform_policies` `scf.prepared_pulse.enabled` is `false` and this migration does not touch it. The sweep is also inert regardless of the flag: it requires a session linked to a PUBLISHED `curriculum_lesson`, and prod has 8 published lessons out of 30,340 with 8 `class_session_lesson` links in total (0 today), so the derived candidate set was 1 across the whole of the last 21 days.

- `supabase/migrations/20260731223500_attendance_protection_approved_onduty.sql` — **NOT applied to any database.** Attendance protection for approved on-duty days: new SECDEF `fn_attendance_protected_days` (reads `v_health_tournament_participation` + approved full-day `leave_onduty_applications`), and `fn_exam_audit_attendance` / `fn_vsr_attendance_core` / `fn_my_running_attendance` gain a `protected` column so an approved trip stops costing exam eligibility. Protection is applied at READ time — `student_attendance` is never rewritten, so withdrawing the approval withdraws the credit. Eligibility thresholds are NOT touched. Rehearsed on prod inside ONE `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` Mgmt-API batch against real records: PB22083 52/70 = 74.3% (condonation) → 52+3/70 = 78.6% (eligible); PB24057 55/74 = 74.3% → 55+2/74 = 77.0%; a control learner not on the squad unchanged at 74.3%; 2 of 555 learners in the college moved; denominators, raw `present`, and the 75/65 bands all unchanged. Production verified untouched in a SEPARATE call — `fn_attendance_protected_days` absent, `fn_exam_audit_attendance` still the original 6-column signature, 0 tournament permission rows, version absent from `schema_migrations`. **Review round 2026-07-31:** the lookup is now SPLIT into an ungranted `fn_attendance_protected_days_core(uuid[],date,date,uuid)` (scoped by argument; definer-chain only, like the `fn_vsr_*_core` helpers) and the granted authorizing wrapper `fn_attendance_protected_days` (institution-scoped always, self-scoped unless the caller holds `academic.attendance.view` or `academic.internal_marks.exam_audit.view`). Re-rehearsed live against #2682's merged per-college view: a real peer learner (`role_has_institution_access`=TRUE, both view permissions FALSE) got **4 rows belonging to another learner** from the pre-split function and **0** from the wrapper; the protected learner still gets their own 4; a real super admin still gets 4; `authenticated` and `anon` are both `permission denied` on the core, `anon` likewise on the wrapper. `fn_vsr_attendance_core` calls the core, not the wrapper, because `fn_vsr_shared_record` (the module's one deliberate anon surface) reaches it with no `auth.uid()` — via the wrapper that path raised `not authenticated`; via the core a genuine `anon` caller gets the full shared record back. A learner with no attendance rows returns 0 rows, not an exception. Whole-college control: 9,025 rows before and after, `present`/`total` identical on every row, exactly 1 learner's `pct` moved (87.5 → 91.7, `protected`=1), no `pct` above 100.
- Hardened after review (same migration file): `fn_attendance_protected_days` self-scopes. Passing the institution gate is NOT enough to read a whole college's squads — verified on prod against a real learner (role `student`): `role_has_institution_access(own institution)` = TRUE while `academic.attendance.view` and `academic.internal_marks.exam_audit.view` are both FALSE. Privileged callers (super admin / `academic.attendance.view` / exam-audit view) see everyone in scope; everyone else sees only their own days. Proven: a privileged caller sees both squad members, the learner sees exactly one (themselves), and that learner's own running card still credits the same 3 protected days the audit gives them. Also fixed in the same file: on-duty team members are joined to the application's institution (no cross-tenant credit in a combined audit); one `v_to` bound now drives both the attendance scan and the protection lookup (the previous asymmetry could only push a percentage down); protection-lookup bounds are COALESCEd so a learner with no attendance rows is safe by construction rather than by planner shape. Re-proven unchanged as a REAL non-super-admin principal (scope `own`): PB22083 74.3% -> 78.6%, PB24057 74.3% -> 77.0%, control 74.3% unchanged, 2 of 555 learners moved. Production verified untouched again in a SEPARATE call.
- `supabase/migrations/20260731234500_vsr_overall_honours_protected_days.sql` — **NOT applied to any database.** Republishes `fn_vsr_record_core` so the Verified Skills Record carries ONE attendance rule end to end. After `20260731223500` every per-course `pct` in the record already credited approved on-duty/tournament days (it comes straight from `fn_vsr_attendance_core`), while `overall.pct` was rebuilt here as `SUM(present) / SUM(total)` and did not — so the headline percentage disagreed with the rows printed directly under it, on the one document that leaves the college and is read by an employer who cannot ask what the difference means. Now `overall.pct` = `(SUM(present) + SUM(protected)) / SUM(total)`, and `protected` rides out per course AND overall so the credited days can be SHOWN rather than folded into `present`. Body copied VERBATIM from the live definition (`pg_get_functiondef` md5 `248fa38c1847679f7c5be0f45dfcf73c`, 4,186 bytes, read 2026-07-31) with only the attendance block changed, so no later work is silently reverted (ref `feedback_secdef_replace_silently_reverted_money_gate`). Eligibility thresholds untouched — this function never reads them. **SECDEF split preserved:** the call is still `fn_vsr_attendance_core(p_learner, v_inst)`, which still reaches the ungranted, argument-scoped `fn_attendance_protected_days_core(uuid[],date,date,uuid)` and NOT the authorizing wrapper — the anon-granted `fn_vsr_shared_record` path carries no `auth.uid()`, so that split has to hold or the share link 500s. `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, authenticated, PUBLIC` re-asserted.
### Sports tournaments — a refusal stops only that college's learners, and we record who hosted (2026-07-31)

A refused college's learners, an undecided college's learners, and a learner with no `institution_id` (nobody could have approved for them) all contribute nothing. `security_invoker` retained; `REVOKE ALL … FROM anon, PUBLIC` re-asserted because DROP+CREATE re-triggers Supabase's default grants on views.

(2) Teaches `public.fn_get_policy` to RESOLVE that scope — measured live 2026-07-30 its WHERE clause enumerated institution/global/role/user only and its ORDER BY had no cohort branch, so widening the CHECK alone would have left every seeded cohort row silently returning the caller's default (objects verify, behaviour broken). AFTER (not BEFORE) because nudge<pause<remove is a cross-row rule the 15-row seed would otherwise trip on its own first row.
