The file carries no `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;` of its own, so the rehearsal stays a rehearsal — an inner `COMMIT` turns it into a live apply. Adds 4 permission keys, 10 RLS policies and re-issues 2 SECURITY DEFINER functions. Writes no learner data and grants no key to any role.
- **The leak is at the BASE TABLE, not the RPC layer.** PR #2740 builds a School of Influence Programme Coordinator out of the shared spine keys `cohort.view/.create/.edit/.manage`. `fn_soi_can_manage_batch` already refuses any cohort whose `kind` is not `school_of_influence`, so the RPCs were never the problem — but the RLS on `public.cohorts` / `public.cohort_memberships` is programme-blind, and a coordinator can reach those tables directly through PostgREST. **Measured live: 5 cohorts (3 school_of_influence, 1 mba_associate, 1 sf100) and 62 memberships — of which all 62 belong to the two OTHER programmes.**
- **New keys:** `cohort.school_of_influence.view / .create / .edit / .manage`, registered in `lib/constants/permissions.ts` (a key registered nowhere is ungrantable and produces a screen that opens and returns empty). Same action→key mapping as the spine: SELECT→`.view`, INSERT→`.create`, UPDATE→`.edit`, DELETE→`.manage`.
- **Additive, and that is the whole safety argument.** Ten NEW policies (`*_soi_scoped_*`) are added BESIDE the eight spine policies; not one existing policy is dropped, replaced or edited. PostgreSQL OR-combines permissive policies, so an extra permissive policy can only ADMIT more rows — it is structurally incapable of hiding a row an existing policy admits. Rewriting the eight to say "broad key OR narrow key" would give the same truth table but means re-issuing eight live objects from text, which is how a money gate got silently reverted here before. Same pattern the spine already uses: `cohorts_soi_member_select` / `cohort_memberships_soi_member_select` (20260808140000) are additive SoI-only policies on these same tables today.
- **The premise is proved, not asserted.** Section 0 snapshots the eight spine policies into a `pg_temp` table before any DDL; section 4 fails the migration if `cmd`, `roles`, `qual` or `with_check` moved by one byte. The snapshot is `pg_temp`-qualified deliberately — an unqualified `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` resolves through `search_path` and would drop a real table of that name in `public`.
- **Live 4-phase impersonation battery inside the rollback**, same user, same institution grants, only the keys swapped: broad-key holder BEFORE = 5 cohorts / 62 memberships; **AFTER = 5 / 62, identical** (existing holders unaffected, measured); narrow-key holder = **3 cohorts, 0 memberships, sf100 and mba_associate invisible**; `fn_soi_can_manage_batch` returns **true** on an SoI batch and **false** on the sf100 batch. Denying the leak is only half the job, so the battery also writes: accept-path `INSERT ... RETURNING` (the exact shape of `CohortService.createMembership`'s `.insert().select().single()`) = 1 row, status move = 1, `cohort_status_events` audit row = 1, batch intake edit = 1 — while an sf100 batch edit returns **0 rows** and an sf100 membership INSERT is **refused**.
- ⚠️ **`institution_scope = 'all'` cannot be minted by a probe** — `guard_no_privilege_escalation` refuses it for any non-super-admin session, correctly. The battery uses `scope='own'` plus explicit `user_institution_access` rows to both cohort-holding institutions, which removes institution as a confound and exercises the real cross-institution grant path.
- ⚠️ **`has_function_privilege('public', …)` RAISES** — there is no role literally named `public`; PUBLIC is the pseudo-grantee oid 0. The anon/PUBLIC assert reads `aclexplode(proacl)` instead, and treats a **NULL `proacl` as LEAKY**: for functions, no ACL entry means the built-in default is in force and that default grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC.
- **Two SECDEF functions re-issued from LIVE `pg_proc.prosrc`, never a repo file:** `fn_soi_can_manage_batch(uuid)` and `fn_soi_can_review_applications(uuid)` — the only two that read `cohort.manage` directly for this module (all other SoI RPCs delegate to one of them). The sole edit in each is "broad key OR narrow key"; both were already hard-scoped to `kind='school_of_influence'`, so widening them cannot reach another programme. `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` re-asserted in the same file.
- **Deliberately NOT widened:** `fn_apply_cohort_adjustment_proposal` also reads `cohort.manage` directly but belongs to the cohort-adjustment module, so a holder of the narrow keys alone cannot reach it — and section 4 FAILS if it ever starts accepting a School of Influence key. `cohort_status_events` UPDATE/DELETE stay admin-only; the audit trail is append-only by design.
- **Grants nothing to anybody.** Section 4 RAISEs if any role is found holding one of the four keys, read **by value** (`(permissions->>key)::boolean = true`) and not by `permissions ? key`, which tests existence — the reading that produced a false governance alarm here before. Live check: 16 roles carry a `cohort.*` key today and **every one is stored `false`**, i.e. as dead as absent.
- **Follow-up owned elsewhere:** `lib/services/school-of-influence/batch-service.ts` sets `SOI_TRANSFER_PERMISSION = 'cohort.manage'` as a client-side pre-check so a refusal reads as a sentence instead of an RLS zero-row silence; it needs to accept either key. Nothing is unsafe meanwhile — the database is the floor — but the message would be wrong. Five SoI RPCs also name only `cohort.manage` in their refusal text: still true, now incomplete.
### IQAC 48 -> 107 mapping register — config table, ships EMPTY on purpose (2026-08-01)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808210200_iqac_cac_metric_map_config.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Creates `public.iqac_cac_metric_map` + `public.iqac_cac_metric_map_audit`, one SECURITY DEFINER trigger function and its trigger. Writes no learner data and touches no existing object. `/accreditation/iqac` reads the table when it exists and reports `registryAvailable: false` (PostgREST `PGRST205`) as "the mapping register has not been created yet" rather than as an error — so the page is correct both before and after the apply.
- **Why a table rather than a TypeScript constant.** `docs/architecture/config-table-pattern.md` names **mappings** in its own DOES list. Which of the 107 master framework metrics a given CAC dimension summarises is a judgement the IQAC makes and revises, not algorithm — so it gets a row, a runtime reader (`lib/services/accreditation/iqac-metric-map-service.ts`) and, on apply, an editable surface.
- **Seeds ZERO rows, deliberately.** No verified correspondence between the CEO's 48 CAC dimensions and these 107 rubric metrics exists today. A plausible seed would close an open question by pretending it was answered, and every downstream reader would inherit the guess as fact. The page therefore renders all 48 as unmapped, and counts "reviewed, no counterpart" apart from "not examined yet" — both display as unmapped and only one still needs doing.
- **Grant order is load-bearing.** `REVOKE ALL ... FROM anon, PUBLIC, authenticated` comes FIRST, then `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ... TO authenticated`. Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` means both tables are born `anon=arwdDxt` AND `authenticated=arwdDxt`, so a bare `GRANT SELECT` is a silent no-op that leaves writes in place. **DELETE is never granted** — a superseded mapping is deactivated, not destroyed, so the record of what the IQAC once believed survives. The audit table grants `SELECT` only; the SECURITY DEFINER trigger is its sole writer.
- RLS on both tables; every guard predicate wrapped in `COALESCE(..., false)` because a NULL guard falls through and grants access. SELECT reads `accreditation.metrics.view`, INSERT/UPDATE read `accreditation.metrics.manage` — both already in `lib/constants/permissions.ts`; no new key was invented. The trigger function carries `SET search_path = public` and an explicit `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` even though trigger functions are exempt from the CI guard.
- 🪤 **No FK to `sh_accreditation_metrics`.** The target is the PAIR `(metric_type, metric_code)` and that pair carries no unique constraint on that table today, so no FK is possible without first altering the framework table — a change that belongs in its own reviewed migration rather than smuggled in beneath this feature. Validation lives in the service layer; a mapping pointing at nothing renders as unmapped rather than inventing a target. A `CHECK ((body_code IS NULL) = (metric_code IS NULL))` blocks the half-mapping that would otherwise read as mapped while pointing nowhere.
- ⚠ **Reported, not changed:** `sh_accreditation_metrics.weightage` is **NULL on all 107 rows** (read live 2026-08-01 over PostgREST). The dashboard prints the column as "not set" instead of hiding it — a coordinator asked to weight the framework needs to know the weights do not exist, and a dropped column would let them assume weighting was already happening somewhere. Nothing on that page weights, totals or ranks, so the absence changes no number there.

Authored from the LIVE `pg_get_functiondef`, not the repo copy; signature, `RETURNS TABLE`, `ORDER BY` and the `improvement.board.manage` guard are unchanged, and the anon revoke is re-asserted because a replace can re-arm Supabase's default grant. Rehearsed inside `BEGIN .. ROLLBACK` as a non-super-admin board manager: 45 people before, the identical 45 after (symmetric difference 0) with only the MBA cohort active; then, with the CSE Resident cohort switched on inside the same rolled-back transaction, a throwaway role holder went from absent (45) to present (46). ### Auto-lock every new public relation, whatever created it (2026-08-01)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808220000_autolock_new_public_relations.sql` — **APPLIED to prod 2026-08-01 with Director approval.** Creates one SECURITY DEFINER function and one `ddl_command_end` event trigger. Writes no data, alters no existing relation, changes no existing grant. This file records what is already live; it is committed so the repo stops disagreeing with the database.
- **Why a CI guard was not enough, and this is not a duplicate of one.** `scripts/ci/check-table-anon-revoke.mjs` shipped **2026-07-27** (PR #2488) and already required an explicit anon revoke + `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` for every new relation added **in a migration**. It did not stop the **2026-07-31** leak of `_bak_learner_section_repair_20260731` (179 learners' `learner_id` / `roll_number` / `section_name`, readable with the public anon key) because **no migration ever created that table** — grepping `supabase/migrations/` for the name returns exactly one hit, `20260731210000_lock_repair_backups_and_hod_leaderboard.sql`, the migration that *locked* it. The table was created by hand through the Management API during a live repair. A CI guard reads the repo; repairs here are run by hand against prod. Those are disjoint sets, so only the database could close it.
- **What it does.** On `ddl_command_end` for `CREATE TABLE` / `CREATE TABLE AS` / `SELECT INTO` / `CREATE VIEW` / `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`, for schema `public` only: `REVOKE ALL … FROM anon, PUBLIC`, and `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` on ordinary tables. RLS-with-no-policy is deny-all for ordinary roles while `postgres` and `service_role` carry `rolbypassrls`, so repair tooling and admin routes keep working. `CREATE TABLE AS` never enables RLS by itself — that is the CTAS vector, and it is now covered.
- 🪤 **Fail-open on purpose.** Every action is wrapped so a failure `RAISE`s a `WARNING` and continues, with an outer handler around the whole loop. An event trigger that throws aborts the DDL that fired it, which would break every `CREATE TABLE` in the cluster — far worse than one unlocked relation. The CI guard stays the enforcing layer; this is the net that also covers hand-run SQL.
- **Proved behaviourally with a control, inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`, before applying.** Without the trigger a fresh `CREATE TABLE` and a fresh `CREATE TABLE … AS SELECT` both came back **RLS off and `anon` granted** — the 2026-07-31 leak reproduced exactly. With the trigger installed, a plain table, a `_bak_` CTAS table, a `_rollback_` CTAS table and a view all came back **RLS on (tables) and no `anon` entry**, and a further probe confirmed the DDL still succeeds so the trigger cannot block a migration. Residue re-verified **0** in a SEPARATE call (0 probe relations, 0 triggers, 0 functions) before the real apply. Post-apply on prod: `pg_event_trigger` shows the trigger present and enabled (`evtenabled='O'`), the function is `SECURITY DEFINER`, and `has_function_privilege('anon', …, 'EXECUTE')` is **false**.
- **Not covered, deliberately:** an explicit `GRANT … TO anon` issued *after* creation. That is a considered act, visible in the diff, and is what `scripts/ci/anon-exposure-allowlist.json` plus `scripts/ci/check-anon-exposure-live.mjs` exist to review.
### School of Influence — folding a batch too small to run (2026-08-02)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809090500_soi_uneven_batch_merge.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Seeds the `soi.min_viable_batch_size` policy row (`scope_type='cohort'`, `scope_id IS NULL`, default **8**) and creates three functions: `fn_soi_min_viable_batch_size` (internal reader, clamped to `soi.batch_capacity`), `fn_soi_merge_plan` (STABLE, guarded by `fn_soi_can_review_applications`, writes nothing) and `fn_soi_record_batch_merge` (records a confirmed fold or its undo, and notifies everybody moved). Adds `uniq_soi_batch_merge_run` + `idx_cohort_status_events_soi_batch_merge` on `cohort_status_events`. Creates no table and moves no membership.
- **The plan is automatic; the move is not.** There is no cron route and no unattended caller anywhere in the change — a coordinator confirms each fold on `/startup-studio/school-of-influence/admin/merge`. Same standard the inactivity engine (`20260808150000`) is held to, for a stronger reason: a merge acts on somebody who has done nothing but apply to a batch that turned out quiet.
- **No move path is added.** Every transfer goes through the existing `CohortService.transferMembership` (via `SoiBatchService.transferToBatch`), so `assertMemberIdentity`, the preserved lifecycle status, the `config.transfers` breadcrumb and the per-person audit row are the spine's, not a second implementation. The recorder BACKFILLS the per-person row when the spine's best-effort event write failed, and says so in its return.
- 🪤 **`fn_soi_min_viable_batch_size` is revoked from `authenticated` EXPLICITLY**, not merely un-granted: Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` hands `authenticated` a direct EXECUTE grant on every new function, so omitting a GRANT would have left the unguarded threshold reader callable by any signed-in user. The apply-time assert refuses the migration if it is. The two caller-facing functions are asserted REACHABLE by `authenticated` in the same block, so a revoke-everything reflex cannot ship the feature dark.
- **`trg_guard_soi_policy_thresholds` is deliberately NOT extended.** It passes any unnamed `soi.*` key straight through, so the new row inserts cleanly; extending it would mean `CREATE OR REPLACE` of a live function from a repo file that may already be behind the database (the 2026-07-26 money-gate reversion). The 1..capacity bound is enforced in the reader instead.

### Session-feedback rollup family goes set-based — 2.7x / 10.2x, proven identical (2026-08-02)
- `supabase/migrations/scfrollups_family_perf.sql` — **APPLIED to prod 2026-08-02 ~00:55 IST (night window) via Management API, Director-authorized speed round.** Re-issues two SECURITY DEFINER functions from proven-identical rewrites; changes no answers, no tables, no grants beyond re-asserting the anon/PUBLIC locks. Rollback with exact prior bodies: `artifacts/ROLLBACK_scf-rollups_2026-08-02.sql`.
- **`fn_scf_confirmation_rollup` 2,735ms → 1,012ms (2.70x)** on its worst caller shape (super_admin, 14 days, all institutions; pg_stat mean 3,173ms ×32 calls — the platform's worst query post-reset); one-institution shape 380→193ms. Mechanics: scope verdicts once per DISTINCT window institution instead of per row; `DISTINCT ON` + 11MB external disk sort → `GROUP BY` + `min(session_end_local)`; 99k per-row `EXISTS` probes → one hash join against the window's DISTINCT feedback keys (the UNIQUE `(student_id, attendance_date, period_id)` makes it multiplication-free); `fn_scf_safe_time` once per period via an `OFFSET 0` fence (the planner flattens a bare lateral scalar subquery — 4.2k calls instead of 99k, ~800ms of the win); Present + uuid-shape filter pushed into C-level jsonpath emitting only `student_id` strings.
- **`fn_scf_faculty_completion` 1,226ms → 120ms (10.2x)** for the heaviest Senior Learner (251 sessions/31d; pg_stat mean 2,812ms ×19, grazed the 8s bell at 7,952ms during the Saturday peak). The whale was ~1.8k per-learner/per-session `fn_get_policy_int/text` calls (~0.65ms each), collapsed into a 14-row materialized per-institution policy map (the `fn_scf_pending_for_learner` recipe) with COALESCE fallback for NULL/unknown institutions; the roster array exploded once per session instead of twice.
- **Zero answer changes, measured not asserted:** md5 of the sorted row-multiset old-vs-new inside one transaction (`now()` held constant) — 100/100 identical pairs for faculty_completion (25 personas × 4 window shapes), 125/125 for confirmation_rollup (25 personas × 5 param shapes; 70 of those pairs prove denied personas raise the identical authorization exception). Post-swap live values byte-identical: `(99309,39157,6087,54065)` all-institutions, `(14955,3869,1422,9664)` one-institution.
- **`fn_scf_admin_faculty_summary` deliberately untouched (parked with numbers):** 272–282ms at night for 188 rows, already under its 300ms target; its plan is already fully set-based (hash anti join), the best candidate variant measured 271ms (~1.0x), and its 598ms pg_stat mean is daytime congestion, not query cost.

### Evidence sources learn where to send a person, so a gap stops being a dead end (2026-08-09)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809100700_evidence_source_registry_fix_routes.sql` — **APPLIED TO PRODUCTION 2026-08-04** under Director authorisation. Adds three NULLABLE text columns to `public.quality_evidence_source_registry` (`fix_route`, `fix_hint`, `owner_role`) and seeds 21 of its 24 rows. Creates no object, drops nothing, adds no function — so no SECURITY DEFINER and no anon-revoke clause applies. The table's existing RLS and anon posture (from `20260423_unification_crud_retrofit.sql`) are untouched, and adding a column cannot widen either. Carries no `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;`, so a `BEGIN .. ROLLBACK` rehearsal stays a rehearsal.
- **Apply receipt (2026-08-04).** Rehearsed in `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`; residue verified `0` **in a separate API call**. Verified after apply by catalog: 3 columns present, 21 of 24 rows carry `fix_route` + `owner_role`, 3 remain NULL by design (no verified destination, so consumers must render the gap with no link). All 21 `fix_route` paths were checked to resolve to a real page **before** the apply — note `/staff` is an `app/(routes)/staff/route.ts` landing rather than a `page.tsx`, so a page.tsx-only check reports it missing when it is not. All four referenced `owner_role` keys exist in `custom_roles`; two of them (`hr_admin`, `lead_auditor`) currently have **zero holders anywhere**, so evidence owned by those roles cannot be assigned to a person until someone is given the role — a data gap, not a defect in this migration.
- **What the registry could not answer.** Its 24 rows say WHAT a source is. They never said where a person goes, what to type, or whose desk it is — so a screen could print "not captured yet" and stop, which is the same dead end as the `0` badge it replaced, only quieter.
- **THREE ROWS ARE DELIBERATELY LEFT NULL, and that is the design, not an omission.** `facility_teaching_snapshot` (a nightly rollup whose upstream entry points are spread across several modules — naming one would hide the others), `coe_result_snapshot` (mirrored from the COE examination system, a different application; there is no MyJKKN screen that edits a pass percentage and there must not be) and `event_feedback_snapshot` (collected per event, so the destination is `/events/<that event>` and never a static path — a link to the event list would look like an instruction and give none). A `fix_route` pointing at a 404, or at a screen that cannot fix the gap, is worse than NULL. Every consumer must treat NULL as "render the gap with NO button"; `app/(routes)/accreditation/_lib/metric-gap-state.ts` enforces it and `__tests__/app/accreditation/metric-gap-state.test.ts` holds it there.
- **Every seeded route was checked against the route tree at `667432d5`, not remembered** — each corresponds to an existing `app/(routes)/<path>/page.tsx`, and assertion (b) fails the apply if any route is relative or carries a dynamic `[segment]`, because the person reading a gap has no id to substitute. Assertion (c) fails on a route with no hint (a button with no instruction), and (d) fails if fewer than 21 rows were reached — the failure mode where a `source_kind` was renamed and the UPDATE silently matched nothing.
- **`owner_role` is a ROUTING HINT and nothing reads it for access.** Not a permission, not a grant, consulted by no RLS policy and no SECURITY DEFINER function. Access still comes from `custom_roles.permissions` via `user_has_permission()`, unchanged. Every value is a `role_key` already present in this repo's migrations (`hr_admin`, `accreditation_officer`, `cdc_head`, `nif_coordinator`, `lead_auditor`, `chief_warden`, `event_coordinator`, `sports_coordinator`, `hod`, `admission`, `accounts`). Section 4 **REPORTS and does not fail on** a hint with no matching `custom_roles` row — which roles are seeded varies per database, and a stale hint must never block a migration that grants nothing.
- **The UI half ships in the same PR and is safe BEFORE the apply.** `hooks/accreditation/use-evidence-fix-routes.ts` reads the registry with `select('*')`, deliberately: merging to main deploys immediately here, so the code WILL run against a database without these columns. A column list would fail the whole request with PostgREST `42703` and kill a registry read that was working; `select('*')` returns what exists, the three read as `undefined`, every source normalises to `fix_route = null`, and the page renders the gap with no button — the designed fallback, reached by doing nothing. The buttons appear the day the migration applies. **Do not tighten that select.**
- ⚠ **An RLS denial on `accreditation_metric_owners` is indistinguishable from an empty register** — PostgREST returns zero rows with no error, and the table holds 0 rows today, so "No owner assigned yet" is true under both readings at present. The renderer keeps a third owner state (`undefined` = could not read) alive for the day that stops being true; wiring a readability probe to it is the follow-up.
### NIRF evidence mappings — first rows for a body that had none (2026-08-09)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809100200_nirf_evidence_mappings.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply** (TIER-1, data-touching). It INSERTs into `quality_evidence_mappings` and does nothing else: creates no object, alters no object, drops nothing, and adds no function, so no SECURITY DEFINER / anon-revoke clause applies to it.
- **What was empty.** Read live 2026-08-02: the junction held 212 rows — NAAC 166, NBA 46, and **zero** for NIRF, PCI, DCI, INC, UGC, QS, NCTE and AICTE. The 17 NIRF metric rows already exist in `sh_accreditation_metrics` (the discriminator column is `metric_type`, **not** `body_code`) and `/accreditation/nirf` already reads this junction through `useNIRFEvidenceCounts` — so the dashboard has been rendering 17 metrics against no evidence at all. Director decision 4 put NIRF first.
- **4 of 17 metrics mapped, 13 deliberately left empty.** `TLR_SS` 3559 · `OI_GD` 3559 · `OI_RD` 3547 · `OI_ESCS` 731 = **11,396 rows** on a first apply. Every mapped row comes from `learners_profiles`, the only source verified to hold enough populated, unambiguous data to back a NIRF figure. Per-record grain is deliberate — this junction is a traceability index, so an auditor can walk a NIRF number back to the exact enrolment records behind it, and one learner record legitimately backs several metrics.
- 🪤 **The institution filter is the load-bearing line: `institutions.iqac_code IS NOT NULL`.** It resolves to exactly the 8 higher-education colleges and **excludes 784 active learners** in JKKN Matric Higher Secondary School, Nattraja Vidhyalya CBSE and JKKN Testing Institution. NIRF ranks higher education only; counting school learners would have inflated every NIRF figure at the source. It is also the same predicate the dashboard's own college switcher uses (`useJKKNInstitutionsNIRF`), so no row is written that the page cannot show.
- **`OI_ESCS` is half-mapped, and says so.** Only the SOCIAL half is written — the statutorily reserved codes SC, SC-A, ST, DNC, DNT read from the `community_categories` master, not a judgement invented here. The ECONOMIC half needs an income threshold, a policy number NIRF restates each submission year and that no Director has set for JKKN. `annual_income` is populated on 4,341 of 4,343 active learners, so that half is one decision away, not a collection project. Until it is set the metric **undercounts by design**.
- 🪤 **`TLR_FP`, `TLR_QF` and `TLR_FE` are blocked by one root cause: teaching and non-teaching team members cannot be told apart.** The 857-row team-member table (named in section 5 of the migration) carries the *same single `role_type` value on all 857 rows* — including designations "Bus Driver", "Attender", "Dental College Ayaah" and "Girls Hostel Scavenger". `employment_type` is likewise identical on all 857, so "permanent" is not recorded anywhere. `designation` is free text with case variants, so a keyword whitelist would be a guess about who teaches. `qualification_summary` is set on only 178 of 857. `TLR_FE` is arithmetic over the other two and unblocks automatically when they do. This is the single highest-value fix for NIRF coverage.
- **`PR_PEER` gets no row, on purpose** (decision 2) — NIRF sources peer perception from its own survey. The remaining gaps are honest and each is recorded in section 5 of the file: `RPC_PU` / `RPC_QP` (`sh_publications` exists, **0 rows**), `RPC_IP` (`ip_filings` exists, **0 rows**), `GO_PS` / `GO_GUE` (`ss_alumni_tracking`, `ss_graduation_evaluations` exist, **0 rows**), `GO_PL` / `GO_MS` (`cdc_placements` holds 2 rows, both merely offered, none accepted — and it carries no `institution_id`), `RPC_FR` (`sh_solutions` holds 2 active consultancy rows; whether consultancy belongs in NIRF's research footprint is an IQAC judgement), `TLR_FS` (no per-institution expenditure table — the fee tables record income, which is a different quantity and not substitutable).
- **Proved by execution, not by reading.** The file was run against a scratch PostgreSQL 16 database stubbed to the live shapes, seeded with a college learner, a school learner, a test-institution learner, a graduated learner, blank-and-NULL gender/state rows, and a pre-existing NAAC row on the same learner. Result: `TLR_SS=5, OI_GD=3, OI_RD=3, OI_ESCS=2` — exactly the predicted set, with the school and test-institution learners excluded, blanks rejected by `btrim`, and the NAAC row untouched. **Re-running inserted 0 rows on all four statements** (idempotent via a `NOT EXISTS` guard per statement — correct whatever the constraint does with NULLs — plus `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` as a backstop).
- ⚠ **`programme_id` and the 5-column unique constraint exist in production but in NO migration file in this repo** — they were applied by hand on 2026-08-02, so the repo cannot tell you this database's shape. Section 0 therefore checks the table, the column and the 5-column unique index before touching anything. **The negative case was tested too:** against a database drifted back to the old 4-column constraint the file stops with a named, actionable error and writes **0 rows**, instead of failing cryptically part-way through.
- ⚠ **Follow-up owned elsewhere, deliberately not touched here.** `app/(routes)/accreditation/nirf/page.tsx` renders an unmapped metric as `evidenceCounts?.[m.metric_code] ?? 0` — a **`0` badge, not a gap**. After this file applies, `PR_PEER` and the other 12 will read "0", which decision 2 says must never happen; that is a one-line UI change in a file this migration has no business editing. The same hook also pulls every NIRF row to the browser to count them client-side, which this file grows from 0 to ~11.4k rows — it works (there is no server row cap; a 7,171-row fetch was confirmed) but it should become a count aggregate.
### Freeze the filed figures — the writer decision 7 never had (2026-08-02)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809100400_accreditation_freeze_reported_figures.sql` — **FILE ONLY, NOT APPLIED to any database. Director-gated apply.** Creates one SECURITY DEFINER function, `fn_accreditation_freeze_reported_figures(uuid)`. Creates no table, alters no column, drops no policy, and grants no key to any role. Idempotent (`CREATE OR REPLACE`) and carries no `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;`, so a `BEGIN .. ROLLBACK` rehearsal stays a rehearsal.
- **The gap it closes: a complete reader over a key nothing writes.** `fn_accreditation_reported_vs_actual` (migration `20260809100000`, PR #2771, applied to prod) reads `accreditation_submissions.metadata -> 'reported_metrics'` and returns reported / actual / drift per metric. Read live 2026-08-02: **zero submissions carry that key**, because no code path anywhere writes it. Every row the reader returns therefore has `reported = NULL` and `drift = NULL` — the function works perfectly and can never answer the question Director decision 7 asked it.
- **The reserved shape is honoured, not re-invented.** `20260809100000` set the shape as a column comment (`{"reported_metrics": {"<metric_code>": <number>}, "reported_at": "<ISO 8601>"}`); this writes exactly those two keys via `metadata || jsonb_build_object(...)` — a MERGE. The DCF export page already writes `filename`, `metrics_seeded`, `evidence_rows`, `exported_at` and `note` into the same object, and all five survive. A `SET metadata = ...` would have destroyed the paper trail with nothing to complain about.
- **WRITE-ONCE, and that is the whole point.** A second call RAISEs `SQLSTATE 55000` and changes nothing. Re-freezing would rewrite history to match the present, collapse the drift to zero, and leave a screen that looks perfectly healthy — the failure mode is silent, so the refusal is loud. There is no force flag and no re-freeze entry point. The guard tests key EXISTENCE (`metadata ? 'reported_metrics'`), so a filing that legitimately captured zero metrics still counts as frozen and `{}` cannot read as "never frozen".
- **`SELECT … FOR UPDATE` before the write-once check.** Without the row lock two concurrent calls both read "not yet frozen" and the second overwrites the first — the check would be advisory rather than binding.
- **An RPC, not a trigger, deliberately.** A `BEFORE UPDATE OF submitted_at` trigger fires on every path that sets the column, including a bulk repair, a backfill, or a future screen correcting a typo in a filing date — each of which would stamp today's counts onto last year's filing. Freezing is a judgement ("this is what we filed"), so it takes an explicit call with an explicit caller.
- **It also performs the filing transition, because nothing else does.** Grepped across `app/`, `lib/`, `components/`, `hooks/` on `jicate/main`: **no code anywhere sets `accreditation_submissions.submitted_at`** (every hit belongs to Startup Studio or the stakeholder surveys). The reader filters `submitted_at IS NOT NULL`, so a snapshot frozen onto a row that was never marked filed is invisible to the only function that reads it. The function therefore sets `submitted_at` — **only when NULL, via COALESCE, never rewritten** — sets `submitted_by` only if a matching `profiles` row exists (else the FK would fire), and advances `status` **only from 'draft'**; `accepted`, `revision_requested`, `rejected` and `withdrawn` are outcomes the awarding body decided and freezing our own figures does not undo them.
- **The counts are gathered exactly the way the reader gathers `actual`** — same three predicates, same `GROUP BY`, same plain `=` on `period_label` (so a `quality_evidence_mappings` row with a NULL `period_label` is counted by neither side). Any divergence here would fabricate drift at the moment of filing, which is worse than no feature at all.
- **Session identity only.** The signature is `(p_submission_id uuid)` — no caller-supplied user id. A SECURITY DEFINER function that accepts the user it should act as is an IDOR, and 75 functions of that shape already exist in this database. Guards are `is_super_admin() OR is_admin() OR (user_has_permission('accreditation.submissions.manage') AND role_has_institution_access(...))`, each wrapped in `COALESCE(..., false)` because a NULL guard falls through and grants access. `SET search_path = public`, explicit `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM anon, PUBLIC` then `GRANT … TO authenticated`.
- ⚠️ **`accreditation.submissions.manage` is registered nowhere and held by nobody.** `lib/constants/permissions.ts` has no `accreditation.submissions.*` entry at all; open PR #2769 adds the family. The key is used anyway because it is what the live `submissions_update` RLS policy (`20260417000001`) already demands — inventing a second key would guarantee the two layers drift. **Consequence, stated not hidden: until #2769 merges and a role is granted the key, only the 14 super administrators and admins can freeze anything**, via the bypass branches. The surface it lives on is already super-admin-gated, so nothing regresses.
- **Assertions run inside the migration:** the function exists, is `prosecdef`, carries `search_path=public`, `anon` cannot EXECUTE, PUBLIC cannot EXECUTE, and `authenticated` can. PUBLIC is read via `aclexplode(pg_proc.proacl)` treating a **NULL `proacl` as LEAKY** (for functions, no ACL entry means the built-in EXECUTE-to-PUBLIC default is still in force) — `has_function_privilege('public', …)` is not used because there is no role literally named `public` and that call RAISEs.
- 🪤 **Found while wiring the caller, fixed in the same PR:** `app/(routes)/accreditation/naac/dcf-export/page.tsx` inserted `status: 'drafted'`, which is not in the table's CHECK (`'draft','submitted','accepted','revision_requested','rejected','withdrawn'`). **Every submission-row insert from that page has been rejected since it shipped** — the page swallowed it into a `console.warn` plus a soft toast, so the "paper trail for IQAC" it advertises never existed. Changed to `'draft'`, which is valid under the original constraint and under any widened one.
- ⚠️ **Reported, not changed:** the export page labels its periods `'2024-25'` / `'2027'`, while `quality_evidence_mappings` carries `'AY 2026-27'` (and `20260809100000` §8 normalises two stray `'2026-27'` rows to that form). Both sides of the reader filter on `period_label`, so freezing an AQAR 2024-25 submission today captures **zero metrics** — correctly, since no evidence claims that cycle. The UI says so in plain words rather than back-filling a number; reconciling the two label vocabularies is a separate decision.
### Accreditation opened to the people accountable for it — 5 roles, read-only but one (2026-08-02)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809100100_accreditation_widen_access_to_accountable_roles.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Two `UPDATE public.custom_roles` statements and one `DO` guard. Creates no object, drops nothing, re-issues no function, writes no learner data.
- **The gap it closes.** `/accreditation/cac` shipped 2026-08-01 gating on `accreditation.cac.view`, which was TRUE on **zero** roles — so the CAC dashboard was reachable only by the 14 super admins, through the `is_super_admin()` bypass rather than through any grant. `accreditation.*` as a family sat on the `ceo` role alone. Director decision 9 (2026-08-01), role keys confirmed 2026-08-02: `accreditation_officer`, `principal`, `hod`, `registrar`, `coo`.
- **Six READ keys to the five named roles** (`accreditation.view`, `.metrics.view`, `.coverage.view`, `.cac.view`, `.evidence.view`, `.naac.narrative.view`) and **one WRITE key to IQAC alone** (`accreditation.naac.narrative.manage`). That write key is what `accred_metric_owners_manage` uses for both USING and WITH CHECK on `accreditation_metric_owners`, i.e. it is the assign-an-owner control. IQAC assigns; principals and HODs confirm what they are given, so they get `.view` and deliberately not `.manage` — otherwise a department could reassign ownership of another department's criterion. It is also the delivery list for the narrative escalation reminder (20260727130000), so scoping it to IQAC keeps that notification aimed at people who can act on it.
- **Scoped by explicit `role_key IN (...)`, never by a rule.** No predicate of the "every role holding X" shape appears, so the migration is structurally incapable of sweeping in a role nobody reviewed.
- 🪤 **`||`, not `jsonb_set`.** For these keys the roles are a MIX — some carry the key explicitly `false`, others do not carry it at all. `jsonb_set(permissions, '{key}', 'true')` without `create_missing` returns the row **unchanged** on the absent case: a silent no-op that leaves half the grant unmade while the migration reports success. `permissions || jsonb_build_object(...)` sets the key in both cases.
- **The guard reads `->>` and never `?`.** `user_has_permission()` tests `(permissions->>key)::boolean = true`; the `?` existence operator returns TRUE for a key stored `false`, so a `?`-based assert would pass on a role that still cannot open the page — the exact misreading that produced a false governance all-clear here before. Section 3 RAISEs unless all 31 (role, key) pairs read the text `'true'`, and reports a **missing role_key as a failure rather than skipping it**. A `RAISE NOTICE` also names any role outside the five that already holds `accreditation.cac.view`, so a pre-existing holder is visible in the apply log rather than silently inherited.
- **Companion (same PR):** `accreditation.evidence.view / .create / .manage` registered in `lib/constants/permissions.ts`. `quality_evidence_mappings` has carried `qem_select`/`qem_insert`/`qem_update` calling `user_has_permission()` on those three keys since `20260417000001_compliance_unification_substrate` — whose own comment says the keys were "expected to be added ... in a follow-up commit. Until then, super_admin bypass handles all testing." The follow-up never came, so the "collect once, report many" ledger has been super-admin-only for ~3.5 months, not by policy but because a key registered nowhere cannot be ticked in Role Management. Registering a key grants it to nobody.
- ⚠ **Not independently re-verified against prod from the build worktree** — the live read of `custom_roles.permissions` was blocked by the permission classifier (it requires the production service-role key). The by-value state is taken from the spec's own live verification; the migration's section-3 guard is the authoritative by-value check and runs at apply time.
### The last two nightly routines: cron identity, and an escalation with no addressee (2026-08-04)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809210000_nightly_cron_identity_and_null_addressee.sql` — **APPLIED to prod 2026-08-04 with Director approval, then proven behaviourally over HTTP.** Re-issues two SECURITY DEFINER functions from their LIVE definitions (`pg_get_functiondef`, captured the same day) with one mechanical edit each; the generator asserted line-by-line that only the lines shown were added and nothing was removed or reordered. Creates no table, grants nothing new, writes no data.
- **`fn_cac_refresh_attendance_rollup` — `HTTP 503 · Not authorised to refresh the CAC attendance rollup`, every night.** `app/api/cron/cac-attendance-rollup/route.ts` calls the RPC through `createServiceRoleClient()`. A service-role client carries no user JWT, so `auth.uid()` is NULL, so `is_super_admin()` and `is_admin()` both correctly return false and the guard correctly refuses. The guard was written for a human caller and the routine has no human. Reproduced before the fix: calling the RPC with the service-role key returned HTTP 403 / `42501` with production's exact message.
- **Adding `auth.role() = 'service_role'` widens nothing.** `service_role` carries `rolbypassrls`, so any holder of that key could already write `cac_attendance_rollup` directly. It is also the mechanism already established in this database — `public.exec_sql` gates on `auth.role() IS DISTINCT FROM 'service_role'` — rather than a new one. `exec_sql` succeeding over the service-role key is itself the proof that `auth.role()` resolves to `'service_role'` on that path. The original `is_super_admin`/`is_admin` branches and the RAISE are untouched, and ASSERT 2 refuses the migration if they go missing.
- **`fn_scf_apply_weekly_escalation_digest` — `null value in column "faculty_email" … violates not-null constraint`.** Its `esc` CTE grouped `session_feedback` by `lower(f.faculty_email)` with no NULL filter, then inserted into `session_feedback_escalations.faculty_email`, which is NOT NULL with no default. A NULL email formed its own group and broke the statement — taking the whole digest down with it, **including every valid escalation in the same run**. The filter is added to BOTH `session_feedback` scans; ASSERT 3 counts them and requires exactly 2.
- **Dropping those rows is the semantics, not a workaround.** An escalation is a message addressed to a person. Measured on prod 2026-08-04: 19,446 of 131,892 `session_feedback` rows (14.7%) carry no `faculty_email`, and `faculty_id` is NULL on **all 19,446**, so no `staff` lookup can recover an address either. When a blank must not count, do not write the row.
- ⚠ **Reported, not fixed — needs a data-capture decision, not code.** Those 19,446 rows are unattributable, so in week 2026-07-27 exactly 2 groups crossed the escalation threshold (`count >= 3 AND avg(understood) < 3`) and **both were unattributable** — CME365 (11 responses) and CME346 (7 responses) escalate to nobody. Zero groups that week had a real addressee, which is why the fixed routine correctly returns `classes_flagged: 0` against 17,431 feedback rows over 350 courses (avg understood 4.12). The digest now RUNS instead of crashing; it still cannot name a Senior Learner who was never recorded.
- **Proved with a negative control.** Dry-run as `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` (the trailing `COMMIT` swapped out — an inner COMMIT turns a dry run into a live apply): clean. The same file with edit 1 deleted was REFUSED by ASSERT 1 (`did not take the service_role branch (found 0)`), so the assertions are not vacuous. Post-apply over HTTP: `cac-attendance-rollup` → `HTTP 200 · institutions_updated 10, total_marks 1,128,250`; `session-feedback-escalation` → `HTTP 200 · classes_flagged 0`.
### IQAC Foundations — programme scope, ownership acknowledgement, reported-vs-actual (2026-08-02)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809100000_iqac_foundations_programme_scope_and_snapshot.sql` — **APPLIED to prod 2026-08-02 with Director approval.** Adds `programme_id` to `quality_evidence_mappings` and `accreditation_metric_owners`, makes `accreditation_metric_owners.metric_code` nullable, adds five acknowledgement/history columns, creates two SECURITY DEFINER read functions, normalises two period labels, and closes the anon table grant on three tables. Rehearsed in `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` with residue re-verified **0** in a separate call before the real apply; every object re-verified afterwards by catalog (`information_schema.columns`, `pg_constraint`, `pg_proc`, `pg_class.relacl`), never by the migration ledger.
- **Two of the spec's own assumptions came back false on the live read, and this file is shaped by the answers.** The spec supposed `accreditation_metric_owners.metric_code` might already be nullable so that body-level ownership needed no DDL — it was `NOT NULL`, so §2 does it here rather than in the ownership-page PR that assumed it. The spec supposed `accreditation_submissions` could carry the reported-vs-actual snapshot as-is — it carries the submission *envelope* (institution × body × period, one `coverage_snapshot numeric`) with no metric code and no per-metric figure, so §6 gives its existing `metadata jsonb` a documented shape instead of adding a second snapshot table beside an empty one.
- **`NULLS NOT DISTINCT` is load-bearing, twice.** Making `metric_code` nullable would otherwise let two competing body-level owners coexist, since standard SQL treats every NULL as distinct — precisely the ambiguity ownership exists to remove. PostgreSQL 15.6 supports it. Both rebuilt constraints use it: `(institution_id, body_code, metric_code, programme_id)` on owners, `(source_table, source_id, body_code, metric_code, programme_id)` on mappings. The mappings key deliberately *permits* the same source row to be claimed once institution-wide and once for a named programme — a paper counts for the college's NAAC return and for that degree's NBA return — while still forbidding two identical institution-level claims.
- **`programme_id` is `ON DELETE CASCADE`, not `SET NULL`.** A programme-level NBA tag whose programme no longer exists is orphaned, not institution-level evidence. `SET NULL` would also collapse two programme rows onto the same NULL and violate the uniqueness rule above.
- **Both new functions are `STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public`, with explicit `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM anon, PUBLIC` and `GRANT … TO authenticated`.** Neither accepts a caller-supplied user id — `fn_accreditation_reported_vs_actual` takes the *institution* being asked about and then checks whether the **session** may see it, because a SECURITY DEFINER function that accepts the user it should act as is an IDOR. Every guard predicate is wrapped in `COALESCE(…, false)`; a NULL guard falls through and grants access.
- ⚠ **Both functions are correct but currently unreachable by anyone except super admins.** They guard on `accreditation.evidence.view`, which the existing RLS on `quality_evidence_mappings` already demands and which is **registered nowhere in `lib/constants/permissions.ts`** — an ungrantable key, so no role can ever hold it. Registering it is the access PR's job, not this one's; noted here so the gap is not mistaken for a bug in these functions.
- **`REVOKE ALL … FROM anon, PUBLIC` on all three tables, asserted in-transaction.** All three were born `anon=arwdDxt` from Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES`. RLS was already stopping anon reading rows, so the live anon sweep read clean before and after — but the table-level grant was one permissive policy away from mattering. §10 fails the migration loudly if the revoke was a no-op or if `authenticated` lost anything. `cockpit_reader`'s existing `SELECT` on `quality_evidence_mappings` is untouched. Live sweep after apply: **10 approved / 0 unapproved · 53 / 0**, unchanged.
- **Period labels normalised by pattern, not by value.** `UPDATE … WHERE period_label ~ '^\d{4}-\d{2}$'` fixed the two stray `2026-27` rows (`AY 2026-27` 86 → 88) and will catch any future bare-year label rather than only the two that existed on the day.
### The named owner may answer, without gaining the power to assign (2026-08-02)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809100600_accreditation_acknowledge_own_ownership.sql` — **APPLIED to prod 2026-08-02 with Director approval.** One VOLATILE SECURITY DEFINER function, `fn_accreditation_acknowledge_ownership(uuid, text)`. Rehearsed in `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` with residue re-verified **0** in a separate call, then verified by catalog (`pg_proc.provolatile='v'`, `prosecdef=true`, `has_function_privilege('anon', …)=false`, `('authenticated', …)=true`). Live anon sweep after apply: **10 approved / 0 unapproved · 53 / 0**, unchanged.
- **What was broken.** Director decision 8 says IQAC assigns and the department CONFIRMS. The ownership page shipped with accept/decline buttons that nobody could reach, behind **two independent locks**: the page gated its whole body on `accreditation.naac.narrative.manage` (true on one role, held by one person), and the only write policy on `accreditation_metric_owners` (`accred_metric_owners_manage`, FOR ALL) demands that same key in USING **and** WITH CHECK — so even past the page the owner's UPDATE came back as a silent zero-row refusal. The 102 HODs and 10 principals who are the intended owners saw an access-denied panel.
- **Why granting `.manage` to principals and HODs would have been the wrong fix.** It unlocks both doors and hands every prospective owner the power to reassign anyone — precisely the imposition decision 8 exists to prevent. Manage is the ASSIGN power; answering is not assigning.
- **Why a function rather than a second RLS policy.** A permissive `FOR UPDATE USING (owner_user_id = auth.uid())` would let the owner answer *and* edit every other column of their row — `owner_user_id` included, so they could hand their accountability to somebody else, or move the row to another institution. **RLS restricts rows and cannot restrict columns.** The function writes exactly three (`assignment_status`, `acknowledged_at`, `acknowledged_by`) and offers no path to any other. Column-level GRANTs were the other candidate and were rejected because `authenticated` already holds a table-wide UPDATE from Supabase's default privileges, so a column grant would have narrowed nothing.
- **Caller identity comes from the session, never from an argument** — the function takes the ownership row id and a decision, then compares `auth.uid()` to that row's `owner_user_id`. A SECDEF function that accepts the user it should act as is an IDOR and 75 of that shape already exist on this database. A row the caller may not answer for raises the same `42501` as a row that does not exist, so a caller cannot probe for existence.
- **Proved behaviourally in `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` before shipping, not just structurally:** a seeded ownership row was answered by a non-owner session and refused with `42501`; an invalid decision value was refused with `22023`. Both assertions had to pass for the block to reach its deliberate final raise. Owner rows re-verified back at **0** afterwards.
- 🪤 **The page's `.select()`-after-write pattern is what surfaced this at all.** A blocked write on this table returns EMPTY rather than an error, so the page asserts on rows returned; without that, the decline would have looked like it worked.
### Named accreditation owner can read their own assignment (2026-08-02)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809100900_accreditation_owner_can_read_own_assignment.sql` — **APPLIED TO PRODUCTION 2026-08-04** under Director authorisation. Replaces the `accred_metric_owners_select` policy on `public.accreditation_metric_owners` so the row that names a person is readable by that person: adds `OR owner_user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())` and changes nothing else. Creates no function, so there is no anon/PUBLIC grant to re-assert; the FOR ALL manage policy (`accreditation.naac.narrative.manage`) is untouched, so assigning stays exactly where it was. Companion to `/accreditation/my-gaps`, which is correct with or without it.
- **Apply receipt (2026-08-04).** Pre-checked that the live SELECT policy was named exactly `accred_metric_owners_select`, so `DROP .. CREATE` replaces it in place instead of leaving a second permissive policy beside it. Rehearsed in `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`; residue verified `0` **in a separate API call**. Verified after apply by catalog (`pg_policies`): still exactly 2 policies on the table, and only the SELECT one carries the `owner_user_id` self-read. Proven behaviourally inside a rollback — an assigned own-scoped HOD reads their own pending row (`is_mine` true) while a different own-scoped HOD reads **0 rows**; residue 0 after. Role scope was NOT lost in the replacement: `pg_policies.roles` reads `{public}` for both policies, matching the untouched `accred_metric_owners_manage` and every sibling accreditation policy (`qem_select`, `submissions_*`), and `anon` holds no grant on the table at all (`relacl` = postgres/authenticated/service_role), so the policy is unreachable for it regardless.
- **Why it is needed.** The live SELECT policy read from `pg_policies` on 2026-08-02 is `is_super_admin() OR is_admin() OR (user_has_permission('accreditation.naac.narrative.view') AND role_has_institution_access(institution_id))` — no clause for the named owner. Measured the same day: `accreditation.view` is true on 6 roles (ceo, registrar, coo, accreditation_officer, principal, hod), `accreditation.naac.narrative.view` on 5 — the same list minus `ceo`. So `ceo`, and any Senior Learner or coordinator IQAC names as an owner, reads **zero** of their own rows. RLS denial is silent, so the worklist cannot tell that apart from owning nothing and would tell an owner nothing was assigned to them while work sat against their name.
- **Narrowest possible widening, not a permission grant.** The added clause is self-scoped and SELECT-only: it reveals rows that already name you and nobody else's workload. It is the missing half of Director decision 8 (2026-08-01), which made `fn_accreditation_acknowledge_ownership` SECURITY DEFINER precisely so an owner could ANSWER an assignment without holding the manage key — but left them unable to SEE what they were answering. Precedent in the same schema: the sibling `accreditation_metric_narratives` SELECT policy has carried `OR owner_user_id = auth.uid()` since `20260725071500`; the owners table was simply never given the matching clause.
- 🪤 **`accreditation.submissions.view` is held by ZERO roles** (live, 2026-08-02), so `accreditation_submissions` — the only source of due dates — reads empty for every non-admin. This file does **not** touch that policy: a due date is institution-wide information, not self-scoped, so the same narrow argument does not apply and widening it is a separate decision. `/accreditation/my-gaps` degrades to "No date set" rather than failing, and never renders a date it could not read.

- `supabase/migrations/20260809011500_mba_case_study_from_improvement_idea.sql` — **NOT APPLIED. A refusal never costs the learner their case; `generated_by` stays at the table default `manual` so the screen's "an AI wrote this draft" banner is never shown over a draft no AI is coming to write. `fn_case_study_grade` now requires `status = 'under_review'` (so a never-submitted draft cannot be graded and a grade cannot be silently overwritten) and refuses the author outright whatever permissions they hold. **Two access rules were corrected on 2026-08-02 after the first dry run.** (1) The job type's `allow_rule` is `permission:improvement.ideas.view`, NOT the sibling's `seat_owner` — `fn_ai_enqueue` resolves `seat_owner` against `ai_model_config.config_json -> 'max_lane_user_ids'` for `feature_key = 'ai_query.natural_language'`, and that allowlist has exactly ONE member against 44 holders of the associate role, so "the AI drafts first" was unreachable for every learner. `permission:%` is an established form already carried by 9 production job types; the seat allowlist itself is untouched because it is a live cost control shared by 48 other job types. (2) `fn_case_study_start` now admits **only the author of the improvement idea** — the previous version also admitted anyone posted to the department, which produced a case bylined to the writer and, under the new SELECT policy, invisible to the learner whose improvement it was, while the UNIQUE index stopped them ever writing their own. Proved in one `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` call: **63/63** checks pass, including both branches of the enqueue, the `enabled=false` kill switch and the `max_inflight` cap firing, every grading refusal, and an unrelated signed-in reader going from **1 row to 0** on another person's draft then back to **1** once it is published. Re-run unchanged against the pre-correction version as a negative control, **15 of those 63 fail** — including a case being started for another learner with no error at all, and `0` AI jobs enqueued for a real associate.
