### IQAC meeting — every member writes their OWN account, the Chairman/Coordinator compiles (2026-08-04)

- `supabase/migrations/20260809101600_iqac_meeting_member_notes.sql` — **FILE ONLY — NOT APPLIED to any database.** Not run against production, not even inside a `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`. Apply is Director-gated. (Version 20260809101600 was allocated to this change up front, so it cannot collide with a sibling lane picking "the next timestamp".)
- **The gap it closes.** `accreditation_committee_meetings` carries ONE `minutes_summary` text column and its only writer is `CommitteeMeetingService.closeMeeting` — one person, one box, at close time. Several members each recording what they took away from a sitting had nowhere to be stored. Measured live 2026-08-04: 1 committee, 1 member row, 2 meetings, **0** meetings with any minutes text.
- **What it adds.** `accreditation_meeting_member_notes` (one row per meeting × author, `UNIQUE (meeting_id, author_user_id)` — which is also the `ON CONFLICT` target the UI upserts on, so the two must never drift or PostgreSQL raises 42P10 at runtime); a BEFORE trigger that **derives** `institution_id` from the parent meeting so a client can never file an account under a college it does not belong to; two STABLE SECURITY DEFINER predicates; four policies; RLS enabled; explicit `REVOKE ALL … FROM anon, PUBLIC` on the table and `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM anon, PUBLIC` + `GRANT … TO authenticated` on both predicates.
- **Why SECURITY DEFINER predicates and not an inline EXISTS.** The policies must consult `accreditation_committee_meetings` / `_committees` / `_members`, and all three are themselves gated on `accreditation.naac.committees.view`. A plain member does not hold that key, so an inline `EXISTS(...)` would silently evaluate FALSE and lock a member out of **their own** note — RLS denial is silent, so it would have looked like "you have not written anything". The predicates read the parent rows as owner and answer honestly. Neither accepts a caller-supplied acting-user id; both derive the caller from `auth.uid()`.
- **Who reads what.** A member reads and writes only their own account. The committee Chairman (`accreditation_committees.chair_user_id` **or** an active member holding role `chair`), the Coordinator, admins, and holders of `accreditation.naac.committees.meetings.manage` within their own institution scope read every account on the sitting. Policy shape is lifted verbatim from the live `accreditation_committee_members` / `_meetings` policies read back from `pg_policies` on 2026-08-04, on the grantable `accreditation.naac.committees.*` family (the one `20260808210001` realigned onto); the self-scoped `author_user_id = auth.uid()` clause mirrors the existing `accreditation_metric_narratives` SELECT policy.
- **Verified behaviourally, on a throwaway local PostgreSQL 16 cluster — never on production.** Stub tables/functions were built from the live column list, then the migration file was applied verbatim and 16 checks run as `SET ROLE authenticated` with `auth.uid()` switched per persona: ordinary member writes their own (1 row); `institution_id` is derived, and a supplied lie is overwritten; author-forgery insert refused **42501**; ordinary member reads exactly **1** row (their own text, not anyone else's); Chairman reads **3**; Coordinator reads **3**; a person with **no note yet reads 0 rows with no error** (an empty box, not a failure); an outsider cannot author (**42501**); a member cannot edit the Chairman's note (`UPDATE 0`) but can revise their own (`UPDATE 1`); the upsert on the declared conflict target succeeds with no 42P10; a `meetings.manage` holder who is not a member reads all **3**; `anon` holds neither table privilege nor EXECUTE on either predicate while `authenticated` holds both; RLS on with exactly 4 policies.
- 🪤 **The substrate is ready before the door is.** Measured live 2026-08-04, only `accreditation_officer` and `ceo` hold `accreditation.naac.committees.view`, and the committee detail page gates on it — so an ordinary member cannot yet reach the page that hosts their own box. This migration grants **no** permission to any role: that is a Director decision in Role Management, deliberately not smuggled into a migration. The table's RLS is written so a member's self-read/self-write works the moment the page becomes reachable, with no further DB change.
- **FK choice, stated so a reviewer can disagree.** `author_user_id` is NOT NULL (the self-read policy has nothing to compare against otherwise) and therefore CASCADEs on profile delete, adding one more table to the profile→auth CASCADE set. The compiled OFFICIAL record lives in `accreditation_committee_meetings.minutes_summary` and survives independently; what disappears is the raw personal note of a person who no longer exists on the platform — which no longer satisfies its own self-read policy in any case.
### Evidence writers institution-scoped — the companion PR #2822 is blocked on (2026-08-09)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809101700_evidence_writers_institution_scoped.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED.** Rebuilds **18** SECURITY DEFINER functions from their **LIVE `pg_get_functiondef`** text (captured from production 2026-08-04) with only the declared predicate changes; a generator asserted every one of its 46 edits matched exactly once, so the emitted body is provably the live body plus nothing else. Creates no table, adds no column, issues **no GRANT**, and **changes no `ON CONFLICT` target** — all 28 evidence targets stay the live five-column `(source_table, source_id, body_code, metric_code, programme_id)`, asserted in-file, because widening them is PR #2822's job and doing it here would raise `42P10` in production.
- **Why it exists.** PR #2822 widens `quality_evidence_mappings_source_scope_key` to include `institution_id`, and its own migration carries an executable `ASSERT 0` that RAISES `REFUSING TO APPLY` while three hazards exist. Measured live 2026-08-04 with #2822's own probes: **19 withdrawal `DELETE`s across 17 functions** with no `institution_id` predicate, **6 catch-up anti-joins** in `fn_accreditation_rollup_loop_evidence()` with none, and **12 `EXCLUDED` institution re-stamps across 11 functions**. Once two colleges can hold a claim on one source row, those become cross-tenant deletion, skipped emission, and fabricated `shared_count` sharing respectively.
- **17 functions, not 16.** `revoke_audit_finding_evidence()` carries a withdrawal and is **not** among the 22 conflict-target writers #2822 rebuilds, so an audit scoped to those 22 cannot see it. The census here was taken over **every** function whose body mentions the table (32), not those 22. Correctly exempt and untouched: the four `*_evidence_cleanup_on_delete` triggers key on `source_id = OLD.id` — the source row itself is being deleted, so removing every college's claim is right there.
- **The COALESCE rule.** Each withdrawal gains exactly one predicate, `AND institution_id = COALESCE(<source row's institution>, institution_id)`. `institution_id` is `NOT NULL`, so a known source institution yields exact tenant scoping and a NULL one yields today's behaviour unchanged — which is correct, because several of these withdrawals fire *precisely because* the source row is gone or has lost its institution, and an unattributable source cannot be legitimately claimed by anybody. Narrowing those to a NULL would turn the withdrawal into a silent no-op and strand the stale claim forever. Never weaker than what ships today; the fallback is stated rather than hidden because it is the one place this is weaker than "always scoped".
- **The re-stamp replacement.** All 12 `institution_id = EXCLUDED.institution_id` assignments are removed and replaced by an explicit withdraw-stale-claim-then-insert step immediately before each INSERT, written `NOT (institution_id = X)` rather than `<>` on purpose: #2822's `ASSERT 0` recognises only `institution_id = / IN` as a tenant predicate and would report `<>` as unscoped. The literal assignment text is deliberately absent from every comment too — that probe reads `pg_get_functiondef`, comments included.
- **Proved behaviourally on production inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`, not just structurally.** With #2822's six-column arbiter simulated and both CAS twins holding a claim on one `cdc_training_programmes` row: **before**, college A's withdrawal left `A_rows=0 B_rows=0` — it deleted college B's claim; **after**, `A_rows=0 B_rows=1` — B survived. The catch-up anti-join, evaluated old-text vs new-text on identical rows, went `emits=false` → `emits=true` for college A's own source row. Under the still-live five-column key an A→B re-assignment ends `total=1 at_A=0 at_B=1` both before and after, so the correction path has **no regression today**. Residue re-verified **in a separate call**: arbiter still five-column, 11,608 rows unchanged, 0 synthetic rows, and the md5 bundle of all 32 live definitions byte-identical to the pre-rehearsal capture. #2822's unscoped-DELETE probe still reads **19** against live production and read **0** inside the rehearsal — which is also the non-vacuity proof for the in-file assertions.
- ⚠️ **ORDERING — a human must resolve this before either file is applied.** This file is `20260809101700`; #2822's is `20260809101400`, which sorts **earlier**. On a from-scratch replay #2822 would widen the arbiter first and these five-column bodies would then **silently revert it** — `CREATE OR REPLACE` does not validate an `ON CONFLICT` target at creation time, so the revert stays invisible until the first runtime `42P10`. A §0 guard makes that loud instead: this file **refuses to apply** when the six-column arbiter is already live. Resolve by renumbering this file below `20260809101400`, or by applying it first and regenerating #2822 from the post-companion live definitions (which #2822's own header already requires as its step 2). No CI job in this repo runs `supabase db reset` (checked 2026-08-04 — the only apply path is `supabase-migration-apply.yml`, `workflow_dispatch`), so the hard guard cannot break a build.
- 🔎 **Defect found in #2822's gate, must be fixed when #2822 is regenerated.** Its `v_restamp` probe is **table-blind** — it matches `institution_id = EXCLUDED.institution_id` in any public function with no reference to `quality_evidence_mappings`. Live it counts 14, of which **three are unrelated**: `fn_ai_pulse_measure_cycle_outcomes` (`ON CONFLICT (cycle_id, dept_id)`), `fn_learner_360_record_verdict` (`ON CONFLICT (learner_id, verdict_date)`) and `link_pre_registered_profile` (`ON CONFLICT (id)` on `profiles`). Each re-stamps `institution_id` on its own key, correctly, and none is affected by this widening — so even with this companion applied, #2822's gate still reports 3 and still refuses. Narrow it to functions whose definition also mentions the table. This file asserts the **narrowed** count is zero.
- 🔎 **#2822's "7 of 11 catch-up anti-joins" does not survive reading the definitions.** Ground truth from all 32 bodies: 13 `NOT EXISTS` in total — **6** are catch-up anti-joins against `quality_evidence_mappings` (all in `fn_accreditation_rollup_loop_evidence`, all unscoped, all six fixed here), 5 are `institutions` FK-existence guards that are not catch-ups at all, 1 is a `service_types` seed guard, and 1 is a scoped narratives anti-join in the read-only `fn_accreditation_narrative_awaiting`. The likely arithmetic behind "7": `fn_sync_bos_meeting_evidence`'s guard reads `i.id = m.institutions_id` — note **`institutions_id`**, which does not contain the substring `institution_id`, so a text probe scores it unscoped. It is an FK existence check and cannot cause a cross-college skip. The real number to fix was 6.
- 🪤 **Left alone deliberately, flagged for a human.** `revoke_audit_finding_evidence()` deletes **without** `AND is_auto` — it is provenance-scoped by `metadata->>'audit_finding_id'` instead, so a manually-curated mapping carrying that key would be destroyed. Out of scope for this PR (it is not one of the three hazards) and untouched here; worth a separate decision. `emit_audit_finding_evidence()` uses `DO NOTHING`, so audit-finding evidence has no institution-correction path at all, before or after this change.
### Committee access follows the roster, not the job title (2026-08-09)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809102300_committee_roster_access.sql` — **✅ APPLIED to production 2026-08-05** (by hand via the Management API, Director-approved at the session gate; rehearsed in `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`, residue verified 0 in a separate call, then verified by catalog). ⚠️ The migration ledger has NO row for it — hand-applied SQL never writes the ledger — so verify by CATALOG, never by the ledger. Catalog proof: `fn_user_is_committee_member(uuid)` exists, SECURITY DEFINER, `anon` cannot EXECUTE; all four committee tables carry a roster-aware SELECT policy. Behaviourally proven with a paired control — the same person, same institution, went 0 committees -> 1 purely by gaining a roster row. Director decision 8. Adds one SECURITY DEFINER helper, `fn_user_is_committee_member(uuid)` (identity from `auth.uid()` inside the function, never a parameter; `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM anon, PUBLIC` + `GRANT … TO authenticated`), and appends it as an `OR` arm to exactly four SELECT policies: `committees_select`, `members_select`, `acm_select`, `acr_select`. **No write policy is touched** — a roster seat buys READ of your committee, its roster, its meetings and its resolutions, nothing more. SECURITY DEFINER is load-bearing: `members_select` calls a helper that reads the table that policy guards, which under SECURITY INVOKER is infinite recursion. External members never match (`is_external = false` + `user_id IS NOT NULL`), and "active" means `is_active = true` and deliberately not a `term_end` test — `listMembers()` uses exactly that predicate to decide who the UI shows as a sitting member, and a stricter gate would refuse the page to someone reading their own name on the roster.
- **The roster arm carries no institution conjunct, on purpose.** Measured on production 2026-08-05: the single committee is filed under `b0b8a724…` (Arts and Science (Self)) while its only roster member — the chair — has `profiles.institution_id = 183847c5…`. Granting that chair `accreditation.naac.committees.view` would still not let them in, because the permission arm is `user_has_permission(…) AND role_has_institution_access(institution_id)`. Being named on the roster IS the scope; that is what a cross-college council means.
- ⚠️ **ORDERING.** `20260808210001_accreditation_committee_rls_naac_permission_family.sql` is also file-only and also rewrites `committees_select` / `members_select`. It sorts earlier, so a from-scratch replay is correct — but applying it AFTER this file would silently drop the roster arm, since `ALTER POLICY` replaces the whole expression. This file writes its four policies in full and already uses the grantable `accreditation.naac.committees.*` family, so it is correct whether or not that one has been applied.
- 🔎 **The verification that matters is §3c, and it cannot be run yet.** Structure passing proves nothing here: RLS denial is silent, so "0 rows, no error" is the expected output of both success-with-no-data and total denial. §3c is a LIMIT-1 readability probe run as a real roster member holding no accreditation permission, requiring a row back from all four tables. As of 2026-08-05 production has 1 committee, 1 active member, 0 external members, 2 meetings, 0 resolutions — and that one member is a **super admin**, who already had access. There is currently no non-privileged member to prove it with. Run §3c the first time a real member is added to a roster; that is the moment this migration stops being inert.

### Member notes survive a leaver, with the author's name on them (2026-08-09)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809102500_member_notes_survive_leaver.sql` — **✅ APPLIED to production 2026-08-05** (by hand via the Management API, Director-approved at the session gate; rehearsed in `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`, residue verified 0 in a separate call, then verified by catalog). ⚠️ The migration ledger has NO row for it — hand-applied SQL never writes the ledger — so verify by CATALOG, never by the ledger. Catalog proof: `author_name`/`author_email` exist, `author_user_id` is nullable, and its FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL`. Behaviourally proven: after deleting the author's profile the note survived, still attributed to its author. Apply is Director-gated. (Version 20260809102500 allocated up front so it cannot collide with a sibling lane picking "the next timestamp".) Implements Director decision 7 — *"Member notes survive a leaver, with the author's name on them. The record does not change because someone left."*
- **Why it exists: the decision was believed already satisfied by `20260809101600`, and is not.** Read back from the live catalogue 2026-08-05: `accreditation_meeting_member_notes` is `(id, meeting_id, author_user_id, note_text, institution_id, created_at, updated_at)` and `accreditation_meeting_member_notes_author_user_id_fkey` is `FOREIGN KEY (author_user_id) REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`. **Both** halves fail on that shape: CASCADE means deleting a departing member's profile *deletes their notes*, and there is no stored name to attribute a surviving note to — the panel resolved the author by joining `profiles` at read time, which returns nothing once the profile is gone. `20260809101600`'s header states the CASCADE choice openly and invites a reviewer to disagree; this file is that disagreement, applied.
- **What it changes.** Adds `author_name` / `author_email` — a **snapshot** of the author taken at write time, denormalised on purpose so attribution outlives the profile row (readers must never re-resolve it by joining `profiles`); backfills that snapshot for every existing row and `RAISE NOTICE`s the count, plus a `RAISE WARNING` for any row left with no snapshot at all; drops `NOT NULL` on `author_user_id` and rebuilds its FK as **`ON DELETE SET NULL`** so the note outlives the person.
- **The write path is the EXISTING trigger, extended — not a parallel mechanism.** `fn_accreditation_meeting_note_stamp_institution()` already derived `institution_id` from the parent meeting; it now also stamps the author snapshot from `profiles`, authoritatively, so a client can neither file an account under a college it does not belong to nor sign it with somebody else's name. `SECURITY DEFINER` + `SET search_path = public` retained, and `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM anon, PUBLIC` is **re-asserted in the same file** because `CREATE OR REPLACE` is a fresh grant surface. The trigger *definition* (`BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF meeting_id`) is deliberately untouched: `ON DELETE SET NULL` issues an UPDATE of `author_user_id` only, which is not in that column list, so a departure cannot fire the function and cannot erase the snapshot it exists to preserve. The `ELSE` branch guards the same hazard a second time.
- **No policy is created, dropped or altered, and that is checked rather than trusted.** The live SELECT policy is `author_user_id = auth.uid() OR fn_accreditation_meeting_note_can_read_all(meeting_id)`. With `author_user_id` NULL the first clause evaluates to NULL — never TRUE, so an orphaned note leaks to nobody — while the second still admits the Chairman, the Coordinator, admins, and `accreditation.naac.committees.meetings.manage` holders in scope, i.e. exactly the people who compile the minutes and the reason the note has to survive. A §5 `DO` block **refuses to apply** if no SELECT policy on this table consults `can_read_all`, since that clause is the only thing standing between a departure and an unreadable orphan. The check is scoped to this one table and this one policy, so it cannot become permanently unsatisfiable for an unrelated reason.
- **`UNIQUE (meeting_id, author_user_id)` is untouched** and stays the `ON CONFLICT` target the UI upserts on. NULLs are distinct in a UNIQUE index, so several departed members' notes coexist on one sitting — the wanted behaviour — and the upsert path only ever supplies a non-NULL author.
- **UI half, shipped in the same PR.** `MeetingMemberNote.author_user_id` is now `string | null`; attribution reads the snapshot **first** via `noteAuthorSnapshotLabel()`, falling back to a live profile only for rows written before the snapshot existed. A departed author's card carries a "Former member" badge, is never mistaken for the signed-in member's own box, and still reaches the compiled minutes under their own name (the compile path keys attribution by **note id**, not author id — keying by a shared NULL would collapse two departed members onto one heading).
- **Tested at the boundary this repo owns, and proved non-vacuous.** `__tests__/app/accreditation/member-notes-panel.test.tsx` feeds the panel the post-departure row shape (`author_user_id: null`, no `profiles` row, snapshot present) and asserts the note is still shown, still named, still compiled. It deliberately does **not** re-implement the FK rule and then agree with itself. Disabling snapshot-first attribution turns 3 of the new tests red and the rest green — measured, not assumed. The database half (that the row survives the DELETE at all) is behavioural and is step (d) of the file's verification block, to be run as a real user after a Director-approved apply.
### One person, a leadership post at MORE THAN ONE college (2026-08-05)
- `supabase/migrations/20260809102100_institution_leadership_posts.sql` — **✅ APPLIED to production 2026-08-05** (by hand via the Management API, Director-approved at the session gate; rehearsed in `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`, residue verified 0 in a separate call, then verified by catalog). ⚠️ The migration ledger has NO row for it — hand-applied SQL never writes the ledger — so verify by CATALOG, never by the ledger. Catalog proof: `public.institution_leadership` exists with RLS enabled and 4 policies; `fn_list_leadership_candidates` exists; all 3 leadership functions deny `anon` EXECUTE. Behaviourally proven: the EAO named Dr Dhanasekar Principal of Allied Health while he remained Principal of Dental, and all sitting principals still resolved via the derived fallback. Apply is Director-gated, and it **requires `20260809101500_college_leadership.sql` (itself still NOT APPLIED) to be applied first** — a §0 guard RAISES `REFUSING TO APPLY` when `fn_college_leadership_can_manage(uuid)` is absent, because `CREATE OR REPLACE` does not resolve the functions a body calls and an out-of-order apply would otherwise fail at the first click instead. **Director decision 5:** Dr Dhanasekar Balakrishnan is Principal of JKKN Dental College AND of JKKN College of Allied Health Sciences — today unrecord**able**, not merely unrecorded. `user_roles` is `(id, user_id, role_id, is_primary, assigned_at, assigned_by)` with **no institution column**, so `principal` is ONE GLOBAL row per person; `fn_get_college_leadership` derived "Principal of college X" by crossing that row with the **single-valued** `profiles.institution_id`, and `fn_set_college_leadership` RAISED `check_violation` when the two disagreed. One college per person was therefore arithmetic, not policy — and widening the write guard alone would not have helped, because the READ would still have resolved him at whichever one college his profile named.
- **What it adds.** `public.institution_leadership` (one row per college × post, `position IN (principal, vice_principal)` only — the other three positions already have college-scoped homes and a second place to look for the same fact is how estates drift), a PARTIAL unique index `(institution_id, position) WHERE is_active` so vacating is a flip rather than a delete and "who was Principal when this NAAC cycle was signed off" stays answerable, RLS enabled with the four standard `is_super_admin() OR is_admin() OR (user_has_permission('organizations.leadership.manage') AND role_has_institution_access(institution_id))` policies, and one new function `fn_list_leadership_candidates(uuid)`.
- 🔴 **The derived fallback is load-bearing and is NOT optional.** Ten people hold `principal` in production and NONE has an `institution_leadership` row, because the table does not exist yet. Both principal/vice_principal reads are `COALESCE(explicit row, the pre-existing derived query copied VERBATIM)`. Proved by mutation: strip the second COALESCE arm and a sitting Principal reads back `null` — all 10 colleges would go dark the day this is applied. **It does not backfill**: inventing 10 rows would assert an assignment nobody made, with an `assigned_by` nobody is. The first row appears the first time a human uses the screen.
- **Vacate is the whole point.** The explicit post is retired for THIS college only, and the global `user_roles` row is deleted ONLY when the outgoing holder holds the post at no other college — by an explicit row elsewhere, or by the derived route (their profile names a different college). Deleting it because they were replaced at one college would blank every other. The `user_roles` grant is `ON CONFLICT (user_id, role_id) DO UPDATE` (**not** `DO NOTHING`): a sitting Principal at a second college already has that row, so a plain INSERT raises 23505 — and `DO NOTHING` would leave them with no primary role at all, because the demotion immediately above has just cleared it. Eligibility widens to `profiles.institution_id = X` **OR** an active `user_institution_access` row; neither still refuses outright, naming the person and the college.
- 🪤 **The picker was the other half of the lock.** `app/(routes)/organizations/leadership/page.tsx` read `profiles` with `.eq('institution_id', institutionId)` — the exact filter that hid Dr Dhanasekar from the Allied Health picker. It now calls `fn_list_leadership_candidates`, which returns precisely the set the write path accepts, SECURITY DEFINER because `user_institution_access` is not readable by a college officer and RLS denial is silent. A widened write path nobody can reach through the picker is not a fix.
- **Proved behaviourally, never on production.** `__tests__/organizations/institution-leadership-posts.test.ts` creates a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 database, applies BOTH migration files **verbatim with `psql`** (nothing re-implemented in TypeScript — a test that models the SQL only proves the model agrees with itself), and runs **15 checks**: all 10 principals still resolve with `institution_leadership` empty; Dhanasekar reads as Principal of Allied Health AND of Dental with exactly ONE global role row; the previous Allied Health incumbent is retired there and, holding it nowhere else, loses the role row; re-naming him raises no 23505; vacating Allied Health leaves Dental intact; an unattached person is refused `23514` with both names in the message and nothing written; a deactivated grant is still a refusal; `anon` holds no EXECUTE on any of the three functions and no table privilege, `authenticated` holds SELECT but not INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, RLS on. **Not run by CI** (no workflow covers this path) and deliberately loud rather than skipped when no local PostgreSQL is reachable. **Non-vacuity control:** the same assignment against the base migration alone is REFUSED with `belongs to a different institution`, and both new objects are absent.
- **Grants no permission to any role.** `organizations.leadership.manage` stays held by nobody; who holds it is a Director decision in Role Management, not something smuggled into a migration.
- `20260812000000_lock_gemba_lapse_ledger_writes.sql` — revoke the default `authenticated` write grant on `gemba_official_lapse_notices`; reads stay RLS-scoped, writes go through `fn_gemba_official_lapse_notify` only.
- `supabase/migrations/20260813000000_meeting_prefs_note_in_title.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED.** Adds `meeting_host_integration_prefs.show_note_in_title boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` (idempotent `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`; no function created or replaced, so no EXECUTE grant to re-assert; the column inherits the table's existing `mhip_host_all` RLS). 27 of 40 bookings carry a guest-written discussion note in `meeting_bookings.answers->>'note'` that was displayed nowhere — the note now ALWAYS rides in the Google Calendar event body, which needs no column and no setting. This column only controls the opt-in to ALSO put it in the event TITLE, default off because the guest is an attendee and the title is their lock-screen surface. Both readers treat a missing column as false (`getIntegrationPrefs` retries without it on `42703` and hides the toggle; `NativeSchedulingService.resolveShowNoteInTitle` reads it on its own so provider resolution is never disturbed), so the code half is safe to deploy before this file is applied.
- `20260813010000_seed_default_meeting_type_four_hosts.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED.** Four booking pages (`gobinath-k`, `mohanraj-v`, `mr-ravishankar-s`, and the CEO's `rangarajan-r`) are `is_public = true` and reachable while their host has **zero** rows in `meeting_types` — not inactive or hidden ones, none — so a visitor reaches a working page with nothing to book. Seeds exactly one `quick-10` / '10-minute meeting' / `duration_min = 10` type per host, `ON CONFLICT (host_profile_id, slug) DO NOTHING`. Sufficient because all four **already** have 1 schedule, 5-6 availability windows and 1 active Google Calendar connection (verified live) — the type was the only missing piece. Does not flip `is_public`, seed a fifth host, or touch any existing row.

Under a CHECK, the UI needs a hardcoded code→behaviour map; add a value to the CHECK without touching that map and the new basis silently inherits whatever the default branch says — which is "a future admin may reasonably assume the successor inherits it", the very failure this file exists to prevent, reintroduced one level up. Carrying the semantic as a column makes the wrong assumption unrepresentable, and a third basis becomes one INSERT with no migration and no deploy. (`institution_leadership.position` stays a CHECK on purpose: that set is closed by design.)

NULL means "not recorded", the screen says so in those words, and an unrecorded basis is never rendered as ex officio. `basis_note` holds the reason AND the end condition as prose because "till he moves out of JKKN" is a **condition, not a date**; a `timestamptz` could not hold it and an invented date would eventually be acted on.
- 🛑 **The derived fallback survives, and that is proved rather than asserted.** Measured live 2026-08-05: **twelve** `principal` `user_roles` rows across **ten** distinct institutions, plus the one explicit row — eleven colleges answer "who is Principal?" through the derived arm or that single row. Each derived arm is **reproduced byte-identically** from `20260809102100` and decorated with `|| jsonb_build_object(…nulls…)` rather than retyped into a longer `jsonb_build_object`; a `||` cannot alter the query it decorates. The joins to the vocabulary and to the appointer's profile are **LEFT** joins — an INNER join would drop the only explicit row there is (its basis is unrecorded), and Allied Health would fall through to a derived arm that resolves nobody, since Dr Dhanasekar's profile names Dental.

The four original parameters keep their names, order and types, so the page's existing 4-argument named call is unaffected and **the code half deploys safely in either order**.
- **An unknown or retired basis is REFUSED (`23503`), never silently dropped**, as is a basis on a post that has nowhere to keep one (`22023` — IQAC bearers and HoDs are stored elsewhere). A re-save that supplies no basis **preserves** the recorded one while the holder is unchanged, and takes exactly what was supplied when the holder changes: a reason recorded about one person cannot describe another.

Everything resolves by **email**, never a pasted UUID. It refuses to invent: no profile / no institution / he no longer holds the role → `RAISE WARNING` and write nothing; a live Education row naming somebody else → left entirely alone, because a migration must not smuggle in a leadership change.

Catalog proof (re-verified 2026-08-06): `fn_user_is_committee_member(p_committee_id uuid)` exists, and `accreditation_committee_members.term_end` is `is_nullable = NO` **with** a DEFAULT expression — the safe shape, since NOT NULL without a default would have refused every machine write path that omits it. ⚠️ This entry read "FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED" until 2026-08-06; that was **stale**, not a fresh apply. **Director decision 7 (2026-08-05):** *"Committee access must be cut off AUTOMATICALLY on the member's term end date, and a term end date must be REQUIRED when adding a member."* Adds one conjunct to `fn_user_is_committee_member(uuid)` — which four SELECT policies call, so the single edit ends access to the committee, its roster, its meetings **and** its resolutions on the same day. Gives `accreditation_committee_members.term_end` a DEFAULT and NOT NULL, and appends one own-seat disjunct to `members_select`.
- 🛑 **The trap, and why the predicate is not the obvious one.** Before the 2026-08-05 backfill 100% of roster rows had `term_end IS NULL`. `m.term_end >= current_date` is NULL for a NULL term_end, and NULL is not TRUE — written that way this file would have locked out **every committee member on the platform**, and silently, since RLS denial here returns 0 rows with `error = null` and renders as "this committee has no members". The predicate is `AND (m.term_end IS NULL OR m.term_end >= current_date)` and the `IS NULL` arm is **permanent**, not scaffolding: any future path that lands a row with no end date must fail OPEN on read, never closed. The file says so in a comment block headed *DO NOT "TIDY AWAY" THE `IS NULL` ARM*, and a test asserts that warning still exists. `>=` not `>`: the term end date is the last day of the term, inclusive.
- ⚖️ **It overturns a decision recorded in its own predecessor, deliberately.** `20260809102300_committee_roster_access.sql` lines 87-94 state the opposite in as many words — *"ACTIVE means is_active = true, and deliberately NOT 'term_end has not passed' … Adding a term_end test here would let the roster render somebody as a sitting member while the database refuses them the page."* Decision 7 overrules the conclusion, **not the hazard**, which is why this file has four sections instead of one: the hazard is neutralised rather than ignored.
- 🔴 **The DEFAULT is load-bearing — without it this migration breaks a LIVE write path.** `public.fn_set_college_leadership(uuid,text,uuid,uuid)` is SECURITY DEFINER, deployed on production **today**, and is what the College Leadership screen calls when somebody is named IQAC Coordinator; its INSERT names no `term_end` column at all. A bare NOT NULL would raise 23502 at the first click — the "green migration, broken product" shape. The default is the 31 March on or after the insert date (the Indian academic year end, and the exact date the Director's own backfill chose for all three existing rows). **Measured, not assumed:** that RPC's INSERT run verbatim under the new default returned `term_end = 2027-03-31`, no 23502.
- 👁️ **§4 is what stops an expiry becoming a blank page.** One disjunct — `user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())` — is appended to `members_select` so an EXPIRED member can still read **their own seat row and nothing else**, which is the only way the UI can name the date their term ended instead of showing them the generic "you are on no roster" refusal (false) or falling through to `notFound()` (worse). Proved: an expired member reads 1 row — their own — plus **0** other members' rows, **0** committees and **0** meetings; a signed-in non-member reads 0 of everything. No write policy is touched; `members_insert/update/delete` still require `accreditation.naac.committees.edit`.
- 🧪 **Proved behaviourally against production, never structurally.** In `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`, as a real signed-in member (`profiles.role = 'principal'`, `is_super_admin = false`, role does not grant `accreditation.naac.committees.view`, simulated with `SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated` + `request.jwt.claims`): term in the FUTURE → **1** committee visible; the **same member** with the term in the PAST → **0**; the same member with `term_end` NULL → **1** (the safety net); `term_end` = today → **1** (the boundary day is inside the term). `is_super_admin()`, `is_admin()` and `user_has_permission(...)` were all **false in every row**, so the roster arm is provably the only thing that ever let them in. Residue verified 0 afterwards in a separate call — 3 rows, all still `2027-03-31`, function unchanged, column still nullable, policy unchanged.
- **UI half, shipped in the same PR.** The Add-member dialog carries a **required** Term end date (prefilled to the same 31 March the DB default uses, still editable); `AddInternalMemberPayload.term_end` / `AddExternalMemberPayload.term_end` are `string`, not `string | null`, so omitting one is a compile error. `useMyCommitteeRoster` now returns `{committeeId, termEnd}` seats instead of bare ids, and `decideCommittee*Access()` refuse an expired seat with a dated sentence naming the Chairman. The members table gained a **Term end** column with a "Term ended" badge, so a manager's list agrees with what the database enforces — the exact desynchronisation the predecessor warned about. 40 vitest assertions, proved non-vacuous by three mutants: inverting the NULL safety net kills 3, `>=`→`>` kills 1, and letting expired seats fall through to the generic refusal kills 6.

### Which awarding bodies apply to which college (2026-08-06)
- `supabase/migrations/20260816010000_institution_accreditation_bodies.sql` — **APPLIED 2026-08-06** by hand via the Supabase Management API after Director approval. **RENUMBERED from `20260814020000` on 2026-08-06** to clear a three-way collision: while this PR was open, two other branches merged their own `20260814020000_*` files to main (`restore_user_has_permission_execute_grant`, `upgrade_frees_old_bed`), which would have made three files share one version. This file was the one renumbered because the other two are already merged and this one was not, and because re-running it is a no-op — `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS` before every CREATE, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` on both seeds, and zero DELETE/TRUNCATE/DROP TABLE statements. **Applied under the OLD version number; the database is unchanged by the rename.** Rehearsed first in `BEGIN..ROLLBACK` (the file carries its own `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;` at lines 52/411, which were stripped for the rehearsal so the ROLLBACK would hold), residue verified 0 in a **separate** call, then applied and **verified by catalog**: 2 new tables, 6 FKs, **0 hardcoded ten-value CHECK constraints left**, 15 bodies, 35 mappings, and `anon` holding no grant on either new table. Behaviourally proven as Super Administrator against production data — Engineering shows 5 bodies and a denominator of **96, not 107**; the Matric school shows MATRIC only, no NAAC. A §0 guard RAISES `REFUSING TO APPLY` when `public.institutions`, `role_has_institution_access(uuid)` or `user_has_permission(text)` is absent. **The bug it closes is a WRONG DENOMINATOR, not clutter:** `/accreditation/manage/owners` showed all ten awarding bodies to every institution, so JKKN College of Engineering was asked to name an accountable person for Dental Council, Pharmacy Council, Nursing Council and teacher-education metrics — and because 7 of the 107 active metrics (DCI 2 + INC 2 + PCI 2 + NCTE 1) can never apply to an engineering college, "0 of 107" was unreachable by construction and that college could never show 100%. **It could not simply be filtered:** verified live 2026-08-06, no institution-to-body mapping table existed anywhere (`bos_body_types` is Board of Studies COMMITTEE types, unrelated), `institutions` records nothing about what discipline a college teaches, and `sh_accreditation_metrics.metric_type` **IS** the body (there is no `body_code` column on that table).
- **Adds two tables.** `accreditation_bodies` (`code` TEXT **PK** — every consumer already stores the code as text, so a surrogate uuid would mean rewriting five `body_code` columns or carrying a join nobody asked for; plus `name`, `short_name`, `kind`, `source_url`, `notes`, `is_active`, `sort_order`), seeded with all **15**: the existing ten plus **NCAHP, CBSE, MATRIC, ABET, THE**. And `institution_accreditation_bodies` (`institution_id` → institutions, `body_code` → the registry, `is_active`, `notes`, `UNIQUE (institution_id, body_code)`), seeded with the Director's mapping for the 10 accredited institutions.
- 🔑 **It RETIRES five hardcoded CHECK constraints and that is the point.** `quality_evidence_mappings`, `accreditation_committees`, `accreditation_submissions`, `accreditation_digest_config` and `accreditation_metric_crosswalk` each carried the SAME ten-value list — so adding NCAHP needed a migration against five tables. Each CHECK is dropped and replaced with an FK to `accreditation_bodies(code)` (`ON UPDATE CASCADE ON DELETE RESTRICT`), after which a sixteenth body is one INSERT with no migration and no deploy. The drop matches on the constraint **DEFINITION** (`pg_get_constraintdef ILIKE '%body_code%' AND ILIKE '%NAAC%'`), not on a name, because all five were created inline with auto-generated names that a later column change could have renumbered. Every FK validates without a failing row precisely because the CHECK guaranteed it until the moment it was dropped. Each table is guarded with `to_regclass` — this repository's ledger has diverged from the repository and a table named here may be absent in some environments.
- ⚠️ **`institutions.accredited_by` is LEFT COMPLETELY UNTOUCHED, and is now legacy / display-only.** It is a single free-text value ('NAAC' on 8 colleges **and** on JKKN Testing Institution, 'CBSE' on Nattraja Vidhyalya, '' on 4 others) and structurally cannot express a college answering to five bodies. The new mapping is authoritative; retiring the column is a separate reviewed change.
- ⚠️ **UGC is deliberately mapped to NOBODY** (Director decision, flagged not forgotten — UGC oversight commonly sits at university rather than college level), and **MATRIC's `name` is a working label, not the registered name of the board** — its `notes` says so in as many words and it must be corrected before it appears on anything filed. The five new bodies have **zero metrics** between them; creating the body is the small half and defining what it measures is scoped separately.
- 🛑 **DELETES NOTHING.** The four non-colleges and two schools hold NAAC evidence across `coe_naac_evidence`, `hr_naac_evidence`, `facility_teaching_naac_evidence`, `event_feedback_naac_evidence` and `sustainability_naac_evidence`. Those rows become DORMANT, not wrong; delete-vs-dormant is a Director decision, not a side effect of a mapping. `accreditation_metric_owners` had **0 rows platform-wide** when this was written and already carried a `body_code` column, so no owner row is orphaned — the zero-risk moment.
- 🔒 **Grants and RLS.** `REVOKE ALL … FROM anon, PUBLIC, authenticated` **before** granting back, because Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` gives every new table `arwdDxt` to anon AND authenticated and a bare `GRANT SELECT` would be a silent no-op. No DELETE on the registry (a retired body is deactivated, never destroyed). RLS on both. The registry is readable by every authenticated user (fifteen public regulator names are a vocabulary, not a record) and writable on `accreditation.bodies.manage`; the mapping is read-scoped by `role_has_institution_access(institution_id)` and written on that key **plus** the same institution scope. Creates no SECURITY DEFINER function, so there is no EXECUTE grant to re-assert.
- ✅ **The code half is deploy-safe BEFORE the apply, and starts filtering the moment it lands — no second deploy.** Every reader resolves a failed read to an `unprovisioned` scope that shows every body exactly as the pages do today. Failing OPEN is the argued direction: a scope filter that failed closed would hide 96 real metrics from a college that has them, and RLS denial and a missing table are indistinguishable (both return nothing), so an empty result is never rendered as "this college answers to nobody". 16 vitest assertions in `__tests__/accreditation/institution-body-scope.test.ts` pin the arithmetic (Engineering 96, not 107) rather than the rendered list — a list-only assertion passes against the half-fix that leaves "of 107" in place. Proved non-vacuous by two mutants: neutering the filter kills 3 assertions, collapsing `unprovisioned` into "answers to nobody" kills 1.
- `20260814000000_quick10_breathing_gap.sql` — **⚠️ SUPERSEDED BY 20260814010000 — set the wrong column.** `buffer_after` alone does NOT protect the slot immediately after a meeting; `buffer_before` does. Its real availability cost was never measured in isolation — the 14-day slot totals were only ever captured with `after=5` already applied, so "no-op" is unproven either way; treat this entry's original rationale as incorrect, not as a measured result. **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED BY CI.** Gives the four seeded `quick-10` booking types (gobinath-k, mohanraj-v, mr-ravishankar-s, and the CEO's rangarajan-r) a 5-minute `buffer_after_min`. Seeded via 20260813010000 they inherited the table default of 0, so a visitor could chain 10:00-10:10, 10:10-10:20, 10:20-10:30 with no wrap-up or walking time on a campus where walking costs minutes. Scoped by BOTH slug and explicit host list; idempotent (skips rows already at 5); changes nothing else — not duration, not is_active, not is_public, not notice or horizon.
- `20260814010000_quick10_gap_use_before_buffer.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED BY CI.** Corrects 20260814000000, which set the wrong column. The slot engine pads the CANDIDATE (`candStart = start − bufferBefore`, `candEnd = start + duration + bufferAfter`) and tests it against busy time, so `buffer_after` does NOT stop a back-to-back booking after an existing meeting — `buffer_before` does. Confirmed live: with 0/0 buffers the public slots API offered 11:35 while 11:20–11:35 was already booked. Sets `buffer_before_min = 5` on the same four seeded `quick-10` types (keeping `buffer_after_min = 5`), giving five protected minutes on each side. Idempotent; changes nothing else.
