### The CEO could not open the council dashboard (2026-08-13)
- `supabase/migrations/20260830010000_cac_open_to_ceo_and_managing_director.sql` — **NOT APPLIED to any database — Director-gated apply.** ONE `UPDATE public.custom_roles` statement and one `DO` guard. Creates no object, drops nothing, re-issues no function, writes no learner data, and touches no table other than `custom_roles`.
- 🔑 **Principals are deliberately NOT granted here (Director, 2026-08-13 round 2).** An earlier draft also granted `.manage` to `principal`; it was withdrawn. `user_has_permission()` has FOUR paths, and the fourth is `fn_handover_grants_key()` — a **Director handover** grants a key with no role change, scoped to one route, revocable, tenant-bound and chased on the Director's Desk. Live precedent, not theory: `eao@jkkn.ac.in` holds no role carrying `.manage` and is not a super admin, yet assigned **14 metric owners on 2026-08-13** under an accepted handover for `/accreditation/manage/owners` granted by `director@` on 2026-08-11. The ruling: permanent role grant for STANDING cluster accountability (`ceo`, `managing_director`); handover for DELEGATED work (principals, one person at a time).
- **The two gaps it closes.** (1) `/accreditation/cac` gates on `accreditation.cac.view` (page: `app/(routes)/accreditation/cac/page.tsx:65`, `isSuperAdmin || can('accreditation.cac.view')`). Read by value on prod 2026-08-13, the `ceo` role did **not carry that key at all** and `ceo@jkkn.ac.in` is **not** a super admin, so no bypass covered for it — the CEO was refused at the one dashboard reporting the council framework they own, while six lesser roles (`accreditation_officer`, `coo`, `hod`, `principal`, `registrar`, `vice_principal`) already held it. `managing_director` was in the same position. (2) `accreditation.naac.narrative.manage` is what `accred_metric_owners_manage` uses for BOTH its USING and WITH CHECK on `accreditation_metric_owners`, i.e. it **is** the assign-an-owner write — and swept across all **90 active roles**, exactly **one** held it (`accreditation_officer`). That is a real single-**role** bottleneck, but it was never a single-**person** one: the handover path above means a Director can hand the desk to anybody, and had already done so. Measured live 2026-08-13: `accreditation_metric_owners` holds **14 rows**, all created that morning (10:52–11:22), all **body-level** (`metric_code IS NULL`), covering **5 of the 8 assessed colleges** — Allied Health, Arts & Science (Aided) and Education have no owner for any body. This migration assigns nobody; it widens who is allowed to.
- **Six (role, key) pairs, verified ABSENT before writing.** `ceo` and `managing_director` each gain `accreditation.cac.view`, `.naac.narrative.view`, `.naac.narrative.manage` — all six were **ABSENT**, not false. `accreditation_officer` already held all three and its row is **not touched at all**. `principal` is untouched by this file entirely.
- **Scoped by explicit `role_key IN (...)`, never by a rule.** No predicate of the "every role holding X" shape appears, so the file is structurally incapable of sweeping in a role nobody reviewed. Verified on a throwaway Postgres 16: `coo`, `hod`, `registrar`, `vice_principal` and `faculty` came out **byte-identical to seed**.
- **Containment, for whenever a principal IS handed the desk.** `accred_metric_owners_manage` is `is_super_admin() OR (user_has_permission('accreditation.naac.narrative.manage') AND role_has_institution_access(institution_id))` — the second arm is an AND, and `principal` is `institution_scope = 'own'` (read live), so a principal holding the key by handover can name owners inside their own college and nowhere else. That containment is pre-existing RLS and applies to the handover path identically; this migration neither adds to it nor removes from it. `ceo`/`managing_director`/`accreditation_officer` are `'all'`, which is the intent for a cluster body.
- 🪤 **The `?` trap is live in this exact data, and the guard avoids it.** `user_has_permission()` tests `(permissions->>key)::boolean = true`, but the `?` existence operator returns TRUE for a key stored `false`. Measured on the real `principal` row: stored value `false`, **`?` says `true`**, `->>` says `false`. A `?`-based assert would have reported principal as already granted while the principal still could not assign an owner. Section 3 asserts **by value** only, against the text `'true'`, so an explicit `false` and an ABSENT key are both caught and named in the error.
- ⚠️ **Correcting the folklore about `jsonb_set`, which was wrong in the brief for this change.** `jsonb_set(target, path, value)` takes a fourth argument `create_if_missing` that **DEFAULTS TO TRUE**, so the three-argument form *does* create an absent top-level key and would have granted these correctly. Measured on PostgreSQL 16.14: `jsonb_set('{"a":true}','{k}','true')` → `k = true`; `jsonb_set('{"a":true}','{k}','true',false)` → **k ABSENT, silent no-op**; `jsonb_set('{"k":false}','{k}','true',false)` → `k = true`. The real hazard is the **four-argument form with `false`**, which here would have left all six pairs quietly ungranted while reporting success. `||` is used because it is immune to that footgun whoever edits the file next, and sets all three keys in one expression where `jsonb_set` needs three nested calls. Both return NULL on NULL input, so neither is safer there; `permissions` is NOT NULL DEFAULT `'{}'`. `||` **merges** — `accreditation.view` survived on `ceo`/`managing_director`, verified.
- **The guard asserts the END STATE (3 roles × 3 keys = 9 pairs), not just the 6 pairs it writes**, and `RAISE EXCEPTION`s — never `NOTICE`, which stamps zero rows and reads as a clean apply while Studio hides it entirely. A missing `role_key` and an **inactive** role are each reported as failures rather than skipped, because both make the UPDATE match zero rows, which otherwise looks exactly like success. **Proven non-vacuous by mutation on a throwaway Postgres 16**, seeded with production's exact by-value starting state: sabotaging the untouched `accreditation_officer` row to `false` raises; deleting each of its three keys raises (ABSENT caught, all three); deleting `managing_director` raises `ROLE DOES NOT EXIST`; setting `accreditation_officer` inactive raises `ROLE IS NOT ACTIVE`; the unsabotaged control applies cleanly. 🪤 Note for whoever extends these tests: sabotaging a key on `ceo`/`managing_director` does **not** test the guard, because section 1 re-grants it before section 2 runs — only the untouched `accreditation_officer` row can. (These mutation results were measured against the earlier four-role draft; the three-role matrix is the same shape with `principal` removed, and the `accreditation_officer` cases are the load-bearing ones either way.)
- **Idempotent:** the UPDATE and the guard are both re-runnable; manage-key ROLE holders settle at 3 (this count excludes anyone holding the key by Director handover). No `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` in the file, so a reviewer's `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` rehearsal against production actually rolls back.
- 📋 **Reported, not enforced** (and never the only check on anything the file intends to change — all 9 asserted pairs go through the `RAISE EXCEPTION` path): a `NOTICE` names every role outside the reviewed three that already holds `accreditation.cac.view` (expected `coo`, `hod`, `principal`, `registrar`, `vice_principal`, granted by `20260809100100`), and a second `NOTICE` prints the count of `.manage` ROLE holders, expected to move **1 → 3** — a count that deliberately does not include anyone holding the key by Director handover.
- ⚠️ **Apply-time consequence beyond access: the manage key is also a NOTIFICATION DELIVERY LIST, and that half is NOT institution-scoped.** `fn_accreditation_narrative_reminders` (`20260727130000`) builds `elig` as every profile where `user_has_permission(p.id,'accreditation.naac.narrative.manage')` and then fans out with `FROM created2 c CROSS JOIN elig e` — no institution predicate, and it is SECURITY DEFINER, so the `role_has_institution_access()` containment that governs what a principal may WRITE does not govern what they are TOLD ABOUT. Measured on prod 2026-08-13: **85 narratives exist and all 85 sit in an escalatable status** (`ai_drafted`, `owner_okayed`, `principal_approved`, `revision_requested`); holders are `principal` 13 via `user_roles` / 12 via legacy `profiles.role`, `ceo` 2/2, `managing_director` 2/1. So this grant takes the escalation audience from **one person to roughly eighteen**, and each of the 13 principals begins receiving escalations about OTHER colleges' narratives. Only narratives older than `p_escalate_days` fire and the idempotency key is per-narrative-per-day so nothing duplicates within a day, but the fan-out is real at that volume. This does not change the Director's decision and is deliberately NOT 'fixed' here — if the noise is unwanted the predicate belongs in that reminder function, not in this grant. The reminder's live schedule was not verified.
- ⚠️ **Unexplained, surfaced for someone with write access to investigate — not fixed here.** `accreditation_metric_owners` is **not empty**: it holds **11 rows**, all created 2026-08-13 between 10:52 and 11:04, covering **4 of 14** active institutions. Every row carries `created_by = eao@jkkn.ac.in`, who is **not** a super admin and holds four roles (`admission`, `admission_counselor`, `ai_assistant_pilot`, `executive_admin_officer`) of which **none** grants `.naac.narrative.manage` — `executive_admin_officer` carries it explicitly `false`. The manage policy has no `is_admin()` arm, `user_has_permission()` has no blanket-admin fallback (super-admin bypass → `user_roles` OR-merge → legacy `profiles.role` join, and all three evaluate false here), and the assigning UI writes with the **browser anon client** under RLS. No `custom_roles` row was updated on 2026-08-13 (latest `updated_at` is 2026-08-11) and no `user_roles` row was assigned that day, so "granted then revoked" is ruled out. Those 11 writes therefore should not have been possible through the documented path — worth establishing whether a service-role route or a SECURITY DEFINER helper is writing this table, since if so the manage key is not the only gate on owner assignment.
### Five sources were already emitting evidence and were not in the registry (2026-08-13)
- `supabase/migrations/20260828010000_register_emitting_evidence_sources.sql` — **FILE ONLY — not applied, Director-gated.** Inserts five rows into `public.quality_evidence_source_registry` and seeds their `fix_route` / `fix_hint` / `owner_role`. Creates no object, drops nothing, adds no function — so no SECURITY DEFINER and no anon-revoke clause applies. The table's existing RLS and anon posture (from `20260423_unification_crud_retrofit.sql`) are untouched, and inserting a config row cannot widen either; no role gains or loses any access. Carries no `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;`, so a `BEGIN .. ROLLBACK` rehearsal stays a rehearsal.
- **The join is on `source_table`, and five of them were missing.** `quality_evidence_mappings` joins the registry on `source_table`, never on `source_kind` — `source_kind` is a logical singular (`bos_meeting`) that can never equal a physical table name (`bos_meetings`). Five source tables emit into the mappings today with no registry row at all: `learners_profiles` (11,396 rows → NIRF `OI_ESCS`, `OI_GD`, `OI_RD`, `TLR_SS`), `obe_course_attainment_rollup` (92 → NAAC 7.3.d, NBA `T1_CO`), `mess_menu_recommendations` (48 → NAAC 7.3.f), `scf_ai_suggestions` (5 → NAAC 7.3.f) and `induction_programs` (2 → NAAC 6.3.1, 6.3.2). Every screen that reads the registry to say where a number came from showed those five as nothing, so an assessor asking "where did this figure come from?" got no answer.
- **Four of the five are machine-derived, so the route points one step UPSTREAM.** Director decision 2026-08-13: all five get a destination, and where no human types the row directly the destination is the screen where the raw data a person *does* type is entered — never the read-only page that displays the derived result, which would be the same dead end as no link dressed up as help. `obe_course_attainment_rollup` has no human write path at all (its own RLS comment reads `WRITES: none (RPC-only)`) → `/academic/internal-marks`, where the CIA marks it is computed from are typed. `mess_menu_recommendations` → `/campus-living/mess/menu`. `scf_ai_suggestions` → `/learners/class-feedback`, where the feedback the model reads is submitted. `induction_programs` → `/events/induction`. `learners_profiles` is human-entered throughout → `/learners/profiles`. All five resolve to a real `app/(routes)/<path>/page.tsx` on `jicate/main` at `905a37d4`, checked against the route tree rather than remembered, and none carries a dynamic `[segment]` — the person reading a gap has no id to substitute.
- ⚠ **One source is AI-written with no human approval step, and its `description` says so first.** Director decision 2026-08-13: AI-written evidence counts, but the registry must state plainly that it is AI-written. `scf_ai_suggestions`'s description opens `AI-WRITTEN —` and says no person approves a row before it becomes evidence. Both halves were read from the source migrations, not assumed: `20260625120000` gives that table `model`, `suggestion jsonb` and a NULLABLE `human_verdict` constrained to `tried_helped` / `tried_no_change` / `not_tried` — a retrospective "did this help?" note, **not** a gate, so a row is evidence the moment it is written whether or not anyone reads it. The description names the contrast explicitly, because `mess_menu_recommendations` (`20260727000000`) is *also* machine-generated but carries `status DEFAULT 'proposed' CHECK (proposed|accepted|rejected|edited)` with `reviewed_by`, `reviewed_at`, `review_note` — a recorded Chairperson verdict. Same registry, two very different provenances; the reader must be able to tell them apart without opening a migration.
- **`owner_role` is evidenced per source, not chosen by feel — and it grants nothing.** It is read by no RLS policy and no SECURITY DEFINER function; access still comes from `custom_roles.permissions` via `user_has_permission()`. `learners_profiles` → `registrar` (Director decision, taken as given). `mess_menu_recommendations` → `chief_warden`, because `20260726073531` grants that role `campus_living.mess.menu.manage` and calls it "the intended loop operator", and the table's own `mmr_select` policy reads that same permission. `scf_ai_suggestions` → `scf_note_reviewer`, created by `20260726095711` at `institution_scope 'all'` to review AI-drafted learner notes across every college. `induction_programs` → `induction_coordinator`, created and appointed per college by `20260630010000`. `obe_course_attainment_rollup` → `hod`: the rollup is course-grain with no human write path, so the desk is the one accountable for the courses and for chasing whoever types the marks — the `faculty` role_key was rejected as the owner because it names ~850 people rather than a desk, and every other course- or department-grain academic source already in this registry (`bos_meeting`, `sh_publication`, `ip_filing`, `learner_exit_outcome`) is owned by `hod`. All five `role_key`s are seeded by migrations already on `jicate/main`.
- 🪤 **Seeded `WHERE NOT EXISTS` on BOTH keys, never `ON CONFLICT`.** One `INSERT` per source, matching the rule this repo states verbatim in its own section headers ("CONFIG, seeded WHERE NOT EXISTS (never ON CONFLICT, per registry seeding rule)"), then a single `UPDATE .. FROM (VALUES ..)` so the routing decision reads as one table rather than five scattered statements. Each guard tests `source_kind = … OR source_table = …`: `source_kind` is the PRIMARY KEY but `source_table` carries its own `UNIQUE` constraint, so a guard on `source_kind` alone would let a duplicate `source_table` reach the table and raise `23505`. All five `source_kind` values were checked against the 24 live kinds and none collides; `is_system = true` matches all 24 existing rows.
- 🪤 **The `UPDATE` matches on BOTH keys, because matching on `source_kind` alone was a silent collateral write.** Because the two keys are constrained independently, a pair can be *crossed* — a row holding one of these `source_kind`s against a different `source_table`. Section 1's `INSERT` is then correctly skipped, but an `UPDATE` joined on `source_kind` alone reaches that unrelated row and rewrites its `fix_route` / `fix_hint` / `owner_role`. Reproduced on a fixture: a row keyed `induction_program → induction_programme_records` had its route rewritten to `/events/induction` and **kept it** after the assertion abort, because the write had already autocommitted. The `VALUES` list now carries `source_table` and the join requires both to match, so the statement can only ever touch the row section 1 means it to. A new section 0b independently refuses such a database by name before any write. Verified: with the crossed row present the file refuses, that row is byte-for-byte unchanged, and **zero** of the five are inserted.
- 🔒 **Sections 0–3 are ONE `DO` block, and that is load-bearing.** Written as separate top-level statements they do not protect each other: under `psql -f` at default settings (no `ON_ERROR_STOP`) and the Management API hand-apply path this repo actually uses, a `RAISE EXCEPTION` prints as an error and the runner moves on. Measured — the section 0b refusal fired and four `INSERT`s plus the `UPDATE` ran anyway and autocommitted, surviving the section 3 abort. A `DO` block is one statement to the server, so it is atomic without any `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;` of ours (which would defeat the `BEGIN .. ROLLBACK` rehearsal). Consequences, all intended and all verified: a precondition `RAISE` prevents every write below it; a section 3 assertion failure now **rolls the writes back** rather than leaving four of five sources registered (proved by forcing assertion (f) to fail — the five inserts were gone afterwards, table back to its original 20 rows); and the five `INSERT`s and the `UPDATE` land together or not at all. Section 4 stays a separate block — it only reads and only `RAISE NOTICE`s.
- **Six assertions, every one `RAISE EXCEPTION`.** A guard whose miss path is `RAISE NOTICE` reads as success in Studio, so none is used for correctness here. (a) all five present, keyed on `source_table` — the column the mappings actually join on. (b) no `fix_route` relative or carrying `[`, table-wide. (c) no route without a hint or the reverse, table-wide. (d) every one of the five carries route **and** hint **and** owner, scoped to the five so it fails **by name** if section 2 is stripped rather than passing on the other 24. (e) exactly 5 newly routed, counted directly rather than off the table total, so it cannot be satisfied by the pre-existing 21. (f) at least 26 routed overall (21 before + 5 here), so an earlier seed silently ceasing to match is caught too. Section 4 stays advisory `RAISE NOTICE` — a deliberate, documented exception — because an `owner_role` naming a role not seeded on *this* database is a stale hint and failing there would block a migration that grants nothing.
- 🔗 **Depends on `20260809100700`.** Section 0 refuses to run if `quality_evidence_source_registry` is absent, and refuses again if the `fix_route` column is absent, naming the file to apply first. It checks the **catalog**, not the migration ledger — see `docs/architecture/2026-08-12-MIGRATION-ledger-drift-unrecorded-applied-versions.md` for why the ledger cannot answer that question on this database.

### Renumber the accreditation committee RLS file off its shared version (2026-08-13)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808210001_accreditation_committee_rls_naac_permission_family.sql` — **FILE ONLY — not applied, Director-gated.** `git mv` from `20260808210000_…`, so history is preserved. Its eight `ALTER POLICY` statements are byte-identical to before; the only content changes are the header and a new section 0 guard described below.
- **Why: one version string cannot represent two files.** `20260808210000` was held by both this file and `20260808210000_soi_programme_coordinator_role.sql`. `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` keys on the timestamp alone, so whichever ran first would claim the version and the second would be **silently skipped** — the shadowing failure this repo has already been bitten by. Director decision 2026-08-13: rename the accreditation file only, leave the School of Influence file exactly where it is.
- 🪤 **The new version is `210001`, one second later — NOT a fresh timestamp at the end of the queue, and this is load-bearing.** `20260809102300_committee_roster_access.sql` (**applied to production 2026-08-05**) rewrites `committees_select` and `members_select` to add a roster arm, and `ALTER POLICY` **replaces the whole expression** rather than merging into it. Moving this file after `20260809102300` would make a from-scratch replay silently drop that roster arm. `210001` keeps it sorting exactly where it always has — after the SoI file it no longer collides with, and comfortably before `20260809102300`. That constraint is already recorded in this index under "Committee access follows the roster, not the job title (2026-08-09)"; the rename was chosen to satisfy it rather than to break it.
- ⚠ **Why the guard exists — read from production 2026-08-13, not inferred.** The two SELECT policies live on production carry an arm this file does not declare: `committees_select` ends `… OR fn_user_is_committee_member(id)`, and `members_select` ends `… OR fn_user_is_committee_member(committee_id) OR (user_id = auth.uid())`, both put there by `20260809102300_committee_roster_access.sql` (applied 2026-08-05). `ALTER POLICY` **replaces the whole expression**, so replaying this file against production would REMOVE that arm and lock every committee member out of their own committee. The other six policies match this file exactly, so only those two are at risk — and they are the two that matter.
- ⚠ **The shared version was NEVER a shield — an earlier version of this entry claimed otherwise and was wrong.** `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` has **no row for `20260808210000`** (checked against production 2026-08-13), so a `supabase db push` has always been free to attempt this file. The rename does not remove a protection that existed; the protection never existed, and section 0 is the first guard this file has ever had. Do not restate the "accidental shield" claim.
- 🔒 **The guard and the eight writes are ONE `DO` block, and that is load-bearing.** A standalone guard block followed by eight bare `ALTER POLICY` statements does **not** guard: under `psql -f` at default settings (no `ON_ERROR_STOP`) and the Management API hand-apply path this repo actually uses, the `RAISE` prints as an error and the runner executes all eight anyway. Demonstrated on a production-shaped fixture: roster arm present on both SELECT policies before, absent from both after, `psql` exit code **0**. The eight statements now run via `EXECUTE` inside the same block as the refusal, so a `RAISE EXCEPTION` provably prevents them whatever the caller's flags — verified both ways: refuses and preserves the roster arm when it is present, and realigns all eight onto the grantable family on a from-scratch replay. The `EXECUTE`d expressions were diffed against the catalog output of the bare statements they replace and are byte-identical, 8/8.
- **Idempotency, stated plainly: yes for content, no for a missing policy.** The eight statements are declarative `ALTER POLICY` rewrites with no `CREATE`, `INSERT` or `DROP`, so re-running them lands on the same expression. But `ALTER POLICY` has no `IF EXISTS` — if any of the eight policies were ever renamed or dropped, a replay errors on that statement rather than skipping it. Re-runnable, not unconditionally safe.
- ⚠ **Applied-state is NOT resolved by this PR.** This index has said **FILE ONLY, not applied** since the file was written, and nothing in this change verified that against production — the author had no database access from the build worktree. A reviewer with Management API access should confirm by catalog (`pg_policies` on the two tables) before this file is applied or marked applied, because two contradictory claims are in circulation and only the catalog can settle it.

### Six SECURITY DEFINER functions any unauthenticated caller can run — one of them expires every active trip (2026-08-13)
- `supabase/migrations/20260827020000_revoke_anon_execute_six_secdef.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED — Director-gated.** Grants only; no function body is created, replaced or altered. Closes six `prosecdef` functions that `anon` can EXECUTE on production. All six carry the identical ACL `=X/postgres postgres=X/postgres authenticated=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres`; **none holds an `anon=X` entry of its own**, so `REVOKE ... FROM anon` alone would succeed, change nothing and report success — the `PUBLIC` half is the load-bearing part, exactly as on 2026-07-30 and in 20260813020000. **Group A (5), revoke `anon, PUBLIC`, re-GRANT `authenticated`:** `fn_resolve_shift_timing(uuid,date)`, `fn_resolve_shift_timings_bulk(uuid[],date,date)`, `fn_save_shift_timing_week(uuid,text,uuid,date,jsonb)` [WRITES], `fn_shift_timing_coverage(uuid,date)`, `generate_hr_leave_balances_bulk(uuid,uuid[],boolean)` [WRITES]. `authenticated` MUST survive — each has live callers (`lib/services/hr/shift-timing-service.ts:157/175/194`, `lib/services/hr/leave-type-service.ts:262`, `app/api/hr/attendance/import|recompute`, the shift-timings weekly grid). These five DO guard themselves and the guard was proven **behaviourally, not read off the source**: called as the `anon` role inside a rolled-back transaction on production, `fn_shift_timing_coverage` raised `42501 Not authorized to view shift timing coverage for this institution` (line 12) and `fn_resolve_shift_timing` raised `42501 Not authorized to resolve shift timing for this …` (line 19 — the string is quoted in full in the migration header). So this is defence in depth, not an incident — it matters because each takes the identity it reports on **as a parameter** (`p_staff_id`, `p_institution_id`), the same shape that made `fn_hostel_unallocated_candidates` return 49 learners to an anonymous caller. **Group B (1), revoke `anon, PUBLIC, authenticated`:** `tms_expire_stale_trips()` — genuinely unguarded (a scan of its body for `is_super_admin`/`is_admin`/`user_has_permission`/`RAISE EXCEPTION`/`auth.uid` returns NULL), **zero application callers** across app/lib/hooks/components/scripts, and invoked only by pg_cron job 24 `tms-expire-stale-trips` (`*/5 * * * *`, username `postgres`). It takes no arguments, so nothing clamps it to an institution: it UPDATEs `tms_trip` to `status='expired'` cluster-wide and switches off `location_sharing_enabled`, `active_route_id` and `location_sharing_started_at` on every affected `tms_driver`. Revoking `authenticated` costs nothing because pg_cron runs it as the OWNER, where EXECUTE is not checked. Estate measured 2026-08-13: 1 active trip, 3 trips, 31 drivers, 1 sharing location — a mechanism fix, not incident response; the function was deliberately **never invoked**, being destructive. 🛑 **Two functions are deliberately NOT revoked** — `fn_is_event_creator(uuid)` and `fn_is_designated_leave_approver(uuid)` are also SECDEF + anon-executable and the sweep flags them, but they derive their whole answer from `auth.uid()` (NULL for anon ⇒ can only return false) AND they sit inside five RLS policies granted `TO public`, where a function is evaluated as the **querying** role — revoking would make anon queries raise `permission denied for function` instead of returning zero rows, breaking the public event-registration form. They are allow-listed in `scripts/ci/anon-exposure-functions.json` instead, with both reasons recorded, so the sweep stops flagging them and the next engineer does not "fix" them into an outage. **Proven against production by rehearsal, then rolled back:** BEFORE all 8 read `anon=true, PUBLIC(=X/)=true`; AFTER, the five read `anon=false, authenticated=true, service_role=true, postgres=true` and `tms_expire_stale_trips` reads `anon=false, authenticated=false, service_role=true, postgres=true`, with the two allow-listed rows **byte-identical**; POST-ROLLBACK all 8 are back to their BEFORE values, so nothing persisted. The closing `DO` block asserts every intended state with `has_function_privilege` and is proven **non-vacuous by three mutations**, each failing by name: dropping `, PUBLIC` from one revoke → `anon STILL has EXECUTE`; dropping `authenticated` from the tms revoke → `authenticated STILL has EXECUTE`; folding `authenticated` into a Group A revoke → `authenticated LOST EXECUTE (live callers would break)`; the unmutated file passes. ⚠️ That mutation run also found a bug **in this file** and it is fixed here: `text[] || 'bare literal'` is ambiguous (PostgreSQL prefers `array || array`) and aborted with `22P02 malformed array literal` instead of naming the wrong privilege — the three Group B appends now carry explicit `::text` casts; the `FOREACH` branch was already safe because `format()` returns typed text. Live sweep, same session: unapproved functions 8 → 6 from the allow-list half alone, `stale=[]`. No `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` in the file, so a reviewer's `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` rehearsal against production actually rolls back. | 2026-08-13 | FILE ONLY — not applied
### One meeting type, many places — the single-location ceiling behind the duplicate booking records (2026-08-13)
- `supabase/migrations/20260830030000_meeting_type_locations.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED — Director-gated.** New child table `meeting_type_locations` (meeting_type_id → `meeting_types` ON DELETE CASCADE, `location_mode` CHECK'd against the same `in_person`/`phone`/`online` vocabulary as the parent, `location_resource_id` → `resources` ON DELETE SET NULL mirroring `meeting_types.location_resource_id`, `location_text`, `sort_order`, `created_at`), plus `idx_mtl_meeting_type` and the uniqueness rule `uq_mtl_type_place`. **Why it exists:** a `meeting_type` holds EXACTLY ONE location today (`location_mode` + `location_resource_id` + `location_text`, all on the parent row), which is why the Director's booking page carries near-duplicate records differing only by place — "One to One Meeting with Ommsharravana 15 Minutes" (in_person) and "Online One to One 15Mins Meeting with Omm" (online) are the same 15-minute purpose stored twice. The locked spec `.claude/booking-rooms-spec-2026-08-03.md` names this as the blocker ("one `meeting_type` can hold exactly one location today… Everything else follows from fixing that") and sizes the payoff at 16 one-to-one records collapsing to 9. **Uniqueness is an expression index, not a table constraint, deliberately:** two of the three place columns are nullable, so a plain `UNIQUE` would treat NULL as distinct from NULL and let `phone` be added to one type any number of times; `COALESCE(location_resource_id, '000…0'::uuid)` + `COALESCE(btrim(location_text), '')` makes the rule total and makes `Room 204` and `Room 204 ` the same place. **BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING BY CONSTRUCTION:** the backfill writes one row per existing meeting type copied from that type's current location columns — measured read-only against production 2026-08-13, that is **248 rows, 45 of them on the Director's `omm` host page**, and all 248 are distinct under the uniqueness key so the unique index cannot reject the backfill (verified: `rows_in=248, distinct_keys=248`). Guarded by `NOT EXISTS` so a re-run is a no-op rather than a duplicate-key error. The legacy `meeting_types.location_*` columns are **NOT dropped, altered, or stopped being written** — they remain the source of truth for every current consumer (`public-host-service`, the slots/book APIs, the manage form, calendar sync) until a later PR flips the read path over; no meeting_type row is merged, deleted or re-grouped here. **RLS mirrors `meeting_type_cohosts` (`mtc_host_all`, 20260619000100)**, the existing child of `meeting_types`: `mtl_host_all` FOR ALL gated on `is_super_admin() OR is_admin() OR` the parent type's `host_profile_id = auth.uid()`, written **initplan-wrapped** (`(SELECT is_admin())`) because that is the form `mt_host_all`/`mtc_host_all` already carry live after `rls_initplan_wrap_sweep`, so a future sweep has nothing to rewrite. Second policy `mtl_public_page_read` expresses the public-page rule — parent `is_active AND NOT hidden` on a page that is `is_public AND NOT auto_hidden`, the same D20 gate `PublicHostService.resolveBookableHost` applies (13 rows qualify live, 4 of them `omm`'s) — granted `TO authenticated` with `REVOKE ALL … FROM anon`, deliberately: the anonymous `/meet/[handle]` surface does not read these tables directly, it holds a **service-role** client that bypasses RLS (documented at the top of `public-host-service.ts`), exactly as it already does for `meeting_types`, which carries no public-read policy at all; `meeting_host_pages` was hardened the same way in `20260612090000`. No SECURITY DEFINER function is created, so there is no EXECUTE grant to revoke. Idempotent (`CREATE TABLE/INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, `DROP POLICY` before `CREATE`, `NOT EXISTS`-guarded INSERT); contains no DELETE, UPDATE, TRUNCATE or DROP. **The code half is safe to merge and deploy before this file is applied:** `PublicHostService.placesFor` fails soft and empty on a missing table so every type falls back to the single place its legacy columns describe, and the manage UI returns `locations: null` and hides the Places section entirely rather than offering an Add button that cannot work.

### Champion Console session trend: starter take-up is unreadable, and "what counts as a session" was a constant (2026-08-13)
- `supabase/migrations/20260828043000_ai_pulse_starter_takeup_readable.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED — Director-gated, and not rehearsed against production by its author.** Two changes, no function created or replaced. ### Both colleges label shared teaching, and the system stamps who said it (2026-09-21)

Adds `labelled_by_institution_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES institutions(id)` with `CHECK (labelled_by_institution_id IN (giver_institution_id, receiver_institution_id))` so an outside college cannot file an opinion on someone else's arrangement, drops `shared_teaching_labels_unique_relationship` and adds `shared_teaching_labels_unique_side UNIQUE (giver, receiver, academic_year, labelled_by)` — **a NEW name for new semantics**, per the drop-and-rename idiom of 20260801000800, because a constraint named for a rule it no longer enforces is a trap for whoever reads the name and trusts it (`unique_position` on `lc_members` already burned this estate). FROM anon, PUBLIC`. The client value is overwritten rather than rejected — rejecting would leak which value was expected. **DECISION 6** adds `edited_at` (NULL until the first correction; the trigger also pins `set_at` to its original value, so "first said" and "last changed" stay separate facts and a correction cannot be made to look like an original answer). **DECISION 8** adds `carried_forward_from_academic_year_id` with `ON DELETE SET NULL` — retiring an old year must not delete a college's position — plus a CHECK that it cannot point at its own year; **nothing writes it yet, deliberately**: the marker ships before the carry-forward job so "unmarked" can never be the shipped default. **DECISION 12** is honoured in the read: a side that has not answered comes back as JSON `null` for the WHOLE object, never an object of nulls and never a zero, so "they said nothing" stays distinguishable from "they said neither". `fn_shared_teaching_relationships(uuid)` is rewritten to join the label table TWICE, each join pinned to one side, returning `giver_label` and `receiver_label` as independent objects — the new unique key is what guarantees each join matches at most one row, so no line can fan out — and **`is_admin()` is added to its guard**: all three RLS policies admit `is_super_admin() OR is_admin()` while the function admitted only the first, so an is_admin() viewer without the view key could SELECT the table directly yet was refused 42501 by the function that exists to read it. The column is nullable, `partner_name` keeps its NOT NULL and its meaning (the register copies the chosen college's name into it), so every existing row stays valid and every existing reader is unaffected. **Director's ruling: both colleges see it** — `ic_select` and `ic_update` gain a partner arm, their `is_super_admin() OR is_admin() OR (user_has_permission(...) AND role_has_institution_access(...))` shape preserved verbatim with the arm appended. `ic_insert`/`ic_delete` are NOT restated: filing and deleting stay with the filing college, deliberately (destroying the other college's record is not what "both signatories" means), and the register UI hides the delete action on a partner-filed row while the service now raises instead of reporting success on an RLS-filtered zero-row delete. 🔴 **The NULL trap this file exists to avoid:** `role_has_institution_access(NULL)` **returns TRUE** by design (`20260521_role_has_institution_access_cas_aware.sql`, first branch: "NULL institution_id: always accessible"), so the obvious `OR role_has_institution_access(partner_institution_id)` would evaluate TRUE for **every external-partner row** — handing every holder of `accreditation.collaborations.view` every other college's external MoUs. Both arms are therefore written `partner_institution_id IS NOT NULL AND role_has_institution_access(...)`, and an apply-time assert re-reads `pg_policies.qual` for both policies and raises if that guard is ever edited out. `fn_cac_internal_agreements_count()` is SECURITY DEFINER because the table is RLS-scoped and a council member scoped to one college would otherwise be shown their own college's agreements as the cluster's — same reason `fn_cac_cluster_totals` exists. Locked per the mandatory template (`REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` + `GRANT ... TO authenticated`); a grant to `authenticated` being only half the question, it also carries its own COALESCEd caller guard (`accreditation.cac.view` OR `accreditation.cac.readiness.view`) and returns a bare integer with no row detail. Asserts check EFFECTIVE privilege via `has_function_privilege`, never the ACL string. **Out of scope, stated so it is not mistaken for an oversight:** `emit_institution_collaboration_evidence` (`20260726100000`) names `NEW.institution_id` explicitly, so the second column does NOT reach `quality_evidence_mappings` — an internal agreement emits evidence for the filing college only, exactly as today; whether a shared agreement should emit twice is an accreditation double-counting question, not a schema one, and the trigger is not touched. Effect on screen: the UGC readiness row `written-agreement` stops being a hardcoded `not-expressible` literal and becomes `awaiting-entry` / `in-place` off a live count — moving the checklist's last "nothing records this" to "nothing recorded yet". Idempotent (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, guarded `ADD CONSTRAINT`, `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, `CREATE OR REPLACE`); no `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` in the file, so a reviewer's `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` rehearsal actually rolls back. | 2026-09-21 | FILE ONLY — not applied
### The department that produces the record could not write it, and one account could file a Council resolution (2026-08-21)
- `supabase/migrations/20260921030000_cac_governance_grants.sql` — **✅ APPLIED to production 2026-08-21.** Rehearsed first inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` (every precondition and assertion passed), then residue confirmed 0 in a SEPARATE call — the Management API wraps a batch in one transaction, so a same-batch check would have proved nothing. Applied with a matching `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` row (version `20260921030000`, name `cac_governance_grants`), because the `/database/query` path writes no ledger row on its own and that omission is exactly what left `20260908020000` invisible to the repo. **Catalog evidence (NOT the ledger), read after the apply, by VALUE not key existence:** `solutions.first_use.record` and `.view` are TRUE on cbo, ceo, hod, managing_director, principal, school_principal, vice_principal (was cbo, ceo, managing_director); `accreditation.naac.committees.meetings.manage` is TRUE on accreditation_officer, registrar (was accreditation_officer alone). People reached: recording first use 4 → **137**; filing Council minutes 1 → **2**. Note `hod` and `principal` carried the minutes key with value **false** before this ran — a `permissions ? 'key'` test would have reported them as holders while they were locked out, which is why every check in the migration reads `->>`. Three permission grants on `custom_roles.permissions`. No table, no function, no policy, no revoke, and no accompanying code edit — all three keys are ALREADY registered in `lib/constants/permissions.ts` (`accreditation.naac.committees.meetings.manage` line 1680, `solutions.first_use.view`/`.record` lines 1892-1893), so this is a DB grant only and that file is deliberately untouched. `solutions.first_use.view` + `.record` → `hod`, `principal`, `vice_principal`, `school_principal`; `accreditation.naac.committees.meetings.manage` → `registrar`. **PURELY ADDITIVE:** `ceo`, `managing_director`, `cbo` and `accreditation_officer` are not named in any UPDATE and keep everything they hold — there is no jsonb `-` and no `false` written anywhere in the file. **Why the first-use grant, and it is a correction of a measured failure rather than a widening:** Director decision #5 is stated in `hooks/solutions/use-solution-first-use.ts` — "The producing department records, at one checkpoint, the first time somebody outside the team used the thing they built" — but read live on production 2026-08-21 against 91 active roles, `solutions.first_use.record` sat on `ceo`, `managing_director` and `cbo`: three roles, four people, none of them the producing department. The cause is in `20260907120000`, which granted the keys with the predicate `WHERE (permissions->>'solutions.dashboard.view')::boolean IS TRUE` under the stated intent "the producing department's existing way into the hub"; on this estate that donor key resolves to the three executives, so the predicate produced the exact opposite of its intent while every assertion in that file passed — a donor-key predicate is self-consistent by construction and can only be wrong relative to an intent the SQL never states. Hence every role here is a **literal**, and no predicate of the shape "every role that already holds X" appears in the file. **Why the minutes grant:** `accreditation.naac.committees.meetings.manage` was held by `accreditation_officer` and nobody else — ONE account platform-wide — while gating ALL writes to `accreditation_committee_meetings` and `accreditation_committee_resolutions` (RLS from `20260710060000`, per the header of `lib/services/accreditation/committee-meeting-service.ts`) and `canManageMeetings` on `/accreditation/naac/committees/[id]`. Those minutes are the Council's only durable output — the 2026-07-10 loop in which "minutes become the Action-Taken Report" — so one person on leave stopped the Council minuting anything, and an unminuted resolution is indistinguishable from a meeting that never happened. `registrar` is a second pair of hands, not a replacement. **Roles are CLUSTER-WIDE and this does NOT leak across colleges:** `custom_roles.role_key` is UNIQUE platform-wide with no row-per-college, so a grant on `hod` is necessarily every HOD in the cluster and no narrower write exists in this table; per-college confinement lives in the RLS policies, which pair the permission test with `role_has_institution_access(s.institution_id)` on the row — the one documented exception (`sh_solutions.institution_id` is NULLABLE and `role_has_institution_access(NULL)` returns TRUE as "system-wide record") is pre-existing and unchanged here. **Widening who may record cannot create competing records:** `sh_solution_first_use.solution_id` is UNIQUE, so "one entry per solution, ever" is a database guarantee and the second writer gets a 23505. **Shape:** ONE `DO $$` block for both grants (a bare UPDATE autocommits under the Management API hand-apply path this repo uses, so a separate guard would guard nothing; sharing one block also makes a half-applied pair impossible), `permissions || jsonb_build_object(...)` never `jsonb_set` (merges, preserves every other key, and behaves identically whether the key is absent or already present — including present-and-`false`, which is overwritten rather than skipped), and every check reads `(permissions ->> key)::boolean IS TRUE` and never `permissions ? 'key'` — the `?` operator tests KEY EXISTENCE, and this estate has measured both halves of that failure (an audit reading "6,287 learners can approve" when the truth was four roles, and `hod` carrying a key explicitly `false` that a `?` test counted as held, producing 107 recipients where 5 were intended; `hod` is one of the roles granted here, so it is not hypothetical). Preconditions RAISE EXCEPTION rather than skip on a missing `role_key` and on a role whose `is_active` is not true (`user_has_permission()` does not filter on `is_active`, so a grant on a deactivated role would still reach people). `GET DIAGNOSTICS ... ROW_COUNT` is asserted against 4 and 1, the end state is re-asserted by VALUE per role per key, and the roles now holding each key are RAISE NOTICE'd but not enforced. Re-runnable — true over true is a no-op. No `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` in the file, so a reviewer's `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` rehearsal actually rolls back. **Reviewer note:** `20260907120000` is still listed above as FILE ONLY while the keys it grants read as live on production 2026-08-21 — worth resolving, but it does not change this file, which touches only `custom_roles.permissions` and is correct whether or not `sh_solution_first_use` exists yet. | 2026-08-21 | FILE ONLY — not applied
### The prospect-reminders RPC that only ever existed in the repo (2026-08-17)
- `supabase/migrations/20260502000002_prospect_reminder_function.sql` — **REPAIRED IN PLACE and APPLIED to prod 2026-08-17.** This migration has sat on `main` since 2026-05-02 and had **never been applied anywhere** — confirmed on both registers, which agreed for once: absent from `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` AND `sh_get_overdue_prospects` did not exist in `pg_proc`. Edited rather than superseded because an unapplied migration has no deployed history to preserve, and the repo's one-file-one-purpose rule forbids a duplicate.
- **What it cost.** `/api/cron/prospect-reminders` is deployed and fires **every day at 13:53 IST**, and had been returning `HTTP 500 · sh_get_overdue_prospects failed: Could not find the function public.sh_get_overdue_prospects without parameters in the schema cache` on every single run. The classic half-landed PR: the TypeScript half shipped, the SQL half never did.
- 🪤 **The file as written would have shipped an anon-callable RPC.** It carried only `REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC`, which is **not sufficient** — Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT ALL ON FUNCTIONS TO anon` gives every new function a **direct** anon grant that a PUBLIC revoke does not touch. `anon` must be named. Added `REVOKE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` plus a `DO` block that RAISEs if `has_function_privilege('anon', ...)` is still true, or if `service_role` has lost EXECUTE (which would break the cron the migration exists to serve).
- **Proved with a negative control, not asserted.** Dry run inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` returned `anon_can=false, auth_can=false, svc_can=true`. **Narrowed further on 2026-08-31**: the original file granted `authenticated`, which the SECURITY DEFINER authz-guard correctly flags — the function returns EVERY overdue prospect regardless of RLS and checks no authority, so any signed-in account could read the whole pipeline. Its only caller uses `createServiceRoleClient()`, so the revoke costs the cron nothing. The same file with the anon revoke deleted was **REFUSED** — `sh_get_overdue_prospects is still EXECUTE-able by anon` — which is the concrete demonstration that the original grant block was a real hole, not a theoretical one. Residue re-checked in a SEPARATE call after the rollback: 0 functions leaked.
- ⚠ **Reported, not fixed: the routine is now green and still does nothing.** `sh_prospects` has **0 rows**, so the RPC correctly returns 0 and the live route now answers `HTTP 200 · processed 0, notifications_created 0, errors []`. Stopping a nightly 500 is worth doing on its own, but nobody will receive a prospect reminder until prospects exist. Do not read the green as the feature working.

### Learners could not ask a question — six poll systems, none of them audience-to-host (2026-08-21)
- `supabase/migrations/20260821111922_session_question_board.sql` — **⚠️ RE-APPLY PENDING — production holds the ORIGINAL 2026-08-21 version of this file, not the one in the tree.** First applied 2026-08-21 (dry-run in `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` with effective-privilege probes, then committed; ledger row `20260821111922`). The file was then corrected for three defects, so production and this file have diverged until it is re-applied. It is written to be re-run whole: every statement is `CREATE OR REPLACE` / `IF NOT EXISTS`, and both functions whose return signature changed are `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS`-ed immediately before their `CREATE`. What changed — (1) the auto-check now genuinely fails open (see below); (2) a **closed board stays readable** to its learners instead of vanishing, which adds `_fn_session_question_can_read` (**13** RPCs now, not 12) and puts `status` into `fn_session_question_boards_for_learner`'s returned columns; (3) the blocked-term check can now read **Tamil**. Adds the shared session question board: `session_question_board` (polymorphic on `host_type` + `host_id`, so induction / AI Pulse / meetings all use ONE piece rather than a seventh parallel copy — five of the six existing poll systems hold 0 rows), `session_question`, `session_question_vote` (UNIQUE `(question_id, learner_id)` = one upvote per learner) and the curated `session_question_blocked_term` list, plus 13 SECURITY DEFINER RPCs, every one carrying `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM anon, PUBLIC` (anon is a MEMBER of PUBLIC, so revoking anon alone leaves it reachable) and a matching `GRANT … TO authenticated`. Q&A is deliberately NOT a poll `kind`: in a poll the host asks and the audience picks, here the audience asks and the audience ranks. `learner_id` sits on the question and vote rows for enforcement only and is never returned by `fn_session_question_room` — the room sees `Learner <n>`, minted per board so the number carries no meaning on the next board, while `fn_session_question_host_list` returns the real name to the host. The auto-check **fails open**, and as of the correction it actually does: a slow, erroring or unreachable checker leaves the question **visible**, with `moderation_note` marking it posted-unchecked so the host can review what the checker never saw. The first version claimed this but did not deliver it — it wrapped the check in `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS`, and **PL/pgSQL's `WHEN OTHERS` does not match `query_canceled` (57014)**, which is precisely what a `statement_timeout` raises. Reproduced against the real function: with `session_question_blocked_term` held in `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` and a 1s budget, the handler never fired and the learner's question was **lost** (0 rows), not shown. Now the check sets `lock_timeout` transaction-locally first (armed per lock acquisition, unlike `statement_timeout`, so an unreachable term list raises the ordinary catchable `lock_not_available` in milliseconds) and the handler names `query_canceled` **explicitly** alongside `OTHERS`. Same scenario re-run: `{success:true, state:'visible'}` and the question is on the board. Still not survivable, and stated plainly rather than papered over: the whole RPC being killed — at which point no line of the function runs, the client gets an error and the UI renders it, so the learner is told and can retry. A blocked question is still written, and the RPC returns `{success:false, error:…}` in general terms rather than failing silently. `answered_at`/`answered_by` are **sticky** — a host who answers a question and later dismisses it does not erase the fact that it was answered — and `fn_session_question_answered_scoreboard` counts what was **EVER** answered, reporting currently-answered as its own column. That is deliberate: the success test is >=3 sessions with an answered learner question in a month, and a metric an ordinary host action can destroy is not a metric (same class as the `status='active'` filter that once zeroed the CAC funnel). The three internal authority helpers `_fn_session_question_can_host` / `_fn_session_question_can_read` / `_fn_session_question_can_participate` are **revoked from `authenticated`**: every caller is SECURITY DEFINER so it changes no behaviour, but the grant would have let any signed-in user probe "is learner X in the event behind board Y?" one boolean at a time. Boards are created `status='open'`: on everywhere, no staged rollout. **Closing a board makes it read-only, never invisible.** Membership and open-ness are two separate predicates on purpose — `_fn_session_question_can_read` (am I in this room?) versus `_fn_session_question_can_participate` (is it still taking questions?). Read paths ask the first, write paths the second. Fusing them, as the first version did, meant a host closing the board raised `not allowed` out of `fn_session_question_room` and dropped it from `fn_session_question_boards_for_learner`, so the learner's page silently emptied — a state failure disappearing instead of being stated (CLAUDE.md #27) — and took with it the learner-visible record of every **answered** question, which is the very thing the success test counts.
### The record could not name who closed a meeting, so it always named the host (2026-08-24)
- `supabase/migrations/20260926010000_meetings_record_real_closer.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED — Director-gated.** `meeting_bookings.outcome_marked_by` could hold exactly two values on production, `CHECK (outcome_marked_by IS NULL OR outcome_marked_by = ANY (ARRAY['host','system']))` — and **both are KINDS of actor, not people**. So when anyone other than the booking's own host closed a meeting the only thing the record could say was `'host'`, which `app/(routes)/meetings/[uid]/page.tsx` rendered literally as *"Recorded by the host"*: a super admin closing one of the Director's meetings **named the Director as the person who closed it**. Nothing lied — the schema had nowhere to put the real name. Adds `outcome_marked_by_profile_id uuid REFERENCES profiles(id)` (no `ON DELETE`, matching `host_profile_id` on this same table, so deleting a profile cannot quietly erase who closed a meeting); **a separate column on purpose** — `outcome_marked_by` keeps meaning WHICH KIND, identity never gets overloaded onto it. Widens `mb_outcome_marked_by_chk` to `('host','admin','system')` via `DROP ... IF EXISTS` then `ADD` — **not** a guarded `CREATE`, which would find the existing narrow constraint, skip, and leave the bug in place. Adds `mb_outcome_marked_by_person_chk` (`outcome_marked_by NOT IN ('host','admin') OR outcome_marked_by_profile_id IS NOT NULL`) as the **enforcement point**: without it `'admin'` could be written with a NULL identity and the record would be anonymous again, the rule existing in prose and nowhere on the write path. Replaces `fn_meeting_mark_outcome(text, text)`, which hardcoded `outcome_marked_by = 'host'` regardless of caller; it now derives the kind from `auth.uid()` and stamps the actor's id — **the actor is never passed in as an argument**, so a caller cannot claim to be someone else. The gate widens from host-only to **host OR `is_super_admin()`**, deliberately narrow (not `is_admin()`, not a permission key) and not a new idea in this module: `MeetingModeSwitchService` already accepts "the booking's host, or a super admin" for host-side mutations on this same table, and `fn_meeting_mark_outcome` was the odd one out. Recording a non-host actor would otherwise be decorative — no non-host actor could reach the write. Still returns the SAME `not_found` for "missing", "not yours" and "signed out" so a uid is never confirmed to someone with no business knowing it, and still re-asserts `status = 'confirmed'` inside the UPDATE so a concurrent cancel wins. ✅ **NO BACKFILL, measured not assumed:** `outcome_marked_by` is NULL on **all 128 production rows** — no meeting has ever been marked by anyone, so there is no historical attribution to migrate and the shape is fixed before first use. Status CHECK, `mb_no_double_booking`, RLS on `meeting_bookings` and `fn_meetings_auto_close_unmarked` are all untouched; `'system'` stays permitted and stays exempt from the person constraint, so the sweep retired on 2026-08-21 — `app/api/cron/meetings-auto-close/route.ts`, which now performs **no database write at all** — is unaffected. 🔒 Revoke names **`anon, PUBLIC` together, never `anon` alone** (`anon` is a MEMBER of `PUBLIC`, so revoking it alone leaves the PUBLIC grant intact), re-asserted in this file on the `CREATE OR REPLACE`; guard `RAISE EXCEPTION`s — never `NOTICE` — on the new column, on `mb_outcome_marked_by_chk` actually containing `admin` (a constraint that still rejected it would leave the bug in place while every other statement reported success), on the person constraint, on the function existing, and on the **effective** `has_function_privilege('anon', …)` rather than the ACL string. ✅ **Dry-run verified inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` against a local PostgreSQL 16 fixture rebuilt from `20260611190000` + `20260831010000` — including Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES … GRANT ALL ON FUNCTIONS TO anon` trap — whose pre-state constraint reproduced production's definition byte-for-byte:** all statements applied, guard passed, `anon EXECUTE = false` / `authenticated EXECUTE = true`, and the post-rollback probe confirmed the narrow constraint restored and the new column gone. Behaviourally proven on the same fixture: a super admin closing the Director's meeting records `kind = admin, closed_by = Gowrisankar M.N` (previously impossible — the pre-fix constraint **rejects that very row with 23514**), a host closing their own records `kind = host, closed_by = Director`, an ordinary signed-in user and a signed-out caller both get `not_found` with nothing written, an unnamed `'admin'` write is rejected, and a `'system'` row stays legal and unnamed. Version `20260926010000` verified free on `jicate/main` (newest there is `20260925000000`). No `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` in the file, so a reviewer's `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` rehearsal against production actually rolls back. | 2026-08-24 | FILE ONLY — not applied

### Seven of the nine colleges with active learners had no ID card design at all (2026-08-25)
- `supabase/migrations/20261012043000_id_card_templates_seven_colleges.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT YET APPLIED — Director-gated.** Measured on production 2026-08-25: nine institutions carry active learners and only **two** have any row in `id_card_templates` — Engineering (791 active, 2 templates) and Nattraja Vidhyalya CBSE (226 active, 1 dark template from `20260904010000`). The other **seven — 3,922 active learners, 79% of the cluster — have no card design**, so no card can be produced for them at all, and the ordering is backwards on top of it: the largest college by head-count (Arts and Science (Self), 1,243) has none while the college with the worst photo coverage (Engineering, 26%) has two. Seeds one template each for Arts and Science (Self) 1,243/93%, Pharmacy 596/40%, Matric Higher Secondary School 552/0%, Dental 498/65%, Arts and Science (Aided) 484/75%, Nursing 277/40%, Allied Health 272/75% (active = `lifecycle_status = 'active'`; photo counts `student_photo_url` non-null **and non-empty** — the empty string is a real value in that column and counting it as a photo overstates coverage). **One shared design, per Director decision 11:** every element, coordinate, colour, font size and field mapping is copied verbatim from the live Engineering tall layout `ad0642ec-10c5-4b06-859e-7006734eb8f8`, read read-only, exactly as the Nattraja file did — this adds no new card design. `front_layout_json.background_image` is **dropped**, because the source points at artwork carrying JKKN College of Engineering branding and none of the seven has artwork of its own (`institutions.logo_url` is the empty string for all seven); that absence is the main reason all seven ship dark. 🛑 **Six of the seven get NO contact block, and that is the one real decision in the file.** The Engineering back carries three hard-coded static lines (`PH: 99659 39333, 99653 63999, 93458 55001` / `engg@jkkn.ac.in` / `www.engg.jkkn.ac.in`) which are Engineering's, so the correct source is each institution's own row — and that row turns out to hold a **placeholder** for six of the seven: `phone = '9876543210'` on **8 of the 14** institutions, `email = 'admin@jkkn.ac.in'` on **9 of 14**, `website = 'https://www.jkkn.ac.in/'` on **7 of 14**. `9876543210` is the textbook fake Indian mobile (digits running 9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1-0) shared byte-for-byte by eight institutions. **The decisive evidence that the column is not maintained is Engineering itself:** its `institutions` row says `9876543210` / `admin@jkkn.ac.in` / `www.jkkn.ac.in/` while its LIVE card prints three different real numbers and `engg.jkkn.ac.in` — whoever built that card did not take the contacts from this table, because this table does not have them. So the three elements are **omitted rather than filled**: a card with no phone number on the back is recoverable, a card printing `9876543210` to 3,370 learners is a reprint. **Exactly one college does have institution-specific contacts and gets them**, verbatim and unverified, exactly as Nattraja did: JKKN Matric Higher Secondary School — `PH: 99658 91999` / `school@jkkn.org` / `school.jkkn.ac.in`, dropped into the same three y-positions (800/836/870) the source used. ⚠️ **Matric Higher Secondary School is flagged, not guessed** — three things a reviewer must decide before that one template is switched on: (a) `lib/utils/school-label-adapter.ts` **does** apply to it (`entity_type = 'school'`) but the ID-card renderer **never calls it** — `adaptLabel` appears nowhere under `lib/id-cards/` — so the card's static `COURSE :` label sits over a value read from `programs.program_name`, which for this school is `Standard 12`, where the repo's own school vocabulary maps Program → Class; changing the label means this college no longer shares the one design, which is a Director call. (b) **0 of its 552** active learners carry a `batch_id`, so `study_period` and `valid_until` both resolve empty while the static `YEAR :` and `VALID UPTO` headings still draw — `static_text` renders unconditionally (`lib/id-cards/render-card.tsx`) — so its card would print two headings with nothing under them. (c) **0 of its 552** have a photo, and the photo is the identity control on a printed card, making this the least ready of the seven. 🔒 **All seven ship DARK** (`active = FALSE`), invisible to every print picker (`lib/services/id-cards/template-picker.ts`, guard workflow `id-card-template-picker.yml`) and reachable only from the admin design tabs; a non-vacuous guard `RAISE EXCEPTION`s — never `NOTICE` — if that `FALSE` literal is ever edited to `TRUE`, scoped to a row the run actually inserted so a replay after a legitimate activation stays a clean no-op. No table, function, policy or grant is created or altered, so there is **no SECURITY DEFINER surface and no EXECUTE grant to re-assert**; no existing template row is read for update or modified; no print job is enqueued. Proof the file never applied, read from the repository rather than asserted: `types/supabase.ts` is generated from the live database and carries neither `grievance_tickets.issue_type` nor any `requirement_requests` table, while `lib/services/issues/issue-service.ts` already queries both. FOUR defects fixed, nothing else rewritten — the file is ONE transaction (`BEGIN` L49 → `COMMIT`), so any single bad statement means none of the 941 lines apply. **(a)** the `platform_policies` seed targeted `ON CONFLICT (policy_key, scope_type, scope_id)`, but uniqueness on that table is the EXPRESSION index `uq_platform_policies_key_scope (policy_key, scope_type, COALESCE(scope_id, '000…0'::uuid))` — 42P10, transaction aborted; now the COALESCE form that 66 other migration files already use. **(b)** the same seed omitted `data_type`, which is NOT NULL with no default and CHECK-constrained to `number|string|boolean|array|object|enum`; `ON CONFLICT` cannot rescue a NOT NULL violation. All five rows hold a scalar number, so all five are `'number'`. **(c)** the rename above. **(d)** RLS on `grievance_tickets`: the ICC branch of `grievance_tickets_select` carried NO `role_has_institution_access(institution_id)` while the ordinary branch two lines below always has, so a single `icc_member` role would have read confidential complaints across all 8 colleges — added to the SELECT and UPDATE policies; and `raised_by_id = auth.uid()` sat INSIDE the `is_icc_only = false` branch, so a complainant lost sight of her own case the moment it was marked confidential — hoisted so it holds for every row. `filed_by`/`assigned_to` were deliberately NOT hoisted (both are writable on an existing row, so hoisting would open a path to hand a third party read access to a confidential complaint). The DELETE policy is `is_super_admin() OR is_admin()` with no ICC or identity branch and is otherwise unchanged. **Second, independent proof the file never applied, and a regression it would have caused:** `supabase/migrations/rls_initplan_wrap_sweep.sql` line 2058 records the LIVE `grievance_tickets_select` read back from production on 2026-07-31 — it carries NO `is_icc_only` branch at all, i.e. production is still running the `20260423_unification_crud_retrofit.sql` policy. Two consequences. (ii) That sweep wrapped every per-row-constant call in a scalar sub-select (bare `auth.uid()` policies 1,273 -> 1), so recreating these three policies with bare calls would have silently undone it for this table — all three are now written in the wrapped form (`(SELECT auth.uid())`, `(SELECT is_super_admin())`, `(SELECT is_admin())`, `(SELECT user_has_permission(...))`), with `role_has_institution_access(institution_id)` deliberately left bare because it takes a per-row column and is not a per-row constant. ### Campus Walk D12 — somewhere for a step reading to land, and an honest empty board (2026-09-03)
- `supabase/migrations/20261103020000_campus_walk_step_days.sql` — **FILE ONLY — NOT APPLIED TO ANY DATABASE.** Creates `campus_walk_step_days` (one row per person per calendar day: `profile_id` → `profiles`, `step_date date`, `steps integer CHECK (steps >= 0)`, `source text`, `recorded_at`, `updated_at`, UNIQUE `(profile_id, step_date)`, index on `(profile_id, step_date DESC)`), plus `fn_campus_walk_step_days_touch()` and its BEFORE UPDATE trigger so a corrected day moves `updated_at` while `recorded_at` keeps the first arrival. Additive only: no existing table, constraint, policy or function is touched, so it cannot regress anything live. **Access is service_role only** — RLS enabled with deliberately NO policies plus `REVOKE ALL … FROM anon, authenticated, PUBLIC`, because this is one named person's daily activity and Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` would otherwise hand it to the browser's anon key; the real boundary is the same app-level gate the rest of the module uses (`lib/campus-walk/reporters.ts` → the `campus_walk.reporters.allowed_emails` policy row seeded in `20261102030000`, failing CLOSED to the Director alone). **THE RULE THIS SCHEMA ENCODES:** a day with no reading is an ABSENT ROW, never a row holding zero — zero claims somebody walked nowhere, absent claims nobody measured, and only the second is true; the intake route additionally refuses `steps = 0` for that reason. **READ BEFORE ASSUMING D12 WORKS:** this is an ingestion surface, not a pipeline — as of 2026-09-03 **nothing sends step readings to MyJKKN and applying this migration does not change that.** Every reading that has ever existed was written by a sync job on the Director's own machine into a local Obsidian vault, which a deployed web app cannot read; something must POST to `app/api/campus-walk/scoreboard/steps` and that sender does not exist. `/campus-walk/scoreboard/coverage` states this in plain words rather than drawing a flat line that would read as "he did not walk". **AND THE GAP IS NOT A BROKEN JOB:** verified 2026-09-03 — that sync job ran that morning, its API token is valid, it cached fresh responses for 2026-09-01/02/03, and its own log line is "0 written, 3 days with no ring data" (an August backfill: "163 written, 99 days with no ring data"). There has been no reading since 2026-04-18 because the wearable stopped producing them; no code phrases that as a software failure, and `__tests__/campus-walk/scoreboard.test.ts` asserts the user-facing strings never do. Per spec §5 the table holds a date and a step count and nothing else — body measurements, blood-test results, sleep, heart rate and diet plans stay in the Director's private vault. Version `20261103020000` is above main's ceiling (`20261102030000`) and clear of `20261103000000` / `20261103010000`, claimed by parallel lanes.

correct on an ACTIVE row whose `last_correct_session_id` is not this sitting's `fp_attempts.session_id` AND which is due (`next_eligible_at <= now()`) ⇒ streak+1, session stamped; streak ≥ `onemark.vault.mastery_streak` (2) ⇒ mastered; else `next_eligible_at = now() + onemark.vault.min_gap_days` (2) days; same sitting, not yet due, or mastered ⇒ no change. **(3)** `fn_onemark_record_response(p_attempt_id uuid, p_item_id uuid, p_chosen jsonb, p_skipped boolean, p_time_ms int) RETURNS jsonb` — SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path=public`, caller must pass the estate's attempt-WRITE gate — `fn_fp_can_manage_student` OR `fn_fp_is_own_or_guardian` OR `fn_fp_teaches_student`, the exact predicate of `fn_fp_record_attempt` (20260808220000) — NOT the read predicate `fn_fp_can_view_student` (42501 otherwise); attempt must be `in_progress` (23514 — decision 19) AND an OneMark attempt (`mode` set; a legacy `mode IS NULL` Foundation attempt is refused 23514 — `fn_fp_record_attempt` owns those and stores `score` as a 0..1 RATIO); the item must be on the attempt's exam and, when the assessment is a fixed paper with `fp_assessment_items` rows, one of them (23514 otherwise). **Two grading regimes by `fp_attempts.mode`.** `practice` / `vault_review` = REVEALED: graded now, verdict returned, and — once per attempt-item — the first response of any kind bumps `fp_items.times_served`, the first GRADED (non-skipped) answer bumps `times_correct` if correct and moves the vault; any later re-answer overwrites the response row (the last answer is what the score counts) and touches nothing else, because the learner has already seen the verdict — so skip-then-wrong reaches the vault, skip-then-correct counts as correct in the bank, and wrong-then-correct-then-wrong counts ONE wrong. `timed` / `live` = WITHHELD: only chosen / skipped / time_ms are stored, `is_correct` stays NULL, no counters, no vault, and the return carries `is_correct` / `vault_status` / `streak` as NULL with `revealed=false` — a learner can SELECT their own `fp_responses` (`fn_fp_can_view_attempt`) and vault rows (`fn_fp_can_view_student`) mid-paper, so a verdict stored ANYWHERE would be an answer-key oracle (try each option, read the verdict, keep the winner); the verdicts are written only by finalize. Returns `{is_correct, skipped, vault_status, streak, revealed}` — never the answer key. **(4)** `fn_onemark_vault_draw(p_student_id uuid, p_exam_definition_id uuid, p_count int) RETURNS SETOF uuid` — STABLE SECURITY DEFINER, caller gate = `fn_fp_can_view_student` (the READ predicate, per the lane spec — a draw returns item ids only); active + due vault rows whose item is active and on that exam, `next_eligible_at ASC` (precisely: least recently TOUCHED — a counted correct pushes the row forward too — which is decision 13's intent), no single `fp_items.topic_id` above `floor(p_count × onemark.vault.max_single_chapter_pct / 100)` with a floor of 1 (60 ⇒ 5 requested gives at most 3 per chapter; `p_count=1` ⇒ one item — shorter, not empty); fewer rather than padded (decision 13). NULL topic is one bucket under the same cap. **(5)** `fn_onemark_finalize_attempt(p_attempt_id uuid) RETURNS jsonb` — same write gate; locks the attempt; refuses `submitted` (decision 19), `abandoned` (a value of the `fp_attempts` status CHECK that must not be revived into a score) and `mode IS NULL` (legacy ratio unit); on a FIXED paper inserts a skipped response for every `fp_assessment_items` row that has none (decision 18 — "unanswered = skipped" without the client enumerating blanks; a POOL attempt has no item list here, so Lane V's finalize route still posts its `skippedItemIds` as skipped responses first, which it does); on `timed` / `live` grades the FINAL answer of every response now (`is_correct` backfilled, `times_served` + 1 per response, `times_correct` + 1 per correct, vault per answer — correct-then-changed-to-wrong is a wrong, skip-then-wrong is a wrong; decision 19 holds); sets `submitted_at`, `status='submitted'`, `score = count(is_correct)` (skipped ≠ wrong, decision 18). Returns `{attempt_id, mode, score, correct, answered, skipped, unanswered_backfilled, submitted_at}`. ⚠️ UNIT: `fn_fp_record_attempt` stores `score` as a 0..1 ratio; OneMark attempts store the COUNT — readers key on `fp_attempts.mode`.
