### AI Pulse feed moderation — global shelf goes nameless + a cleared verdict becomes appealable (2026-08-05)
- `supabase/migrations/20260805120000_ai_pulse_global_shelf_and_flag_recency.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Director decisions #6 and #9 of `specs/ai-pulse-feed-moderation-decisions-2026-07-30.md`, one predicate each in two different read functions. **#6** `fn_ai_pulse_topic_peer_prompts`: `author_name` becomes `CASE WHEN p_topic_type = 'global' THEN NULL ELSE <the existing expression> END`, so the shared "All JKKN" shelf is nameless while programme and course shelves are unchanged — that shelf has neither a name filter nor an institution filter, and a real school↔college bridge exists in prod (the course name `VALUE EDUCATION` exists in 3 institutions, one of them JKKN Matric Higher Secondary School). The concern is how far a name TRAVELS, not whose it is; decision #7 keeps past learners named. The UI needed no change — `classmates-prompts-card.tsx` already falls back to the neutral label `A classmate` when `author_name` is null. **#9** `fn_ai_pulse_topic_graduated_prompts`: `report_cleared_at` stops being a PERMANENT shield. The `b.report_cleared_at IS NULL AND …` outer prefix is dropped and recency moves INSIDE the count as `AND (b.report_cleared_at IS NULL OR r.created_at > b.report_cleared_at)`, so flags filed after a clear count again while flags the champion already dismissed stay dismissed and can never resurrect a build on their own. **Both bodies were authored from the LIVE definitions** (`pg_get_functiondef`, prod 2026-07-30: peer `dc0a4d9cec1b9ca264df4af87324cc45`, graduated `d931e57af2996f6be074837adc49dfd1`), never from a repo file — a `CREATE OR REPLACE` written from a stale migration has silently reverted a live gate in this codebase before; a byte-for-byte diff against live shows the two predicates and their comments as the only deviations, leaving the feed kill-switch, the fail-closed `safety_status='passed'` gate, the 60–79 band, the `disqualified_at` guard, the `duplicate_of` canonical-only filter, the 1-year retire window and the LEFT (never INNER) joins intact. Each replace re-asserts `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM anon, PUBLIC` in the same file, because Supabase's `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` re-grants `anon` EXECUTE on every function it sees created, including a replace. Rehearsed on prod inside transactions that end in `RAISE EXCEPTION` (so they can only abort, never commit): the feed returns zero rows today for two independent reasons — `prompt_classmates_feed_enabled` is `false` and no build is `safety_status='passed'` — so the whole world was constructed in-transaction and discarded. Results: global shelf 1 row `author_name = NULL`, course shelf 1 row `author_name = MONEESH G`; with the migration absent the same world leaked `DEEPIKA R` onto the global shelf, which is what makes the change causal rather than incidental. For #9, two fresh flags after a clear removed the build (present 1 → 0) while the same two flags dated before the clear left it present, and the never-cleared case still hides at the threshold read live from `prompt_report_autohide_threshold` (2). A separate call then confirmed both md5s unchanged, the flag still `false`, the spread still 1 `failed` / 7 `pending`, zero report rows added and `anon` holding no EXECUTE.

### The public programme catalogue — a page an outsider can browse without logging in (2026-09-05)
- `supabase/migrations/20260905010000_public_programme_catalogue.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED — Director-gated.** Creates `public_programmes`, the single table read by the new public page `app/(public)/programmes`. **Why a new table and not a marker on something that exists:** `programs` is the degree spine that attendance, billing, timetables and the board of studies all join — an `is_public` boolean there would put every one of those rows one flag away from the open web, on a table many screens can already edit, which is leak-by-omission; and `cohorts` is the internal intake structure where School of Influence lives, which the Director ruled on 2026-08-13 is **not** a public programme (JKKN learners and senior learners only, `allow_external_registration=false`), so hanging the catalogue there would put the two one column apart. This table's only reason to exist is to be published, so nothing arrives in it by inheriting a flag. **Default closed at three layers:** `is_published BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false`; the RLS policy `public_programmes_select_published` (`TO anon, authenticated USING (is_published)`); and `PublicProgrammeService.listPublished()` filtering it again, which is the layer that actually protects the rendered page because that page reads through the service-role client where RLS is bypassed. Second policy `public_programmes_admin_all` gives `is_super_admin() OR is_admin()` full read/write — **no new permission key is registered on purpose**, because this PR ships the reader and not an admin screen, and a key no role holds would be a dark lane; the key arrives with the screen that needs it. **Grants are explicit:** `REVOKE ALL … FROM anon, PUBLIC` first (Supabase's default privileges otherwise give the anon key INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE the moment the table is born), then `GRANT SELECT TO anon` — deliberate, documented in the file header, and the audit-trail signal that this relation is public on purpose — plus the normal `authenticated` DML and `service_role` grants. **Seeds zero rows, on purpose:** JKKN has no public programme today, the first will be the forthcoming paid programme sold to companies, and the page is written so its empty state reads as deliberate rather than broken. **Privacy is enforced by the schema, not by the query:** there is no column for a coordinator, a contact person or any count of people, so the page cannot render what it must not show. Five CHECK constraints — slug shape, non-negative fee, free-and-priced mutually exclusive, `ends_on >= starts_on`, and `apply_url ~ '^(https?://|/)'` so no other scheme can reach a rendered href. **No SECURITY DEFINER function is added** (the public page reads through the service-role client, the same pattern as `app/(public)/meet/page.tsx`), so there is no RPC to lock. Closing `DO` block asserts RLS on, anon holding SELECT and **not** INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and `authenticated` keeping SELECT, so a partial apply cannot look successful. Version `20260905010000` checked free against `jicate/main` (max `20260903041500`) and against every open pull request (max claimed `20260904113000`). No `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` in the file, so a reviewer's `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` rehearsal against production actually rolls back. | 2026-08-14 | FILE ONLY — not applied

The route builds the object in one place, lower-cases it, checks the uuid shape and re-runs that membership test before insert; a recipient failing any check is counted and reported, never dropped quietly.

### `ai_pulse_live_attendance.left_at` has never been written — and reads as a confident zero (2026-08-21)
- `supabase/migrations/20261104020000_ai_pulse_left_at_deprecate_comment.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED — Director-gated.** **COMMENT ON COLUMN only — adds no object, alters no type or nullability, drops nothing, backfills nothing, touches no policy, function, trigger or grant; idempotent, instantly reversible (`COMMENT ... IS NULL`), takes no rewrite lock.** Measured on production 2026-08-21: **3,631 rows, `left_at` NOT NULL on 0 of them** since the table was created 2026-06-11, while `joined_at` is set on 3,228 and `engagement_signals->'stayed_until'` on 2,568. **The failure is silent, not loud** — `left_at` is a nullable TIMESTAMPTZ on a well-populated table, so an ad-hoc duration query, a Studio report or a "how long did they stay" dashboard gets a confident NULL/zero that is indistinguishable from a real measurement of *never left*. **Root cause, and it is a single mistake:** the only writer of the column, `app/api/ai-pulse/meet/webhook/route.ts`, targeted `event_team_attendance` — the per-TEAM table keyed by `registration_id`, which has **no `left_at`, no `joined_at` and no `learner_id` column** — and additionally selected `startup_events.starts_at`, which also does not exist. Its first SELECT therefore failed 42703 and it returned 500 before reaching `ai_pulse_live_attendance`; **it could never once have succeeded.** Migration `20260611_ai_pulse_live_attendance_and_champion.sql` created the per-learner table for exactly this reason and its header names the same imagined shape — `live-session-service.ts` was moved onto the new table then, and this route was missed. The accompanying PR repoints the route and removes the last application read of the column. **Leave time lives in `engagement_signals`, verified not assumed:** `last_heartbeat_at` (ISO, last observed moment) and `stayed_until` (that instant as IST "HH:MM") co-occur on exactly the same 2,568 rows — **0 rows carry one without the other** — and `stayed_until = to_char(last_heartbeat_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kolkata','HH24:MI')` on **2,568 of 2,568**, so `stayed_until` is a *rendering* of `last_heartbeat_at`, not an independent fact. ⚠️ **No backfill, deliberately, and the obvious one is impossible:** `stayed_until` is a dateless wall-clock string, so it cannot become a TIMESTAMPTZ; the only ISO source is `last_heartbeat_at`, which is a HEARTBEAT (last-observed) and not a leave event — copying it into a column named `left_at` would manufacture a precise-looking claim the data does not support. 🔒 **Not a DROP, deliberately:** a DROP is destructive, forces a `types/supabase.ts` regeneration and must be sequenced against a deploy, and buys nothing this comment does not — after the accompanying PR there are **0 application reads, 0 views and 0 functions** referencing the column (verified against `pg_proc` and `information_schema.views` 2026-08-21). Dropping it stays available as a separate, separately-gated decision. **The comment is the only warning a schema-reader ever gets** — the code-side guardrails live in TypeScript files that an analyst writing SQL in Studio is not reading. Post-apply: **118 preference rows**, all `push_enabled=false`, matching the 118 distinct opted-out users exactly; **all 109 resurrected users covered, 0 unprotected**. The schema is live but the CODE is not until this PR merges — safe, because `lib/push/opt-out.ts` treats a missing table (`42P01`/`PGRST205`) as "feature not live". Creates `public.push_notification_preferences` (`user_id` UNIQUE → `auth.users`, `push_enabled` default true, `opted_out_at`), modelled on the existing `email_notification_preferences` precedent, and **backfills every user who currently holds an `is_active = false` `push_subscriptions` row** — read on production 2026-08-21, ~118 people, 109 of whom were being messaged again. ⚠️ **No `is_active` filter could ever have fixed this, and every sender's filter was already correct.** Unsubscribing calls `subscription.unsubscribe()` in the browser, which DESTROYS that endpoint; on the next visit `Notification.permission` is still `granted` and `getSubscription()` is null, so the auto-subscribe effect mints a **brand-new endpoint** and posts it. A new endpoint is a new row, so it is a fresh INSERT (or, on `/api/dashboard/push-subscribe`, an upsert that sets `is_active: true` explicitly) and it satisfies every sender's filter perfectly — the opt-out signal had been stored on the very object the opt-out deletes. The preference therefore lives on the **person**. ⚠️ **The UI unsubscribe button left no trace at all** before this: `/api/notifications/subscribe` DELETE hard-deletes the row, so the 160 `is_active = false` rows on production all came from the *other* endpoint's soft-delete, not from the button. RLS is super-admin/admin `FOR ALL` plus own-row SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE (`user_id = auth.uid()`) — deliberately **no permission-key policy**, because a preference about being left alone should not become readable platform-wide with a notifications key, and every sender already reads through a service-role client that bypasses RLS. Own-row **INSERT** is granted, not only UPDATE, because the first opt-out creates the row and `/api/dashboard/push-subscribe` is deliberately user-scoped; it is no more permissive than the UPDATE policy already is. DELETE is admin-only — removing the row does not undo an opt-out, it erases the only evidence one was ever made, after which the next auto-subscribe silently resurrects the person. `REVOKE ALL ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` (both named: anon is a member of PUBLIC, so revoking anon alone leaves PUBLIC granting it straight back), and the one SECURITY DEFINER function here — the `updated_at` trigger `fn_push_notification_preferences_touch()` — carries the same paired revoke plus `GRANT ... TO authenticated`. Backfill uses `INSERT ... SELECT DISTINCT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO NOTHING`, so it is idempotent and **cannot overwrite a live preference** if re-applied after somebody has switched push back on; a `RAISE NOTICE` prints candidates-vs-inserted. Ships with the code that consults it: 8 of 8 sender reads now gate on the preference, both POST handlers refuse to write a subscription for an opted-out person (200 + `skipped: 'user_opted_out'`, not an error), and both DELETE handlers record the opt-out. ⚠️ **Until this file is applied the register does not exist** — the helper (`lib/push/opt-out.ts`) treats `42P01`/`PGRST205` as "feature not live" and senders behave exactly as before; any *other* read error fails **closed** and the batch is skipped, because a delayed notification is recoverable and re-buzzing 109 people who asked for silence is not.
### Doctrines weekly cards: a whole week in one statement, not one round-trip per user (2026-08-17)
- `supabase/migrations/20260908120000_doctrines_bulk_emit_cards.sql` — **APPLIED to prod 2026-08-17.** Adds `fn_doctrines_emit_cards(jsonb)`, a SECURITY DEFINER bulk emitter for `/api/cron/friday-reflection` and `/api/cron/sunday-wrap`. Creates no table and grants nothing new to any human role.
- **What was broken.** Both routes looped over every eligible profile in JS, making TWO sequential PostgREST round-trips per user (a SELECT on `idempotency_key`, then an INSERT): **13,410** round-trips for friday-reflection's 6,705 users, **13,626** for sunday-wrap's 6,813. The AI-routine dispatcher aborts any routine at **120s** (`AbortSignal.timeout(120_000)`), so both were cut off mid-loop and recorded `error: The operation was aborted due to timeout`.
- 🪤 **They were not dead — they were PARTIAL, which is worse**, because the truncation left no trace in the output. Measured coverage per run: `sunday-wrap` served **1,894 of 6,813 (28%)** on 08-16, and the share was **falling every week** — 2,374 → 2,146 → 2,029 → 1,935 → 1,870 → 1,841 — as `notifications` grew (298,721 rows) and each per-user lookup cost fractionally more. `friday-reflection` was erratic: **6,703** on 08-14 but **51** on 07-10. ~4,900 people missed their wrap weekly, and which people was arbitrary.
- 🪤 **Why an RPC and not `.upsert({ onConflict })`.** `idx_notifications_idempotency` is a **PARTIAL** unique index (`WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL`). Postgres will not infer a partial index from a bare `ON CONFLICT (col)`, and PostgREST's `on_conflict` parameter cannot express a predicate — so the obvious one-line bulk upsert raises **42P10** on every call. Proven on prod before the code was written: the bare form returned `42P10`, the same insert with `WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL` on the conflict target returned 201. Same failure class as `20260809000000`. ASSERT 1 refuses the migration if that predicate is ever removed.
- **service_role ONLY, deliberately narrower than the house template.** The function writes notifications addressed at **arbitrary caller-supplied user ids**; granting `authenticated` would let any signed-in learner notify anyone in the cluster. `anon` and `authenticated` are both revoked, and ASSERT 3 refuses the migration if either regains EXECUTE.
- **Measured, not asserted.** Full-scale rollback test: **all 6,705 friday cards emitted in 1.4s** (`inserted 6705, skipped_duplicate 0`), residue re-checked in a separate call = 0. A replay of the same payload inserted 0 and skipped 1, so dedupe survives the batching. Negative control: the same migration with the `ON CONFLICT` predicate deleted was **REFUSED** by ASSERT 1.
- **`sunday-wrap` also reordered.** `fn_precompute_percentile_cache` measured at **79 seconds** — two thirds of the 120s budget, spent before a single wrap was written. It warms the cache for the week's later `fn_cluster_rank_private` calls, which the wrap itself does not use, so it now runs **last**: user-visible work completes first, and if the abort lands during the cache warm nothing a person sees is lost. Per-user score RPCs (~20ms each, ~135s sequential) now run at concurrency 20 (~7s) — same RPCs, same results, just not serialised.
### PDE enrolment confined to the learner's own institution (2026-08-08)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808190100_vac_enrollments_same_institution_only.sql` — **NOT applied to any database.** Adds `fn_vac_may_enrol_in_course(uuid)` plus two RESTRICTIVE policies (`vac_enrollments_insert_same_institution`, `vac_enrollments_update_same_institution`). Rehearsed on prod inside a Mgmt-API `BEGIN … ROLLBACK`; residue verified 0 in a SEPARATE call, twice (helper absent, both policies absent, 4 policies total, 550 enrolments unchanged).
- **The hole, reproduced live before writing a line of the fix.** `vac_enrollments_insert` is `WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid() OR super_admin)` — it constrains WHO the row is for and places no constraint at all on `course_id`. Any authenticated caller could enrol themselves in ANY course at ANY institution with one POST using the public anon key. Confirmed against today's policies in a rollback transaction: the cross-institution INSERT **succeeded**, rows=1.
- **`vac_enrollments_update` carries the identical hole and is closed in the same file.** Its `with_check` is NULL in production, so PostgreSQL reuses the `USING` expression — `user_id = auth.uid()` — as the check. A learner could enrol legitimately at their own college and then re-point that row's `course_id` at any course anywhere. Also reproduced live: the UPDATE re-point **succeeded**, rows=1. Closing INSERT alone would have left a one-request bypass.
- **RESTRICTIVE, never a rewrite.** Permissive policies OR together and can only widen, so they are the wrong instrument for a narrowing fix; RESTRICTIVE policies AND with the permissive result. Neither live policy is dropped or re-created, so this file cannot repeat the regression where a `CREATE OR REPLACE` from a stale repo file silently reverted a live tightening.
- **SECURITY DEFINER is load-bearing.** Inlining the institution join would re-evaluate `vac_courses_select`, which demands an ACTIVE `user_institution_access` row that 544 of 545 enrolled learners do not hold — the inlined version would deny every legitimate same-institution enrolment. The helper has three branches: super admin, own-institution match, and an active cross-institution grant (branch 3 keeps a cross-college team member working; it grants an ordinary learner nothing, since they hold no such row). Never takes a caller-supplied identity — it reads `auth.uid()` itself.
- Lock: `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM anon, PUBLIC` then `GRANT … TO authenticated`, asserted in-transaction from `has_function_privilege` — anon `f`, PUBLIC `f`, authenticated `t`. `TO authenticated` on both policies is load-bearing too: without it the policy would apply to PUBLIC and an anon write would raise *permission denied for function* instead of the RLS denial. Verified: anon SELECT returned 0 rows with no function error, anon INSERT rejected `42501` with the generic message.
- **Both directions proven, not asserted.** With the file applied in-transaction: same-institution self-enrolment **INSERTED** (rows=1); cross-institution INSERT **rejected 42501** by `vac_enrollments_insert_same_institution`; cross-institution UPDATE **rejected 42501** by `vac_enrollments_update_same_institution`; an ordinary status/payment update on the same row still **succeeded** (rows=1), which is the only update shape `lib/services/vac/vac-service.ts` ever issues.
- **Existing rows: nothing to backfill.** Of 550 live enrolments, 547 already satisfy the constraint, **0 are true cross-institution**, and 3 have a `user_id` with no `profiles` row. Both policies are write-time, so no existing row is re-validated, deleted or modified. The 3 orphans stay administrable because the UPDATE policy leaves `USING` unrestricted and constrains only where the row lands.
- **NULL on either side is not a match — measured, not assumed.** 6 of 93 courses have `institution_id IS NULL` (all six `is_active = false`, zero enrolments) and 18 of 7,227 profiles do (zero enrolments), so the strict reading costs nothing today; a future institution-less course would be enrollable by a super admin only. Stated so it is a decision, not a surprise.
- Carries no `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;` of its own so a Mgmt-API `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` stays a genuine dry run. Idempotent (`DROP POLICY IF EXISTS` + `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION`).
- `supabase/migrations/20260828020000_revoke_anon_admitted_source_fns.sql` — **FILE ONLY / NOT APPLIED — Director-gated.** Grants only; no function body is created, replaced or altered, so no `CREATE OR REPLACE` and no anon-revoke re-assertion applies. Both are `prosecdef`, owner `postgres`, and both carry the identical ACL `=X/postgres postgres=X/postgres authenticated=X/postgres service_role=X/postgres`; **neither holds an `anon=X` entry of its own**, so `REVOKE ... Production does **not** do that. Rehearsed inside `BEGIN..ROLLBACK`, residue then verified `0` **in a separate API call** (the Management API wraps one batch in one transaction, so an in-batch check would have read its own uncommitted state). The live apply matched the rehearsal exactly: `hr_staff_details` 543 → 583 rows, `designation_id` and `cadre_id` set on **314** (274 UPDATE + 40 INSERT), both `0` beforehand. Cadres now populated: Teaching 284 · Supporting (Technical) 20 · Non-Technical 9 · Administrative 1. **543 people remain unsorted** and are the work the new screen exists to do.
- 🪤 **The column the build order asked for must NOT be created.** The instruction was `public.staff.designation_id uuid NULL REFERENCES hr_designations(id)`. Read live 2026-08-03 against `kvizhngldtiuufknvehv`: `public.staff.designation_id` does not exist, but **`hr_staff_details.designation_id` does** — nullable, with `hr_staff_details_designation_id_fkey → hr_designations(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`, exactly the link requested — alongside `hr_staff_details.cadre_id` and `hr_staff_details_cadre_id_fkey → hr_cadres(id)`. Adding the `staff` column would put one fact in two places, which is the second-vocabulary failure this work was explicitly told to avoid. Merged **PR #2664** (2026-07-30) exists *because* `payslip-generator.ts` selected `designation_id` from `staff`, where it does not exist, and returned `42703` for every caller; it moved payroll onto `hr_staff_details`. `lib/services/hr/employee-service.ts` already filters on `hr_staff_details.designation_id` and `.cadre_id` today. The migration therefore only fills the existing column in.
- **It also makes the screen work on deploy rather than after the apply.** Because the column already exists in production, `/hr/admin/designation-mapping` reads and writes correctly the moment it deploys and honestly reports `0 of 150 job titles sorted`. Had the feature depended on a brand-new `public.staff.designation_id`, the page would have been broken from deploy until the Director applied the migration.
- **Exact case-insensitive name match only, inside one institution:** `btrim(lower(d.name)) = btrim(lower(s.designation))` joined `public.staff → hr_organizations (institution_id) → hr_designations`. No fuzzy match, no prefix match, no nearest guess. Production carries one 12-person title and an 11-person misspelling of it (the exact pair is quoted in the unit test's comment) — one character apart, two different rows a human must judge — and `Reader` (15) is a prefix of `Reader & HOD` (4), a different job. Everything unmatched stays NULL so it reads as unsorted.
- 🪤 **The build order's "320 of 857" is the UNSCOPED number.** Measured live: the institution-scoped match the same sentence mandates resolves **314**, not 320; dropping the institution join gives exactly 320. Likewise the "136 distinct unmapped designations" is **137** when scoped (150 distinct case-insensitive titles − 13 matched). The scoped, safer number is what shipped. `Senior Lecturer` is 30 not 27, the upper-case nursing variant of `Tutor` is 23 not 22 and `Tutor` itself 15 not 14, because case variants collapse (`Senior Lecturer` + `SENIOR LECTURER`); `Attender` 35, `Bus Driver` 30, `Lecturer` 26, `PG Assistant` 21, `Dental College Ayaah` 21, `Girls Hostel Scavenger` 16 and `Reader` 15 all confirmed as written.
- **Ambiguity guard, not decoration.** A `count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY s.id)` window drops any team member whose title resolves to more than one designation. Live there are **0** duplicate designation names per organisation so it drops nothing today, but without it a future duplicate would hit the same `staff_id` twice in one `INSERT … ON CONFLICT` and abort the whole migration with `cardinality_violation` (21000).
- **Never overwrites a human's decision:** the `ON CONFLICT` branch carries `WHERE hr_staff_details.designation_id IS NULL`, so it fills blanks only. `cadre_id` is written alongside `designation_id` from the same row, so the pair cannot drift.
- **Proved by dry run inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` (the file contains no `COMMIT`), then verified rolled back in a SEPARATE call.** Inside the transaction: designation_id set **0 → 314**, cadre_id **0 → 314**, `hr_staff_details` **543 → 583** (274 updated, 40 inserted), and three invariants all **0** — designation/cadre disagreement, cross-institution link, and any link whose names do not match. Resulting split: **284 teaching, 30 not teaching** (the 30 are the Bus Drivers), **543 still unsorted**. After rollback, re-read separately: `hr_staff_details` back to **543**, designation_id set **0**, cadre_id set **0**, and `public.staff.designation_id` still absent.
- **Deliberately does NOT touch `public.staff.role_type` or `public.staff.employment_type`.** Both are uniform across all 857 rows today (`role_type='teacher'` on every row including Bus Driver and Attender; `employment_type='full_time'` on every row, so 'permanent' is recorded nowhere). Rewriting them from a partial mapping would replace one wrong answer with a differently wrong one; the cadre link is the source of truth from here and those columns are a separate Director decision.
- ⚠ **Reported, not changed — the screen can be silently empty for 3 of its 4 intended users.** `hr_staff_details`, `hr_designations` and `hr_cadres` are all gated by `hr_organization_id = auth_hr_organization_id() OR is_super_admin()`, and `auth_hr_organization_id()` reads `user_hr_access`, which holds **exactly 1 row**. Of the 4 users carrying `hr_admin` / `hr_head` / `hr_manager` / `coo` / `ceo`, only **1** has a `user_hr_access` row and **none** are super admins; the 14 super admins pass both the guard and RLS. RLS denial returns zero rows with `error = null`, so the page would otherwise read as "nothing left to sort". It therefore says so in words instead — separate messages for "no HR organisation is visible to your account" and "no designations are visible for this organisation" — rather than rendering an empty table. No grant was widened to paper over this; all five roles already hold `hr.employees.edit` and the view key under `staff`.
### School of Influence — a real waiting list when a batch is full (2026-08-02)
- `supabase/migrations/20260808231500_soi_waiting_list.sql` — **NOT applied to any database — Director-gated apply.** Adds TWO new SECURITY DEFINER reads and rewrites one config row's human-facing strings. Creates no table, no column, no policy, no trigger, and **no new write path**. `fn_soi_waiting_list(uuid)` is the coordinator queue: every `events_registrations` row with `status='waitlisted'` and `source='soi_apply'`, grouped by the batch it names (all-NULL under the locked `staff_assign` default, so the whole programme is one queue — the truth, not a degraded case), oldest first, with position, queue size, when the person joined, and `already_placed_batch_name` as a D10 pre-warning. Guarded by `fn_soi_can_review_applications`. `fn_soi_my_waiting_list_place(uuid)` answers the SAME derivation for the caller alone — **no `p_user_id` parameter at all**, identity is `auth.uid()`, so a position can be returned without exposing another applicant's name or place; always returns exactly one row (`on_waiting_list=false` when not waiting) so no screen has to guess. Both `REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM anon, PUBLIC` + `GRANT ... TO authenticated`, both asserted in **both directions** at apply time.
- **Promotion is MANUAL, by decision, and that is the design.** Promotion IS the existing accept path (`fn_soi_prepare_acceptance` → `CohortService.createMembership` → `fn_soi_confirm_acceptance`), which already accepts a `'waitlisted'` application. Automatic promotion was rejected on three grounds: `soi.require_approval` is true (D3) and a waitlisted application has **never been read by anybody**; an auto-promotion must INSERT `cohort_memberships` from inside the database, i.e. a second enrolment path bypassing `assertMemberIdentity()` + the lifecycle map + `cohort_status_events` — the shape that let SF100 admit 23 fabricated roster rows; and it would fire as whoever removed the previous member, at a moment nobody chose.
- **Position is DERIVED at read time, never stored.** `ROW_NUMBER()` over the rows that are `'waitlisted'` right now, `ORDER BY created_at, id` (the id is the tiebreak — `created_at` ties on a bulk write and a position that reshuffles between two reads of an unchanged list is worse than none). A withdrawal (`'cancelled'`), an acceptance (`'confirmed'`) or a rejection (`'disqualified'`) drops the row out of the set and everyone behind moves up on the next read — **no backfill, no queue to repair**. Both surfaces state that the order is the order people applied in and NOT a promise about who is offered the next place.
- **Capacity accounting is unchanged by construction.** A waiting-list entry is an `events_registrations` row; a seat is a `cohort_memberships` row. A waitlisted person has **no membership**, so there is nothing to exclude and **no second definition of occupancy is introduced** — occupancy stays "every non-terminal membership" computed once in `fn_soi_review_batches`, which this file calls rather than re-implements.
- 🪤 **No signature change to any live function.** Adding waiting-list columns to `fn_soi_review_batches` would change its OUT columns, which `CREATE OR REPLACE` cannot do; the required `DROP` would break `fn_soi_prepare_acceptance` (`SELECT * INTO v_batch FROM fn_soi_review_batches(...)`) mid-flight on a live accept path.
- **`soi.batch_full_behaviour` now describes what it does.** `20260808200000_soi_review_permission_coherence.sql` had reworded it to say the waiting list was "not built yet"; that sentence is now the false one, so `ui_consequence` / `ui_options` / `ui_cascade` are rewritten at EVERY scope. Key, value, enum options and data type are untouched — no behaviour changes and no Director choice is overridden. **Apply this file AFTER 20260808200000**, or the earlier file puts the false wording back. The end-state assert checks BOTH halves (the old phrase is gone AND the new one is present), so dropping the claim without replacing it fails.
- Ships with an apply-time `DO` assert on the END STATE only, never on "did I change a row": it verifies the two dependency functions exist (`to_regprocedure`, not `::regprocedure`, which RAISEs on a missing object), that both new functions are `SECURITY DEFINER`, that `anon` **cannot** execute either and `authenticated` **can**, and that no surviving policy row still disagrees with the behaviour. No `BEGIN;`/`COMMIT;` of its own, so a Mgmt-API `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` stays a genuine dry run.
